  5. #26602 — Desktop hits 5-minute Headers Timeout with slow local providers CLOSED · 24 comments · 👍2 Requests abort at exactly 5 minutes even with "timeout": false, breaking local llama.cpp/Ollama-style setups. A key local-first usability gap.

  6. #45417 — Session cost excludes subagent cost CLOSED · 10 comments · 👍17 TUI sidebar, opencode stats, and /export under-report spend for fan-out workflows. High upvote ratio signals teams rely on these numbers for billing.

  7. #51497 — perf(v2): every LLM call re-reads and re-decodes full session history OPEN · 5 comments · 👍1 O(n) per step, O(n²) per session, with full-table SELECTs and per-row schema decoding. Accompanied by a deliberately non-mergeable demonstration PR (#51499) proposing an incremental cache + opt-in step GC.

  8. #60381 — Desktop side-panel tabs can't be closed (2.2.2 regression) OPEN · 4 comments Fresh regression, persists after window reload; launcher rows except Terminal/Open file are dead. Timely because it directly follows the v2.2.2 upgrade path.

  9. #60410 — Project experimental block hides every global experimental option OPEN · reproduced · 2 comments Config.latest returns whole blocks rather than merging fields, so any project-level experimental key silently nullifies the user's global settings. Config-semantics bugs are quietly destructive for power users.

  10. #16626 — Add session.stopping plugin hook to re-enter the agent loop CLOSED · 15 comments · 👍12 Plugins cannot prevent the loop from terminating. Closely related to the new /goal feature and a prerequisite for real stop-condition automation.

Also notable: #18654 — no way to change/remove email in OpenCode Zen (👍20), #31554 — MCP servers spawn 2–4 duplicate processes, #34877 — cost shows $0.00 for GLM/DeepSeek/Qwen via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #60414 — feat(app): voice in the composer with first-call onboarding OPEN Promotes the experimental Desktop voice call from behind a Knobs toggle to the composer, with onboarding on first use. Follow-up to #58249/#58587/#58591.

  2. #60388 — fix(desktop): keep the browser pane chunk parseable OPEN Fixes an unparseable browser-pane chunk produced by the desktop main build in 2.2.2 (closes #60369, #60386). Direct remediation for the current release.

  3. #60039 — feat(mcp): per-server TLS trust for remote MCP servers OPEN Adds an optional tls block so a self-signed or private-CA MCP server can be trusted individually instead of globally disabling verification.

  4. #60041 — feat(mcp): trust private-network server certificates on first use OPEN Stacked on #60039: a first-use trust flow, mirroring SSH-style TOFU instead of a manual fingerprint copy.

  5. #59954 — fix(core): apply webfetch permissions to Code Mode fetch OPEN Security-relevant: a URL denied for webfetch could previously still be fetched from inside a Code Mode program, and "ask" rules never prompted.

  6. #60406 — fix(client): store session forms created without a location OPEN Closes #59759, where the question tool published form.created without location, leaving a pending question on the server that the TUI never rendered.

  7. #59803 — fix(core): price Copilot long-context tiers and cache writes OPEN Corrects severe undercounting on long GitHub Copilot sessions (closes #52089, #59671) — relevant for anyone using cost data for budgeting.

  8. #58066 — fix(server): allow credential.update to rotate the stored value OPEN PATCH /api/credential/:id only accepted label, so rotating an expired API key silently kept the old secret. Important for automated key rotation.

  9. #60416 — fix(tui): keep HTML error pages out of the retry notice OPEN Truncates/summarizes provider HTML error bodies (e.g. nginx 503) instead of dumping whole documents into multi-line retry banners.

  10. #60044 — feat(ai): type OpenRouter options on the Responses route OPEN Surfaces OpenRouter's provider routing, models fallbacks, and plugins in the typed Responses options instead of letting them pass through untyped/unschematized.

Also in flight: #60109 (surface permission feedback inside Code Mode), #60407 and #60390 (unifying tool() across Promise/Effect clients and fixing typed-tool variance), #60380 (run dynamic provider npm fallback after external SDK hooks).

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Agent loop control & long-horizon autonomy. /goal shipped in v2.2.1, but requests for a session.stopping hook and stop-condition plugins (#16626) show the community wants programmatic control, not just UI verbs.
  • Observability for parallel agents. A dedicated agent activity sidebar (#27995) for monitoring explore / librarian / oracle background agents, instead of calling background_output() manually.
  • Plugin/extensibility surface area. A generic cross-client "UI intent" channel (#6330) plus richer hook coverage — plugins currently can't influence UX across TUI/Desktop consistently.
  • Configurable input & accessibility. Disabling/remapping Ctrl-C (#2999), RTL/Bidi rendering for Persian and Arabic (#16875).
  • Account & identity management. Changing or removing email in OpenCode Zen (#18654, 👍20) and cleaner handling of duplicate identities after GitHub email changes.
  • Enterprise/private-network connectivity. Per-server TLS trust for remote MCP servers (#60039, #60041, tracked under #40111), driven by self-signed certs in corporate environments.
  • Cost transparency. Subagent costs in session totals (#45417), long-context/cache pricing for Copilot (#59803), and non-zero cost reporting for OpenAI-compatible Chinese providers (#34877).

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Free-tier quota logic is the #1 source of friction. Reset timers that add 24 hours instead of firing (#60062), limits that never reset across days (#59178, #60297), and repeated "one message and blocked again" reports (#60064) have converged into a 113-comment mega-thread (#59387). The absence of a documented window/counter amplifies frustration.
  2. Scale and storage on long-lived instances. Unbounded event-table growth to 13 GB (#33356) and O(n²) history re-reads per session (#51497) suggest the persistence layer hasn't kept pace with multi-hour, subagent-heavy workflows.
  3. Release-to-release Desktop regressions. v2.2.2 broke side-panel interaction (#60381) and produced an unparseable browser-pane chunk (#60388). Users on fast upgrade cadences feel this immediately.
  4. Cost accounting is not trustworthy enough for teams. Missing subagent spend (#45417), $0.00 for openai-compatible Chinese providers (#34877), and Copilot undercounts (#59803) undermine /export and opencode stats as billing evidence.
  5. Timeouts and networking assumptions break local-first use. A hard 5-minute headers timeout that ignores "timeout": false (#26602), plus IP-sensitive ECONNRESET against the built-in Zen provider (#60422).
  6. Resource leaks in the process layer. MCP servers spawning 2–4 duplicate processes each, exhausting TasksMax and producing EAGAIN (#31554).
  7. Config semantics surprise power users. A project-level experimental block silently shadowing all global experimental options (#60410) — a class of merge bugs that is hard to diagnose from the TUI.
  8. Permission boundaries leak across execution modes. Code Mode fetch bypassing webfetch permission rules (#59954) and rejection feedback being swallowed (#60109) weaken the trust model users expect from explicit allow/ask/deny config.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-10-30

1. Today's Highlights

No new release landed in the last 24 hours, but the repository saw a heavy maintenance wave: 50 issues and 23 PRs were updated, with a large batch of fixes closed around Windows path handling, terminal input sequences, session-file privacy, and project-trust semantics. Performance and determinism were the other dominant themes — transcript virtualization for the TUI (#11598), prompt-cache stability via stable tool ordering (#11529), and per-request Bedrock client creation (#11527) all drew attention. Provider-compatibility gaps in pi-ai remain the most structurally important open problem (#9508), while the newly filed RPC shutdown bug (#11599) was triaged and closed the same day.

2. Releases

None in the last 24 hours. Omit.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #9656 — Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript in fullscreen on Windows + Zellij OPEN The most-discussed issue in the window (12 comments, 5 👍). Input routing breaks only in the Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi chain, while direct terminals and Linux+tmux work. It signals that the fullscreen input model still lacks a correct multiplexer-aware path, and it has stayed open since mid-September despite steady engagement.

  2. #9508 — pi-ai sends unsupported OpenAI-specific request fields/roles/auth to compatible providers OPEN 9 comments and still unresolved. Providers behind the "OpenAI-compatible" label reject OpenAI-only fields, roles, and auth headers with 400/422, so otherwise-valid models.json configurations fail. This is the clearest ecosystem-level blocker for third-party model support.

  3. #11157 — Extensions that sendMessage at session_start turn every session into a legacy transcript OPEN prio:p0 inprogress Because getInitialSystemMessage reads messages[0], extensions like pi-memory and pi-session-search push custom messages ahead of the system prompt, causing Anthropic requests to lose the system field. A high-severity correctness issue affecting the extension ecosystem, now marked in progress.

  4. #10982 — pi.sendMessage(triggerTurn) starts a run while manual compaction is in progress OPEN A concurrency bug: the triggered run executes against uncompacted context and interleaves with compaction output. Low comment volume but high impact for anyone relying on programmatic turns during /compact.

  5. #11529 — Tool order depends on registration order, so the same tools can bust the prompt cache OPEN getCurrentTools() returns insertion order, so a tool removed and re-added (MCP reconnect, tool_search loads, extension reload) shifts to the end of the Map. Since tools sit in the cached prefix, this silently invalidates prompt caches and inflates cost.

  6. #11527 — Bedrock: a new BedrockRuntimeClient is created for every request OPEN stream() instantiates a fresh client per call, discarding the credential provider and HTTP/2 session. With SSO profiles this forces a GetRoleCredentials round trip on every model call — a straightforward but meaningful latency and throughput regression.

  7. #10770 — Default permissions of .pi/agent/sessions should be 0700 CLOSED Session directories were created under the process umask, leaving transcripts world-readable on typical 0022 systems. 6 comments and a prompt fix — a privacy-hardening win with clear user demand.

  8. #10947 — isProjectTrusted() ignores saved Do-not-trust decisions CLOSED A saved false in trust.json was ignored for projects without trust-requiring resources, because the auto-trust check ran before the trust store was read. Security-relevant semantics bug, now resolved.

  9. #11570 — V8 OOM (SIGABRT) in long sessions with giant ConsString flattening CLOSED no-action Five production crash reports from 2+ day sessions (~8MB session files) sharing stack signatures in a flatMap string allocation. Closed without action, which leaves long-session memory behavior as an open operational risk.

  10. #10187 — Move deviceId out of the global settings CLOSED no-action 3 👍 and 5 comments from users managing agent settings as shared dotfiles. A device-specific identifier in a committed config file is a real workflow conflict and a recurring class of request.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11598 — perf(tui): virtualize the transcript and resize the fullscreen layout lazily CLOSED Directly addresses the O(transcript) per-frame cost: every message component previously stayed alive for the whole session, making scrolling, typing, and the working indicator scale with history size. The most consequential performance change in this batch.

  2. #6881 — feat(ai): use provider-reported cost when responses include it CLOSED Uses billed cost for usage.cost.total when available (including cost_details.upstream_inference_cost on BYOK), falling back to calculateCost. Improves cost accuracy for gateway and upstream-billed setups.

  3. #11594 — fix(ai): handle reasoning models on Alibaba endpoints CLOSED Avoids 400 errors caused by the developer role on Alibaba reasoning endpoints — another concrete instance of the provider-heterogeneity problem tracked in #9508.

  4. #11591 — fix(tui): drop space after styled word at wrap boundary, reset strikethrough at line end CLOSED Fixes #10925. ANSI close codes attached to the following space caused an extra leading space on wrapped lines; the tokenizer and wrapSingleLine are corrected.

  5. #11588 — fix(coding-agent): compare paths case-insensitively on Windows CLOSED Fixes #10488. realpathSync preserves input casing, so c:\Users vs C:\Users produced false skill collisions; path comparisons now normalize casing on Windows.

  6. #11587 — fix(coding-agent): create session directories as 0700 and session files as 0600 CLOSED The implementation for #10770. Closes the transcript-readability gap that existed under a standard 0022 umask.

  7. #11590 — fix(coding-agent): refresh unpinned temporary npm extensions CLOSED Fixes #11375. pi -e npm:<pkg> previously reused the first download forever; unversioned specs and dist-tags now re-resolve when a newer version exists.

  8. #11586 / #11585 — fix(tui): treat ESC+Return with native Shift held as Shift+Enter CLOSED Apple Terminal sends \x1b\r for Shift+Enter; without the kitty protocol this parsed as alt+enter and queued a follow-up instead of inserting a newline. Both the native-Shift fallback and the Apple Terminal path are covered.

  9. #11577 — fix(coding-agent): pick the smaller of PNG and JPEG when resizing images CLOSED The candidate list always tried PNG first, so photo-like JPEGs were sent as PNGs many times larger even when a smaller JPEG was available under maxBytes.

  10. #11580 — Add Arabic RTL rendering to the TUI (bidirectional text, Windows Terminal) CLOSED Implements UAX #9 bidi reordering for terminals that don't apply it (notably Windows Terminal), fixing mirrored Arabic text. Notable as an internationalization step for the TUI layer.

Also worth tracking: #11562 (OPEN) starts new sessions in the cwd's default directory instead of inheriting a foreign project's folder, and #11572 stops retrying Zhipu/Z.ai usage-limit errors (code 1308, HTTP 429).

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11503 — pi-rs: a Rust port of the headless core, behavioral parity verified atom by atom (1 comment, 1 👍) A community Rust reimplementation of pi 0.74.2's headless core — agent loop, 7 built-in tools, session JSONL, CLI surface, and system prompt — with byte-level parity checks against the original. Includes a DeepSeek API compatibility finding. Valuable both as an independent parity harness and as validation that the headless core is cleanly separable from the TUI.

Q&A

  • #11574 — How to upload an npm package to the Pi package source? (0 comments) A package author has built an extension but can't find documented guidance on publishing it. Unanswered, and it points at a gap in the extension distribution story rather than a one-off question.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Provider abstraction correctness. The largest cluster by far: OpenAI-specific fields leaking to compatible providers (#9508), Alibaba developer role handling (#11594), Google thought-signature merging/dropping (#11538), Z.ai forced-thinking behavior (#8706), Zhipu retry classification (#11572), and Bedrock client reuse (#11527). Users are running Pi against a long tail of providers and want the request layer to be conservative and provider-aware.
  • Prompt-cache and cost determinism. Stable tool ordering (#11529), provider-reported cost (#6881), and output-budget defaults that trigger 402s on OpenRouter (#11517) all point to a demand for predictable spend.
  • Security and privacy defaults. 0700/0600 session artifacts (#10770, #11587), correct trust-store semantics (#10947), and separating device-local state from shareable config (#10187).
  • Long-session performance and memory. Transcript virtualization (#11598), getSessionName() scanning every entry per render (#11567), and V8 OOM in multi-day sessions (#11570).
  • Terminal and platform compatibility. Windows drive-letter casing (#10488), Zellij mouse routing (#9656), Apple Terminal Shift+Enter (#11559/#11586), split mouse-report tails (#11172), Orca Kitty-image detection (#9329), and RTL text (#11580).
  • MCP and extension ergonomics. Namespace-scoped tool_search queries (#11558), recoverable unsupported image formats in tool results (#11552), passing model-call origin to HarnessOptions.models (#11596), and lifecycle-safe extension calls (#11157, #10982, #11599).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows remains the roughest platform. Case-sensitive path comparisons, drive-letter inconsistency between cwd and home, and terminal-specific escape sequences generate a steady stream of bugs (#10488, #9656, #11586). Several were fixed this window, but the pattern is recurring rather than one-off.
  • "OpenAI-compatible" is not a contract. Developers repeatedly hit 400/422 errors because Pi emits OpenAI-only fields, roles, or auth headers — or because model metadata (context, output capacity, thinking format) is misapplied. #9508 has been open since September with 9 comments and no resolution.
  • Sessions degrade as they grow. Typing latency at ~400k entries, O(transcript) rendering, and multi-day sessions aborting with V8 OOM are three symptoms of the same scaling problem. Two of the three were closed without action, leaving operators to work around it.
  • Silent correctness failures are the worst class of bug. Empty stdout with exit 0 in pi -p (#11568), an idle RPC process that never exits after ctx.shutdown() (#11599), and extensions silently converting every session to a legacy transcript (#11157) all fail quietly rather than loudly.
  • Configuration portability. Users who version-control their agent settings cannot safely do so while deviceId lives in global settings (#10187), and trust decisions stored on disk were previously not honored (#10947).
  • Extension lifecycle races. session_start message injection, triggerTurn during compaction, and async shutdown are all cases where extensions and core have unclear ordering guarantees — a gap that will grow as the extension ecosystem does.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-30

Source: github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code

1. Today's Highlights

Qwen Code shipped v0.26.4 across all three tracks — CLI/nightly, TypeScript SDK (v0.1.26) and Desktop (v0.26.4) — with a small, low-risk change list focused on generated-UI theming and Managed Agent SQL history bounds. The bigger story is behind the scenes: CI and release infrastructure dominate the issue tracker, with chronic main-branch failures (#14724, #12714) and a wave of runner-capacity/partitioning work landing in PRs. Meanwhile, core reliability fixes (SDK stream-json message identity, /loop cancellation, config persistence) are accumulating as the community stress-tests the daemon, SDK and Web Shell surfaces.

2. Releases

v0.26.4 — stable CLI release, with no documented breaking changes.

  • feat(generated-ui): follow the host theme in generated views — PR #15798. Generated UI now inherits the host application's theme instead of forcing its own.
  • feat(managed): add bounded SQL history queries (nightly channel, PR #15839 by @doudouOUC) — caps history query cost in the Managed Agent service.
  • feat(generated-ui): keep chatting with a ca… — incremental continuation work in the same generated-UI area.

sdk-typescript-v0.1.26 — bundles CLI 0.26.4 (built from the same source branch/ref as the SDK). Note: the generated release body still lists both 0.26.4 and 0.26.3 in duplicated "Bundled CLI Version" blocks, and the bundled-CLI section appears malformed in the published notes — worth a docs cleanup.

desktop-v0.26.4 — includes fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped (#15794 by @yiliang114) and docs for the shared-session flow.

v0.26.4-nightly.20261029.70be140e14 — nightly release cut from release/v0.26.4-nightly.20261029.70be140e14.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified (OPEN, 95 comments, updated daily since 2026-10-19) A bot-filed, per-commit CI failure tracker that has become the single noisiest thread in the repo. It signals a real structural problem: the Managed Agent gate can fail without attributing a test, so nothing gets actioned. With 95 comments and autofix/skip, it is effectively a standing alert nobody can close.

  2. #15052 — CI: preserve independent main E2E validation when pending runs are replaced (OPEN, P2, 14 comments, ready-for-human) Ref-scoped concurrency replaces older pending main E2E runs, so intermediate SHAs never get an independent validation result. Maintainer @yiliang114 argues for per-SHA validation and failure attribution — this is the root cause behind many "provisional" CI reports.

  3. #14215 — Context immutability for self-hosted models (OPEN, P2, 7 comments, 1 👍, need-discussion) The most substantive community feature thread: users running local models with slow prompt processing want memories, dreams, sessions and suggestions to stop mutating context, since each rewrite costs minutes of prefill. Tagged roadmap/context-performance and scope/caching — a genuine architectural tension between feature richness and local inference economics.

  4. #15461 — Release: reserve ECS runner slots and activate the build/publish split (OPEN, P2, 8 comments, ready-for-human) publish is the last release job still competing for GitHub-hosted capacity; the ECS release host was never provisioned. This is release-engineering debt directly affecting how fast fixes reach users.

  5. #15861 — ci(smoke): web-shell host-directory-picker smoke times out, PR-independent (OPEN, P1, 3 comments) A deterministic smoke failure on unrelated PRs, meaning every contribution pays a re-attribution round. P1 on a test-infra issue reflects how much CI trust has eroded.

  6. #15855 — contextWindowSize gets automatically removed (OPEN, P1, need-information, 3 comments) A user's explicit 128k limit in an OpenAI-compatible provider block is silently stripped. High severity because it breaks local-model workflows with no error — silent config rewriting is a recurring trust breaker (see also #15794 and #15829).

  7. #15894 — /loop stop sent as a user message doesn't cancel pending loop_wakeup (OPEN, P2, daemon, background-automation) An 80-minute autonomous /loop tick ignored an explicit stop and resumed. This is a control/safety issue for autonomous agents — users expect stop to mean stop.

  8. #15875 — SDK stream-json: text snapshot changes message.id after thinking (OPEN, P2, scope/sdk, scope/non-interactive) With --include-partial-messages, the final text snapshot's message.id differs from the originating message_start. Breaks any SDK consumer that correlates streaming fragments by ID — a core protocol-fidelity bug for integrations.

  9. #15327 — tracking(core): run every surface on one agent loop behind experimental.unifiedAgentLoop (OPEN, P1, ready-for-human) The architectural north star: one agent loop in packages/core shared by CLI, daemon, Web Shell and Desktop. Today each surface has its own loop, which explains the long tail of surface-specific bugs.

  10. #13649 — feat(a2a): contextId-less A2A messages each create an indistinguishable, unbounded chat session (OPEN, P2, need-discussion) Since #13583, the default A2A request shape (no contextId) creates one session per message, flooding the owner's Web Shell session list with no way to distinguish or bound them. A multi-agent design gap with real UX fallout.

Also notable: #12714 (13 comments, CI src/llm.test.tsx routing failures), #15739 (closed after 9 comments), #1206 (2 👍, dynamic multi-model support for OpenAI-compatible APIs — long-running and still open since 2025-12), #15877 (remote daemon listener/origin setup unclear), #15869 (PRs #14348/#15450 stalled 3 days — community escalation on review latency).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15871 — refactor(managed-agent): split server into Maven modules (@doudouOUC) Splits the Managed Agent Server into six production Maven modules plus one unpublished verification module, with framework-neutral contracts at the boundaries. The largest structural change in flight for the managed surface.

  2. #11854 — feat: add hybrid code mode (@DragonnZhang, autofix/takeover) Adds a Codex-aligned tools.mode enum (direct / code_mode / code_mode_only) exposing an isolated exec JavaScript tool while keeping ordinary tools callable. This is the most significant capability addition in the queue for tool-using agents.

  3. #15466 — feat(serve): add user-scope Skill activation routes (@callmeYe) New daemon routes PUT /skills/:name/activation and batch PUT /skills/activation (up to 100 names) for the user settings scope. Unblocks Skill management from the Web Shell without a workspace selector.

  4. #15863 — fix(cli): separate instruction files from auto memory in context usage (@callmeYe) Project/user/extension/language instructions now report under Instruction files, while auto-memory policy and catalog snapshots report under Auto memory. Directly improves context-budget transparency — relevant to the #14215 debate.

  5. #15854 — perf(release): reuse verified native audio prebuilds across releases (@yiliang114) Reuses audio prebuilds from a successful main release when build-input fingerprints match; validated cache hits skip the five-target build matrix, and any lookup/download/validation failure falls back to a full rebuild. Clear release-latency win with a safe fallback path.

  6. #15888 — fix(ci): partition the complete macOS test suite into bounded jobs (@yiliang114) Splits macOS CI into seven jobs (three CLI shards, two core shards, remaining workspace suites, standalone/runtime scripts) with the original check retained as an aggregate. Follow-up findings tracked in #15895.

  7. #15885 — fix(ci): route the E2E build job through the pool-first runner expression (@yiliang114) Moves the E2E shared build job onto the same self-hosted ecs-qwen pool-first routing every other job uses. Together with #15854 and #15461, this is the runner-capacity story of the week.

  8. #12799 — fix(edit): keep the line endings an edit did not touch (@feiiiiii5) Preserves original bytes outside local edit spans and selects inserted line endings per span, while whole-file replacements keep prior CRLF behavior. A long-running correctness fix with outsized impact on Windows/dirty-diff complaints.

  9. #15829 — fix(vscode): keep sibling model settings when writing provider config (@2SinceJuly) Configuring a provider from the VS Code companion previously rewrote the entire settings.model object with only name, deleting sibling keys. Now writes name/baseUrl key-by-key — same class of silent-config-loss bug as #15855 and #15794.

  10. #15851 — fix(cli): report pre-send refusals instead of replaying answers (@2SinceJuly) When a turn is refused before sending (session token limit or a UserPromptSubmit hook block), the shared result builder fell back to the previous turn's assistant message. Fixes a serious correctness bug for persistent stream-json sessions.

Also worth tracking: #15883 and #15882 (recovery-fixture transcript coverage; Managed JDBC selection in Hosted fault fixtures), #15803-series Java cache hygiene fixes (#15286, #15274), #15060 (shared session view reset state), #13026 (report speculation copy failures), #13035 (tolerant managed-session metadata parsing), #13067 (Ctrl+named-key bug), #13080 (/stats scrolling on short terminals), #14653 (/mcp selection by identity).

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided in this dataset — section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Context & memory economics for self-hosted models (roadmap/context-performance, scope/memory, scope/caching) — the strongest single direction. #14215 argues that memories/dreams/suggestions/sessions should become opt-in or immutable when prompt processing is slow, and #15863's instruction-vs-auto-memory split shows the team moving toward better context transparency.
  • One agent loop / unified session management (roadmap/session-management) — #15327 proposes a single packages/core agent loop behind experimental.unifiedAgentLoop, explicitly to eliminate surface-specific divergence across CLI, daemon, Web Shell and Desktop.
  • Multi-agent and A2A hardening (roadmap/multi-agent) — #13649 (unbounded session creation), #13645 (shared mention grammar, typed executing-status set) and #13583 follow-ups show demand for predictable multi-agent semantics rather than more features.
  • Dynamic multi-model support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints — #1206 (open since 2025-12, 2 👍) still asks for fetching and switching models dynamically instead of hardcoding one.
  • Web Shell / Desktop UX parity — keyboard shortcuts for Session Overview and Split View (#13175, closed), Russian/arbitrary-locale i18n (#13391, closed), no-workspace session visibility (#11878, closed), sidebar category consistency (#15867), macOS daemon PATH extension (#12690). The closure rate suggests active triage here.
  • CI/release infrastructure as a product surface — ECS runner reservation (#15461), overnight macOS validation policy (#15783), pool-first runner routing. These are now first-class feature requests, not chores.
  • Remote/daemon access ergonomics — #15877 (listener + origin setup for remote qwen serve) and #12059 (remote-webview failure modes: forwarded-port Host gate, IPv6 CSP, Remote-SSH/WSL) point at growing remote-development usage.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Chronic, unattributable CI failures. #14724 (95 comments), #12714 (13), #14796, #15712, #15281 and #15739 all trace back to the same pattern: a run fails before any test result is reported, so the tracker can only file per-commit. #15052 diagnoses the concurrency root cause. Contributors are losing time to re-attribution on unrelated PRs (#15861 is explicitly "PR-independent").
  • macOS CI cost and duration. #15783 requests moving routine macOS/Darwin validation to overnight Asia/Shanghai runs; #15888 partitions the suite into seven bounded jobs. Both exist because macOS lanes are the slowest, flakiest gate.
  • Silent configuration loss. Three independent reports in one window: contextWindowSize stripped (#15855), VS Code provider writes clobbering sibling settings.model keys (#15829), and Desktop dropping controls without notice (#15794, now fixed). The pattern — mutate a shared config object instead of patching keys — is a systemic hazard for user trust.
  • Streaming/SDK protocol fidelity. #15875 (message ID changes mid-stream) and #15851 (replaying a previous turn's answer after a pre-send refusal) both break consumers that treat the stream as authoritative. Machine-readable output is now a contract, and it's leaking.
  • Autonomy controls that don't take effect. #15894: an explicit stop does not cancel a pending loop_wakeup, so a self-paced /loop re-arms itself. For users running autonomous managers, this is the difference between a tool and an unbounded process.
  • Edit correctness on real filesystems. Long-lived PRs #12799 (line endings), #13026 (speculation copy failures), #13035 (torn transcript lines) and #13067 (Ctrl+named-key input) show a steady undercurrent of byte-level and input-level correctness bugs that take weeks to land because they sit behind a noisy CI gate.
  • Local/self-hosted model ergonomics. #14215 (slow prompt processing), #15855 (context window ignored), #15877 (remote daemon setup) — the self-hosted segment consistently hits friction where cloud users don't, and the issues carry the highest per-user impact.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-30

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-30 02:07 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-30

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 仍是一个高速推进的项目：过去 24 小时内有 500 个 issue 和 500 个 PR 被更新，其中 174 个 issue 已关闭、192 个 PR 已合并或关闭，显示出较强的问题分诊和合并吞吐能力。共发布两个版本：以安全为重点的稳定补丁 v2026.10.9，以及仅面向 Gateway 的 v2026.9.36 扩展稳定/LTS 版本。活跃积压仍然很大——更新项中有 326 个未关闭 issue 和 308 个未关闭 PR——并且主要集中在围绕 Gateway 状态数据库、会话生命周期完整性、MCP 运行时管理以及更新/恢复路径的 P0/P1 可靠性工作。总体而言，项目在响应速度和发布节奏方面健康状况良好，但风险集中在状态/会话持久性以及若干长期存在的 P0/P1 issue 上。注意：数据集展示的是按评论数排序的前 50 个 issue 和前 30 个 PR；PR 评论数不可用。

2. 版本发布

v2026.10.9 — 稳定版安全补丁

发布 v2026.10.9

发行说明中列出的关键变更：

  • fast-uri 4.2.3：在 MCP schema 校验期间拒绝格式错误的 URI scheme 和 host。
  • Zod 集合限制：在 A2UI 和 Discord 嵌入式应用 SDK 中会提前拒绝过大的集合。
  • IMAP 发件人解析：现在使用 nodemailer 10.1.4，因此能够正确处理伪造的发件人。

破坏性变更 / 迁移说明： 提供的发行摘录中未说明任何此类内容。这是一个依赖加固补丁；执行标准升级并重启 Gateway 即可。使用 MCP schema 校验、A2UI、Discord 嵌入式应用 SDK 或 IMAP 接入的团队应优先采用此版本。

发布验证注意事项： 2026.10.9 验证期间观察到的偶发测试失败记录在 #187490。发布方将其归类为偶发失败（flakes）；按照政策，需要在 main 上并行修复。

v2026.9.36 — 仅 Gateway 的扩展稳定版（等同于 LTS）

发布 v2026.9.36

  • 仅面向 Gateway 的 extended-stable 版本，被描述为项目当前的 LTS 等效版本。
  • 基于 2026 年 9 月底的 OpenClaw，并包含关键安全更新、可靠性/性能修复以及新的模型支持。
  • 最适合需要受支持且持续维护安全的基线、而非最新稳定特性的保守部署。

3. 项目进展

192 个已合并/关闭的 PR 和 174 个已关闭 issue 表明清理工作有实际成效，不过数据集未区分已合并与仅关闭的 PR。

活跃前 50 个 issue 中值得注意的已关闭项：

  • #178000 — 会话状态竞态被误分类为 reason=unknown，触发跨提供商的模型回退。被评为 diamond lobster / P1 后关闭。
  • #186813 — 聊天内托管更新（gateway.update.run）因 SQLite 锁竞争而无限期卡在 epoll_wait。P0，已关闭。
  • #156635 — 账户发现后，Copilot 上下文预算仍停留在合成的 128k 回退值。已关闭。
  • #187468 — 2026.9.8 的更新失败报告。已关闭。

推进关键领域的 PR：

  • 更新/恢复加固： #188034 在回退发布过程中保留权限；#188021 从恢复歧义中排除已解决的捕获；#188024 报告失败的定时注册表观测；#188027 通过主键读取命名恢复；#188010 在返回失败后重试安装发现（已关闭）。
  • Gateway 响应性/性能： #188033 在插件工具发现期间保持 Gateway 响应；#188030 阻止 doctor 重复读取 SQLite 检查副本；#188025 阻止 GitHub 就绪检查复制整个 agent 数据库（P1，安全敏感）。
  • Web/UI 正确性： #188013 在相对 HTML 预览中保留作者编写的 CSP（已标记安全边界风险）；#188017 修复会话高级菜单中的重复分隔线（已关闭）；#188039 为工作区栏文件搜索增加规范 Unicode 匹配。
  • 渠道/集成： #188003 在 Teams 实时目录搜索中匹配规范等价的名称；#188018 修复进度模式下 Matrix 图片回复。
  • 记忆： #186649 通过标记让主题文件启用按条目分块。
  • 开发者体验： #187962 增加 OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS，用于开发期间重新加载捆绑插件代码。

4. 社区热点

评论最多的 issue 显示，用户持续关注状态持久性、记忆提升和 MCP 工具可靠性。

  1. #164294 — Gateway 状态数据库 WAL 自动检查点永不完成（38 条评论，P2）。
    Gateway 自身对 state/openclaw.sqlite 的 WAL 检查点被一个进程内读取器永久阻塞；consecutiveBlocked 持续增长，检查点始终无法完成。底层需求：在真实 Gateway 负载下实现可预测的 SQLite 维护和有界的 WAL 增长。

  2. #150635 — 短期回忆保留策略每晚驱逐已回忆条目，导致 dreaming 深度阶段永不提升（23 条评论，P2）。
    在 512 条目上限下，夜间摄入阶段会暂存零回忆条目，深度阶段永不提升。底层需求：在短期回忆容量、dreaming 和提升之间建立一致的记忆生命周期语义。

  3. #120385 — Code Mode 工具目录在定时/cron 和 memory-flush 轮次中不完整；MCP 工具缺失（22 条评论，P2）。
    定时任务以“Unknown tool id”失败，仅表现为通用 exec 失败。底层需求：在交互式、cron 和 memory-flush 执行路径之间实现工具目录一致性。

  4. #164923 — 一个工作区提升 0/512，而同级工作区提升 50–90%（19 条评论，P2）。
    openclaw memory promote 即使将阈值覆盖为零也返回无候选。底层需求：多工作区记忆提升中可确定、可检查的过滤机制。

  5. #172837 — Codex nativeSubagentAssignments 在完成交付放弃后从未移除（18 条评论，P1）。
    每个新的父线程都会重新固定并重新发送陈旧分配。底层需求：原生子代理的生命周期清理和重试耗尽语义。

PR 侧活动： 数据集中 PR 评论数不可用，但若干 PR 标记为“ready for maintainer look”，包括 #188003、#188021、#187986 和 #184511。长期运行的 XL PR #181813（Gateway 原生状态所有者身份）自 2026-10-23 起保持打开，正在等待维护者审查。

5. Bug 与稳定性

过去 24 小时更新的活跃 issue，按严重程度排序。在可识别处注明修复 PR。

P0 — 发布阻断 / 严重可用性

  • #166634 — 迟到的回收提交检查点失败导致 agent 在崩溃恢复后永久不可用；agent 拒绝 chat.history、chat.metadata、models.list 和进度卡请求。18 条评论。未显示关联修复 PR。
  • #162211 — Gateway 启动阻塞事件循环 40–200 秒；健康监控将此停顿误判为断开连接，并升级为重启循环。14 条评论。未显示关联修复 PR。
  • #158592 — macOS 睡眠/唤醒后，某个 agent 的已准备模型运行时发布超时且永不恢复；在 Gateway 重启之前，所有入站消息都以“runtime owner was not published”失败。11 条评论。未显示关联修复 PR。
  • #141413 — macOS 应用在使用受保护的 SecretRef 为本地 Gateway 时省略 token；嵌入式仪表板可以认证，但外部连接不能。P0，需要安全审查，7 条评论，2 个 👍。
  • #186813 — 托管更新因 SQLite 事务锁竞争卡在 epoll_wait。已关闭；可能已处理，但提供的数据中未列出具体合并 PR。

P1 — 严重功能/崩溃循环回归

  • #172837 — Codex 原生子代理分配在交付放弃后泄漏；在每个新的父线程上重新固定。18 条评论。未显示修复 PR。
  • #177656 — 原生 host exec 返回“Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission”且没有子结果；在稳定版 2026.10.5 上至少 28 次失败。17 条评论。未显示修复 PR。
  • #166017 — 未设置时 mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs 默认值（10 分钟）未生效；MCP 运行时永不驱逐，spawn broker 达到 256 个子进程硬上限，所有 exec/read/MCP 启动均失败。13 条评论。关联修复 PR 已打开。
  • #159094 — Gateway 持有状态生命周期租约，但内部 worker 报告另一个进程持有该租约，从而关闭 agent DB 执行准入。14 条评论。
  • #126950 — 非插件调用方发送的 Telegram 不透明回调 payload（tgcb1:）被静默丢弃。11 条评论，1 个 👍。关联修复 PR 已打开。
  • #163566 — 更新修复后，持久化上下文引擎轮次卡在 session-rebound；session-resource-loader 每轮消耗约 100 秒 CPU。10 条评论。
  • #167876 — 会话设置完成后，Talk 咨询丢失调用方权限；需要安全审查。9 条评论，1 个 👍。
  • #158070 — 当运行在 lane 队列中等待时，预检压缩失败并提示“agent tool caller authority is no longer active”，使进行中的交付失效。9 条评论。
  • #148789 — 模型回退链在 harness 级会话失败时耗尽所有候选，并将其错误归因于最后一个回退模型。9 条评论。
  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive 在插件捕获阶段空闲 15+ 分钟，从未进入 agent DB 修复。8 条评论。相关性能 PR #188030。
  • #155396 — 普通 Codex 工具轮次在最终答案恢复期间因 provenance_rejected 而失败关闭（fail closed）。8 条评论。
  • #160762 — claude-cli + Telegram：轮次中途发送的消息被丢弃；排空后的 prompt 携带上一条消息的正文。7 条评论。

P2 — 值得注意的摩擦/正确性

  • #164394 — 当滚动到历史记录时，Control UI WebChat 转录内容持续抖动。13 条评论。
  • #177094 — 重启/重新加载后，系统通知交付镜像会将轮次的最后答案挤到折叠的工具步骤中。9 条评论。
  • #172969 — 不带 modelProvider 的 registerCliBackend 被静默丢弃；表现为“Invalid URL: must be http or https.” 8 条评论。
  • #176342 — 非正常关闭后，陈旧租约完整性门禁将 agent 启动串行化，导致数分钟不可用。7 条评论。
  • #186973 — /clear 状态检查在运行数周后仍渲染过时的更新历史横幅，且跨 Gateway 重启和系统重启仍然存在。7 条评论。
  • #165433 — 当客户端不是 Operator UI 客户端时，chat.send 拒绝带有 __controlUiReconnectResume 的重连 envelope。7 条评论。
  • #164690 — claude-cli 运行会为每个 stdio MCP server 启动两次；每个 Gateway stdio 子进程都带有约 144 MB 的 supervisor wrapper 开销，且不可配置。7 条评论。
  • #167667 — ChatGPT Responses 工具续接失败并提示“Rustponses cannot replay”，表现为通用 agent 运行错误。P1，6 条评论，1 个 👍。

稳定性评估： 最高风险集群是 Gateway/会话状态完整性和崩溃恢复。若干 P0/P1 issue 已开放数周且没有关联修复 PR，而更新路径和 doctor 性能修复正在积极审查中。2026.10.9 安全补丁值得欢迎，但并未解决核心的状态生命周期故障。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

活跃的用户请求功能，按可能的相关性排序：

  • #6757 — Agent 触发的上下文压缩（self-compact 工具）。 P2，9 条评论，2 个 👍，自 2026 年 2 月起开放。与项目记忆/上下文工作高度契合；是路线图关注的有力候选。
  • #172547 — 从记忆搜索索引和回忆信号中排除围栏式 dreaming 范围。 7 条评论。与热门记忆提升 issue 直接相关；可能会并入 memory-core 修复。
  • #112638 — session.maintenance enforce 模式没有限制存储；线程/渠道条目被豁免回收。 8 条评论，自 7 月起开放。强烈的可靠性/可运维性信号。
  • #163739 — 使 Control UI 的 Ctrl+Shift+A（归档）可配置；它与浏览器快捷键冲突。 7 条评论，1 个 👍。小型、面向用户的 UX 修复。
  • #140244 — 在 openclaw infer model run 中支持 --prompt-file。 7 条评论，1 个 👍。面向自动化的 CLI 改进。
  • #154524 — 将聊天消息暴露为标题以供屏幕阅读器导航。 6 条评论。无障碍缺口。
  • #147732 — 为波斯语/阿拉伯语/希伯来语与英语混合消息提供段落级 RTL 方向。 6 条评论。国际化/UI 正确性。
  • #150743 — QQ 渠道可持续性：腾讯交接停滞；明确长期支持。 7 条评论。生态系统/支持模式问题，不是代码功能。

对下一版本的预测： 最强的近期信号是记忆/回忆正确性（多个高评论 issue 加上 PR #186649）、更新/恢复加固（已经是 PR 集群）、MCP 运行时生命周期默认值，以及 Control UI 无障碍/本地化修复。Agent 触发的上下文压缩是价值最高的较大功能，但自 2 月以来一直待定，可能需要产品决策。

7. 用户反馈总结

反复出现的痛点：

  • 状态与会话持久性： 用户报告 agent 在崩溃恢复后永久不可用、WAL 检查点永不完成、陈旧租约使启动串行化，以及会话状态竞态触发跨提供商回退。这些是最具破坏性的反馈体验，因为它们需要重启 Gateway 或导致 agent 无法使用。
  • 记忆/dreaming 不一致： 多份报告描述提升流水线静默产生零候选、每晚驱逐已回忆条目，或索引永远无法提升的 dreaming 输出。用户显然将记忆作为核心工作流，而非外围功能。
  • 更新与恢复可靠性： 聊天内更新因 SQLite 锁挂起、doctor --fix 空闲、失败的注册表查找被记录为成功，以及包替换失败。这侵蚀了对升级路径的信任，尤其是稳定版/LTS 用户。
  • MCP/资源管理： MCP 运行时未在默认 TTL 下驱逐、spawn broker 达到 256 个子进程、claude-cli 下重复的 stdio server，以及每个子进程约 144 MB 的 wrapper 开销。多 agent 或 Docker 沙箱部署的运维人员对此感受尤为强烈。
  • UI/UX 摩擦： WebChat 转录抖动、过时横幅、系统通知挤占最终答案、快捷键冲突、RTL 渲染，以及屏幕阅读器导航缺口。
  • 平台特定问题： macOS Homebrew Node 升级破坏裸 openclaw 命令；Android 反复查询未知 agent openclaw；QQ 渠道支持不确定性。

满意度信号： 问题分诊量大、若干 P0/P1 issue 快速关闭、清晰的 LTS 等效版本以及安全补丁节奏，均表明维护响应积极。“ready for maintainer look”标签和结构化评级系统表明审查流程健康。

不满意度信号： 若干 P0/P1 issue 已开放数周且没有关联修复 PR，许多高评论 issue 带有 needs-product-decision、needs-maintainer-review 或 stale 标签。用户在详细复现上投入了大量精力；对这些报告的决策延迟可能导致倦怠和变通方案。

8. 积压关注

重要 issue/PR，它们陈旧、高影响，或等待维护者/产品行动：

  • #6757 — Agent 触发的上下文压缩。自 2026-02-02 起开放，9 条评论，2 个 👍，需要产品决策。可见集合中运行时间最长的高价值功能请求。
  • #112638 — session.maintenance enforce 没有限制存储。自 2026-07-22 起开放，8 条评论。对长期运行部署具有重要运维意义。
  • #120385 — Code Mode 工具目录在 cron/memory-flush 轮次中不完整。自 2026-08-08 起开放，22 条评论。社区参与度高；影响定时自动化可靠性。
  • #126950 — Telegram 不透明回调 payload 被丢弃。自 2026-08-21 起开放，11 条评论，1 个 👍，关联修复 PR 已打开。渠道集成阻塞项。
  • #141413 — macOS 应用在使用 SecretRef 为本地 Gateway 时省略 token。自 2026-09-07 起开放，P0，7 条评论，2 个 👍，需要安全审查。严重性高但评论量相对较低——可能分诊不足。
  • #150635 — Dreaming 深度阶段因回忆驱逐而永不提升。自 2026-09-17 起开放，23 条评论，diamond-lobster 评级，需要产品决策。用户影响大且参与度高。
  • #158592 — 睡眠/唤醒运行时发布超时。自 2026-09-26 起开放，P0，11 条评论，需要现场复现。严重但依赖复现。
  • #162211 — 启动事件循环阻塞 → 重启循环。自 2026-09-30 起开放，P0，14 条评论，需要维护者审查。发布阻断级严重性。
  • #166634 — 迟到回收检查点失败导致 agent 不可用。自 2026-10-07 起开放，P0，18 条评论。最高严重性的开放 issue 之一。
  • PR #154033 — 来自原始响应项的 Codex 原生工具输出图像。自 2026-09-20 起开放，需要证明，存在安全边界和消息交付风险。长期存活的 PR，具有协议级影响。
  • PR #181813 — 暴露持有的原生状态所有者身份。自 2026-10-23 起开放，XL，P2，已准备好供维护者查看。与状态所有者/租约混乱集群相关。
  • PR #184511 — 提交带有参与关系的邀请成员资格。自 2026-10-26 起开放，P2，已准备好供维护者查看，证明充分。授权/会话正确性。
  • #150743 — QQ 渠道可持续性与腾讯交接。7 条评论，自 2026-09-17 起开放。需要生态系统/支持决策，而非代码修复。

底线： OpenClaw 发布迅速，并维持了可信的 LTS/安全节奏，但其最有价值的用户正遭遇状态/会话持久性和记忆提升故障，而这些故障已数周未解决。下一发布周期应以其是否能对 P0 状态生命周期集群（#166634、#162211、#158592）和记忆提升集群（#150635、#164923、#172547）给出具体修复，而非进一步分诊，来评判。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告——个人 AI 助理 / Agent 开源生态

快照日期：2026-10-30 | 项目：OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw

1. 生态概览

个人 AI 助理 / agent 开源格局正围绕一套共同架构栈收敛——由网关进程持有会话/状态、MCP 工具层、记忆子系统，以及多渠道路由面——厂商则在部署模型（单用户 vs 多租户）、语言/运行时和渠道覆盖上形成差异。活跃度极不均衡：OpenClaw 的活跃度比同侪高一个数量级（每天触及 500 个 issue + 500 个 PR），Hermes/ZeroClaw/QwenPaw 集中在每天 40–55 个条目的聚焦区间，IronClaw 在本窗口实际上处于休眠。在所有活跃项目中，主导工程主题已从 能力 转向 持久性与信任：崩溃安全状态、诚实故障报告、记忆来源和身份作用域，在社区参与度上现已超过功能发布。发布节奏正在分化——OpenClaw 是唯一同时维护快速稳定通道和等效 LTS 通道的项目，这对保守型采用者而言正成为有意义的竞争护城河。

2. 活跃度对比（过去 24 小时）

项目 更新的 Issue（开放/关闭） 更新的 PR（开放/已合并-关闭） 发布状态 健康度评分*
OpenClaw 约 500（174 关闭） 约 500（192 合并/关闭） 2 个发布：v2026.10.9 稳定安全补丁；v2026.9.36 仅网关 LTS 8.5 / 10
Hermes Agent 50（48 开放 / 2 关闭） 50（10 合并/关闭，40 开放） 无 7.5 / 10
IronClaw 0 0（2 个开放的 Dependabot） 无 4.5 / 10
QwenPaw 15（10 关闭 / 5 开放） 40（13 合并/关闭，27 开放） 无（2.3.0 beta 发布前稳定化） 7.5 / 10
ZeroClaw 50（17 关闭 / 33 开放） 50（6 合并/关闭，44 开放） 无（介于 v0.8.7 与 v0.9.0 之间） 7.0 / 10

*健康度评分是由分流/合并吞吐量、发布节奏、未关闭积压严重度和未解决 P0/P1 风险合成的派生综合指标。它是方向性的，不是维护者指标。OpenClaw 在吞吐量和发布纪律上得分最高，但集中承载 P0 状态持久性风险；QwenPaw/Hermes 从相反方向得到相似评分（速度 vs. 积压清理）。IronClaw 的评分反映低活跃度，而非不稳定。

解读表格： OpenClaw 的原始吞吐量约为第二大项目的 10 倍。QwenPaw 相对 issue 最偏 PR 密集（40:15），表明实现速度超过需求接收速度——这是评审带宽受限的典型特征。ZeroClaw 显示出最大的 录入到合并缺口（44 个开放 PR vs. 6 个已关闭 PR），这是其主要结构性风险。Hermes 是唯一表现出 积压清理行为 的项目（本窗口合并了数月前的 PR）。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相对同行的优势

  • 社区规模： 每天约 500 个 issue + 500 个 PR，对比 50/50（Hermes、ZeroClaw）和 15/40（QwenPaw）。贡献者和分流基础大一个数量级，因此它能在一天内维持 174 个 issue 关闭和 192 个 PR 处置。
  • 双发布通道： 唯一同时发布稳定安全补丁（v2026.10.9）和仅网关等效 LTS（v2026.9.36，包含回移的安全 + 可靠性修复）的项目。对保守型/企业采用者而言，这是具体的差异化优势。
  • 流程成熟度： 结构化严重度评级（P0–P2、“diamond lobster”）、明确的“ready for maintainer look”状态，以及发布验证注意事项策略（flaky 测试被跟踪到并行 main 修复）表明其具备同行缺乏的治理层。
  • 集成面广度： 渠道（Telegram、Matrix、Teams、Discord、QQ、IMAP）、Web/UI、Code Mode、A2UI 和 MCP 运行时——在本组中最广。

技术路线差异

  • 以网关为中心、SQLite 支撑的状态： 会话生命周期、状态生命周期租约、WAL 检查点和崩溃恢复都是网关的一等关注点。这既是其最强保证雄心的来源，也是其最高严重度未关闭 bug（#166634、#162211、#158592）的来源。
  • 记忆/dreaming 作为子系统： 短期召回上限、夜间“深度阶段”晋升和 dreaming 范围索引在本组中为 OpenClaw 独有，并推动其评论最多的问题（#150635、#164923）。
  • 将 MCP 视为带生命周期管理的运行时： 会话空闲 TTL、spawn-broker 子进程上限和运行时驱逐被视为运维关注点（#166017），而不仅仅是协议管道。

社区规模对比： OpenClaw 是参考实现和生态的引力井；QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 的每日条目量各约为其 10%，IronClaw 当前不活跃。Hermes 在范围上最接近，但吞吐量约为 OpenClaw 的 10%，且没有发布通道。

4. 共同技术重点领域

相同的需求族在独立代码库中反复出现——这是一个强信号，表明它们是生态级而非项目局部问题。

需求 提出该需求的项目 具体需求
会话/状态持久性与崩溃恢复 OpenClaw (#166634, #162211, #158592), Hermes (#146643, #139210), ZeroClaw (#10526 RFC, #11432) 崩溃安全状态机、有界 WAL 增长、重启安全会话接管、仅追加可回放历史。ZeroClaw 是唯一一个已 接受 RFC 来实现仅追加事件历史的项目（#10526 → 实现 #11921）。
记忆/上下文正确性与来源 OpenClaw (#150635, #164923, #172547), Hermes (#143379 doc-chain RFC), QwenPaw (#8500, #8457, #7835), ZeroClaw (#9647 knowledge-graph attribution) 一致的召回→晋升生命周期、保留来源的压缩、不向渠道静默泄漏 payload、按 agent 隔离知识。
静默失败 / 诚实状态报告 QwenPaw (#8500 "success=True on dropped data", #8150, #8488), ZeroClaw (#11332, #11336 false-positive plugin validation), OpenClaw (registry lookups recorded as successes), Hermes (#124874 mislabeled provider failure) 区分“什么都没做”与“没有数据”；大声失败；绝不将有损操作检查点为成功。QwenPaw 的三份独立报告使这成为最清晰的跨项目主题。
多租户身份、RBAC 与归属 ZeroClaw (#5982 per-sender RBAC, #9647 S0 cross-agent knowledge), Hermes (#35147 stable user_id, profile-scope mismatches), OpenClaw (operator authority, Talk authority loss), QwenPaw (Hub admin password reset #7740) 按主体授权、稳定身份映射、作用域隔离、管理操作对等。
MCP / 插件生命周期完整性 OpenClaw (#166017 idle-TTL eviction, spawn-broker cap), QwenPaw (#8473 plugin loader regression, #8499 provider decomposition), ZeroClaw (#11562 manifest/component generation mismatch, #11336), Hermes (#142235 read-only MCP tool call) 确定性插件注册、代际一致性、运行时驱逐默认值、仪表盘的只读/受限访问。
Cron/定时任务持久性 Hermes (#135487 SQLite lock, #146428 silent wedge, #145596 paused-job reactivation), OpenClaw (#120385 tool catalog missing for cron/memory-flush), ZeroClaw 重启安全的触发处理、重试语义、跨执行路径的工具目录对等、可见的运行历史。
上下文压缩正确性 OpenClaw (#6757 self-compact, #8464-adjacent), QwenPaw (#8464 /compact ignores session model, #6189 save_decision()), Hermes (#139210 compaction duplicates messages) 会话范围的模型路由、压缩期间决策持久化、无重复行副作用。
配置 schema 信任（“接受但未读取”） ZeroClaw (#9394 pairing dashboard never read, #11589 cost override no-op), OpenClaw (#172969 silent CLI-backend drop), Hermes (#90040 Managed Scope ignored) 配置键必须接通或被拒绝；静默无操作会侵蚀 schema 信任。
Agent 循环 / 成本控制 Hermes (#137170 no circuit breaker, 430 duplicate calls), QwenPaw (#6116 doom loop, closed wontfix), ZeroClaw (#11484 repetitive-tool safeguards disabled) 重复成功检测（不只是重复失败）、token 预算、调用指纹去重。QwenPaw 的 wontfix 是一处显著差异。
安装/更新占用 Hermes (#139500 ~22,600 .pyc / >303 MiB, #143577 1 GB uv cache), QwenPaw (#8488 desktop packaging regression), OpenClaw (update/recovery hardening cluster) 可修剪缓存、带 TTL 自愈的崩溃安全更新尾部、打包资产完整性。

5. 差异化分析

功能重点与目标用户

  • OpenClaw——最广泛的个人助理平台：记忆/dreaming、多渠道、Web/UI、Code Mode、A2UI。面向希望获得全栈助理并愿意运维网关的高级用户和自托管者。唯一具有明确保守部署（LTS）层级的项目。
  • Hermes Agent——工作流自动化：看板驱动执行、cron 投递保证、多 profile/团队配置，以及针对分机使用的 强烈需求的桌面纯前端安装（#38519，31👍）。面向消费者/生产力和小团队自动化。
  • IronClaw——基础设施/延迟测试装置（基于 wasmtime，/harness/latency/runner）。当前仅维护；本窗口无面向用户的信号。
  • QwenPaw——派生自 AgentScope，面向中国市场优先，渠道密集（飞书、QQ、微信、企业微信、钉钉、OneBot、元宝）。桌面端（Windows、zh-CN）和 Hub 多租户模式是一等公民。正处于 2.3.0-beta 稳定化，插件/provider 拆分正在进行中。
  • ZeroClaw——基于 Rust，明确朝 多租户、可审计 agent 基础设施 推进：按发送者 RBAC、按 agent 知识作用域、仅追加可回放会话、ZeroCode TUI。本组中最偏安全/治理的前瞻路线图。

技术架构差异

  • 语言/运行时： ZeroClaw（Rust、wasmtime）、IronClaw（wasmtime harness）、QwenPaw（AgentScope/Python、PyInstaller 桌面端）、Hermes（Python 网关）、OpenClaw（网关 + SQLite 状态 DB + MCP 运行时）。
  • 状态模型： OpenClaw 和 Hermes 是可变的、带租约的 SQLite 模型（其锁竞争和过期租约 bug 的来源）。ZeroClaw 是唯一一个 用仅追加事件日志替换 可变持久化的项目（#11921），这在结构上消除了 OpenClaw 仍在修补的若干故障类别。
  • 租户模型： OpenClaw/Hermes/QwenPaw 从单用户起步，正在改造以支持多 profile/多租户；ZeroClaw 从一开始就面向多租户设计（RBAC、知识作用域、principal withholding）。
  • 分发： OpenClaw 提供双通道；QwenPaw 提供 PyInstaller 桌面 beta；Hermes 没有发布，且存在强烈的安装卫生抱怨；IronClaw 本窗口未发布任何内容。

6. 社区动能与成熟度

活跃度层级

  • 第 1 层——超高频： OpenClaw（每天触达约 1,000 个条目、2 个发布、持续分流）。这是一个在运行发布列车的项目，而不是短跑。
  • 第 2 层——高活跃、聚焦： Hermes、ZeroClaw（各 50/50）、QwenPaw（55 个条目，偏 PR）。三者都在围绕明确主题（可靠性 / 安全基础设施 / beta 稳定化）高强度迭代，但本窗口无发布。
  • 第 3 层——休眠： IronClaw（0 个 issue，2 个 Dependabot PR）。数据不足以区分稳定与脱离。

谁在快速迭代 vs. 稳定化

  • 快速迭代： QwenPaw（2.3.0-beta 回归正在积极修补：#8473 通过 #8497 当日关闭）、OpenClaw（周节奏修复 + 安全补丁）、ZeroClaw（v0.9.0 里程碑持续累积；今日关闭 17 个 issue）。
  • 稳定化 / 清理积压： Hermes 本窗口合并了 数月前的 PR（#73923、#63812、#5490 一类清理），表明这是一次维护性清理，而非新功能工作。IronClaw 持平。
  • 评审带宽受限： QwenPaw 最老的 PR 已 40–53 天，且为 XL/XXL/XXXL（#7613 已 53 天，#7874 已 41 天）；ZeroClaw 有 44 个开放 PR vs. 6 个已关闭 PR，存在堆叠依赖链（#11320→#11322→…）和一个自 2026-08-04 起等待评审的 P1 安全 PR（#9745）；OpenClaw 有长期存活的 XL PR（#181813 自 10-23 起开放）等待维护者查看。常见故障模式是 大型、堆叠、高风险 PR 挤占评审队列，而非贡献者不足。

成熟度信号排序： OpenClaw（最高：双通道、严重度分类法、验证策略）> ZeroClaw（已接受架构 RFC、发布里程碑标记、安全评审标签）> Hermes/QwenPaw（贡献量强，决策吞吐较弱——needs-decision/awaiting-reporter/wontfix 集群）> IronClaw（未知）。

7. 趋势信号（面向 AI agent 开发者）

  1. 持久、可回放状态正成为基本门槛。 每个活跃项目都在与会话/租约/崩溃恢复 bug 斗争；ZeroClaw 的仅追加 RFC 是最清晰的前瞻答案。启示： 从第一天起就按事件溯源或可回放持久化来设计——在可变 SQLite 上补持久性，是整个组中最大的单项重复成本。

  2. 静默失败是新的信任杀手。 最具破坏性的报告不是崩溃，而是 报告成功但实际无操作：QwenPaw 的 Auto-Dream 检查点将丢弃记忆记录为 success=True（#8500）、飞书媒体被静默丢弃（#8150）、Visual Compact 静默无操作（#8488），以及 ZeroClaw 的插件“加载”但从未注册（#11336）。启示： 将“什么都没做 vs. 没有数据”视为独立、可测试的故障类别；对操作进行埋点以证明效果。

  3. 多租户身份是下一个架构前沿。 单用户助理正在改造以服务团队：ZeroClaw RBAC/知识作用域、Hermes 稳定 user_id 和 profile 作用域隔离、QwenPaw Hub 管理操作、OpenClaw 操作员权限。启示： principal/scope 应成为会话和工具调用模型中的一等维度，而不是配置附加项。

  4. 记忆正确性如今是可靠性要求，而非功能特性。 召回上限、夜间晋升、压缩模型路由和来源边界在 OpenClaw、QwenPaw、Hermes 和 ZeroClaw 中同时成为热点。长上下文（QwenPaw #8464 中的 340k token 会话）已是主流，而非边缘场景。启示： 记忆生命周期（摄入 → 召回 → 晋升 → 压缩 → 归档）需要明确、可检查的语义和测试。

  5. 成本与循环控制是用户可见的痛点。 Hermes 的 430 次重复调用报告（#137170）和 QwenPaw 的量化 token 浪费（#6116）表明用户正在计量 agent 运行。QwenPaw 在参与度最高的线程上标记 wontfix 是一处值得关注的差异——这可能将注重成本的用户推向竞品。启示： 重复成功检测、调用指纹去重和 token 预算应属于运行时，而不只是告警。

  6. MCP/插件生命周期是运维问题。 空闲 TTL 驱逐失败（OpenClaw #166017）、spawn-broker 子进程上限、重复 stdio 服务器（约 144 MB/子进程开销）和代际不匹配发现（ZeroClaw #11562）是运维事件，而非协议 bug。启示： 将驱逐默认值、broker 上限和注册验证作为一等功能发布。

  7. 配置 schema 信任是留存风险。 “接受但完全未读取”的配置（ZeroClaw #9394、#11589；OpenClaw #172969；Hermes #90040）是一类反复出现的问题，会悄悄破坏用户假设。启示： 校验并接通配置键，或在加载时大声失败。

  8. 发布纪律正在形成差异化。 只有 OpenClaw 维护稳定 + LTS 组合；Hermes 和 ZeroClaw 尽管活动频繁，本窗口未发布任何内容，QwenPaw 仍是发布前 beta。对决策者而言，OpenClaw 目前是生产邻近部署唯一安全的默认选择，而 QwenPaw/ZeroClaw 最好视为高动能、GA 前押注，IronClaw 则视为不活跃。

技术决策者要点： 若需要生产级广度和发布节奏，选择 OpenClaw（同时接受活跃的 P0 状态持久性风险）；若需要团队/渠道特定的工作流自动化，在 Hermes/QwenPaw 的稳定化阶段选择它们；若多租户可审计性和仅追加状态是硬性要求，则关注 ZeroClaw，但这取决于其 P1 安全评审队列能否清空（#9647/#9745 已停滞约 3 个月）。

同赛道项目详细报告

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent 项目摘要 — 2026-10-30

数据说明： 本数据集报告的是过去 24 小时内更新的条目，不一定是当天创建的。PR 评论数不可用。“已合并/已关闭”的 PR 合并报告，因此无法从所提供的数据中完全区分已合并与未合并关闭。

1. 今日概览

Hermes Agent 依然高度活跃：过去 24 小时内有 50 个 issue 和 50 个 PR 被更新，没有新版本发布。Issue 队列严重偏向未完成的工作——50 个更新 issue 中有 48 个仍处于打开/活跃状态——而 PR 吞吐量更强，50 个更新 PR 中有 10 个已合并或关闭。活动集中在 P1 可靠性问题上，涉及安装/更新状态、凭证池轮换、cron 持久性、Kanban worker 稳定性以及 agent 循环控制。社区参与度很高，包括一个 30 条评论的架构 RFC 和一个获得 31 个 👍 的桌面安装功能请求，但若干高严重性 bug 仍缺乏明确关联的修复 PR。总体而言，项目看起来健康且维护活跃，但存在相当大的积压，以及 gateway、cron 和多 profile 子系统中可见的可靠性债务。

2. 版本发布

过去 24 小时内没有发布新版本。

3. 项目进展

报告窗口内有 10 个 PR 被合并或关闭。在可见的已关闭 PR 中，进展集中在交付可观测性、资源安全、文档卫生和 Kanban 正确性方面：

  • PR #98918 — 使本地 STT 回退可配置，避免在小型 VPS 实例上使用昂贵的本地 Whisper 回退。

7. 用户反馈摘要

真实痛点

  • 安装占用与缓存管理： 用户报告小型安装中约 22,600 个 .pyc 文件和超过 303 MiB 的膨胀（#139500），以及位于所有清理器之外的 1.0 GB uv 缓存（#143577）。#139500 中的语气（“开发团队拒绝修复”）表明对长期存在的安装卫生问题感到沮丧。
  • 部署灵活性： 仅前端安装请求（#38519）反映了一个真实的分机使用场景：agent 在一台主机上，桌面 UI 在另一台上。
  • 后台自动化的可靠性： Cron 和 Kanban 用户遇到丢失执行、静默卡住、暂停任务重新激活和 worker 崩溃（#135487、#146428、#145596、#145022）。
  • 规模与会话状态： 几千个会话即可导致高 gateway CPU 和桌面超时（#146643）；压缩可能在 state.db 中重复用户消息（#139210）。
  • 多 profile 与身份摩擦： Profile 范围不匹配、托管范围配置被忽略以及路由的 Discord/cron 会话表明多 profile 设置仍然粗糙（#146237、#90040、#143953）。
  • 提供商与计费信任： 凭证池轮换回退和池化订阅计为一个（#118379）对付费用户来说是一个高信任问题。

数据中可见的使用场景： 远程桌面对 agent 连接、多用户团队 profile、基于 Kanban 的工作流自动化、具有交付保证的定时 cron 任务、读取 MCP 服务器的插件后端，以及包括 Discord、Telegram 和企业微信在内的平台集成。

满意度/不满意度： 社区深度参与并贡献详细的报告和 PR，包括插件维护者更新自己的目录条目（PR #146713）。然而，反复出现的根因家族以及在安装膨胀和会话可见性方面进展缓慢，表明维护者的注意力被分散。整体情绪是建设性的，但对可靠性敏感。

7. 用户反馈摘要

发声者是谁： 主要是使用 Windows 桌面端和 Hub 部署的中文用户，以及大量使用渠道的用户（飞书、QQ、微信、企业微信、钉钉、OneBot、元宝）。

具体痛点：

  • 静默失败侵蚀信任。 #8500（“运行报告 success=True……没有任何用户可见信息表明内容被丢弃”）、#8150（“静默丢弃……无警告”）、#8488（“Visual Compact 静默空操作”）。三份独立报告，同一个抱怨：产品失败时不告诉我。
  • 成本焦虑。 #6116 明确量化了浪费（“许多 API 调用和 token 已被浪费”）。用户正在计量其 agent 运行成本。
  • 长上下文重度使用已是主流，而非边缘场景。 #8464 记录了一个 340k token 的会话。压缩正确性现在是一等可靠性要求。
  • 桌面端的本地化/资源卫生。 #8502（中文路径破坏浏览器打开）、#8490（设置页占用 690 MB RSS）。桌面端打磨落后于后端。
  • 安全默认值。 #8501 —— env list 以明文打印所有密钥，env set 回显已存储的值。社区发起的修复，强烈表明此前并不存在默认安全。
  • 满意度指标： 带有版本/提交固定的详细、可复现报告（2.3.0b1、b12b06ed、2.2.2.post1）表明用户参与度高、技术成熟并投入了真实精力——首次贡献者（#7613、#8400、#8291）也展现出善意。不满集中在 beta 回归的响应速度，以及对成本相关 issue 的 wontfix 决定上。

需要维护者关注的 issue

  • #8500（Auto-Dream 静默记忆丢失）——开放且无关联修复 PR；今日集合中唯一不可恢复数据丢失 bug。应成为明天队列的首要项。
  • #8488（桌面构建缺少 visual_compression 资源）——开放，无修复；很可能只是 PyInstaller spec/datas 的一行条目，因此是低成本、高价值的收益。

结论： 吞吐量强劲，贡献者也在积极参与，但本窗口显示出三个结构性风险——（a）beta 打包/插件回归泄漏到用户侧（#8473、#8488）；（b）静默失败模式侵蚀用户对记忆和上下文功能的信任（#8500、#8150）；（c）大型 PR 评审队列中最老的条目如今已 40–53 天（#7613、#7874）。这些并不需要新增工程能力，更需要的是一套分诊策略：小型 PR 快速通道、“静默失败”测试类别，以及对存在重叠的记忆召回 PR 做出决策。

ZeroClaw 依然高度活跃：过去 24 小时内共有 50 条 issue 更新（33 条开放/活跃，17 条已关闭）和 50 条 PR 更新（44 条开放，6 条已合并/关闭），但未发布新版本。最值得注意的信号是“接收—合并”缺口扩大：44 个 PR 仍处于开放状态，而仅有 6 个关闭；大量开放 PR 带有 size:XL、needs-author-action 或 needs-maintainer-review，说明瓶颈在评审产能，而非贡献者兴趣。活动集中在四个主题：身份与访问安全（按 agent 归属、RBAC、principal 作用域）、仅追加的会话/事件持久化、插件系统可靠性，以及 ZeroCode TUI 打磨。今天关闭了 17 个 issue，反映出实打实的清理势头——包括一项已接受架构 RFC 和若干 S2 bug 修复——同时 v0.9.0 里程碑仍在累积带安全标签的工作。

回归 #11416 自 v0.8.5 起 Slack“is thinking…”状态缺失 UX 回归，报告者询问是否有意为之 已接受

今日修复： #11517（重新加载时提示词丢失）、#11432（卡住的 running 会话）、#11562（manifest/组件代际不匹配）、#11484（重复工具防护）、#11708（工具 schema 不完整）、#11970（无 gateway 构建中缺少级联）、#11792（孤立安装阶段）、#11987（Semgrep 抑制）。

评估： 报告出来的 bug 流是健康的——今天关闭了 8 个稳定性修复，pulldown-cmark 版本提升还移除了一个全仓库范围的 CI 阻塞。未解决风险的集中点在于长期存在的安全问题（#9394、#9647），而非新近回归。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • 面向多租户部署的按发送者 RBAC——#5982。范围已收窄并获接受；已有草稿。是 v0.9.0 或 v0.10 的有力候选。
  • 统一文件接收/解析/投递——#11013 跟踪项，承接已接受的 RFC #9488。跨渠道文件处理是用户反复提出的需求。
  • 公开运行时组合边界——#10993。涉及 agent 运行时的可嵌入性；这是生态/扩展层面的举措，而非终端用户功能。
  • 插件安装重新播种语义——#10162。是安装持久性工作（#11098）的后续。
  • 运维方成本上限覆盖——#11589。cost.allow_override 已有文档但无人读取；该 PR 使其生效。小改动、高价值，可能很快落地。
  • 会话事件重放 + 派生流——#10526 / #11921。RFC 已关闭，实现已开放；这是头条架构事项。
  • ZeroCode TUI 可配置性——按窗格会话数上限（#11731）、transcript 时间戳（#11622）、多选编辑器（#11502）。

v0.9.0 预测： 安全/身份工作（知识图谱作用域、非管理员工具隐藏、守护进程授权修改传播）、pulldown-cmark 安全公告修复，以及 Telegram 未授权通知变更。会话事件历史规模足够大，可能推迟到 v0.9.x 或 v0.10。

7. 用户反馈摘要

真实用户表达的痛点：

  • “这个‘Copy’按钮对我没用。它对我的剪贴板完全没有任何作用。”——基础 TUI 功能损坏（S1），#11418。
  • “我同时启用了 skill_improvement 和 skill_creation，但学习循环只对 CLI/cron 风格的运行生效。”——对 Matrix/webhook/web-UI 用户而言是功能静默降级，#11332。
  • “我 agent 的所有技能都在一个 skill bundle 里……但技能审查 fork 看不到其中任何一个。”——#11333。
  • “在 agent 回合仍在运行时重新加载仪表盘页面，会让用户提示词从屏幕上*和 localStorage 中消失。”*——正常使用中的数据丢失感知，#11517（现已关闭）。
  • “守护进程死亡时正处于进行中回合的会话，会永久停留在 state = 'running'。”——影响运维方对会话状态的信任，#11432（现已关闭）。
  • “自 v0.8.5 起……唯一的生命迹象就是入站确认表情反应（👀）。”——Slack 用户失去了进度反馈，#11416。

满意信号： 对范围明确的 bug 响应迅速（多个 10 月初提交的 S2/S3 issue 今天关闭）；维护者在讨论串中主动收窄范围，而不是让提案停滞；ZeroCode UX 工作由一位资深贡献者以持续、聚焦的 PR 流交付。

不满意信号： Slack 反馈回归；本地模型用户（Ollama qwen3.5:9b、MLX-LM）反复报告工具循环损坏；以及“被接受却完全未被读取”的配置（#9394、#11589）——这类 bug 会侵蚀对配置 schema 的信任。

8. 积压事项观察

条目 存在时长 关注点
#9394 配对仪表盘被忽略 + 配对码不过期 自 2026-07-26 起开放（约 14 周） priority:p1、security:pairing，标记为 release:v0.9.0，未关联修复 PR。未解决风险最高且实现零进展的条目。
#9647 知识图谱跨 agent 访问 自 2026-08-01 起开放 S0 严重程度。修复 PR #9745 自 2026-08-04 起一直停留在 needs-maintainer-review——将近三个月。需要分配评审资源，而不是更多作者工作。
#5982 按发送者 RBAC 自 2026-04-22 起开放（约 27 周） 已接受且范围收窄，有 11 条评论，但收窄后的设计没有 PR。数据集中最古老的高互动功能请求。
#10999 Discord 插件安装证明 自 2026-09-20 起开放，status:blocked 因 9 条评论而阻塞；运行时已验证，打包证明仍待补齐。需要决定验收标准是否改变。
#10162 插件安装播种重试 自 2026-08-20 起开放，in-progress 部分修复已通过 #11098 落地；已安装场景仍缺少一致认可的答案。
#11013 统一文件接收跟踪项 自 2026-09-20 起开放 实现批次跟踪项仅有 3 条评论——对一个横切工作流而言可见度偏低。
#11301 / #11313 自 2026-10-01 起开放 两者均为 priority:p1、risk:high、size:XL，等待维护者评审——属于没有推进的 P1 安全队列。
#11320 / #11322 自 2026-10-01 起开放 深层依赖栈（#11319 → #11339 → #11165 → …）；每一层都重新堆叠。堆叠 PR 链是结构性评审瓶颈。
#11265 用户密码生命周期 CLI 自 2026-09-30 起开放，do-not-merge 明确标记为 do-not-merge，并堆叠在两个未合并 PR（#11264、#11313）之上——在基础 PR 落地前不会推进。
#10294 file_write 创建/覆盖歧义 自 2026-08-24 起开放 对 transcript 消费方而言是 observability/审计缺口；优先级低，但会阻碍可靠的文件效果审计。

数据说明

  • 仅展示按评论数排序的 50 个 issue 中的前 30 个，以及 50 个 PR 中的前 20 个；PR 评论数返回为 undefined，因此 PR 互动度是根据标签和范围推断，而非实测讨论量。
  • 在报告的 6 个已合并/关闭 PR 中，仅 #12095 在提供的样本中可见。
  • 标签计数和评论总数为 2026-10-30 的时点快照。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-30

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-30 02:07 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-30

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains a high-velocity project: 500 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with 174 issues closed and 192 PRs merged or closed, indicating strong triage and merge throughput. Two releases shipped: a security-focused stable patch, v2026.10.9, and a gateway-only v2026.9.36 extended-stable/LTS release. The active backlog is still large—326 open issues and 308 open PRs among updated items—and is dominated by P0/P1 reliability work around gateway state databases, session lifecycle integrity, MCP runtime management, and the update/recovery path. Overall project health is good on responsiveness and release cadence, but risk is concentrated in state/session durability and several long-running P0/P1 issues. Note: the dataset shows the top 50 issues by comment count and top 30 PRs; PR comment counts were unavailable.

2. Releases

v2026.10.9 — stable security patch

Release v2026.10.9

Key changes called out in the release notes:

  • fast-uri 4.2.3: rejects malformed URI schemes and hosts during MCP schema validation.
  • Zod collection limits: oversized collections are rejected early in A2UI and the Discord embedded app SDK.
  • IMAP sender parsing: now uses nodemailer 10.1.4 so spoofed senders are handled correctly.

Breaking changes / migration notes: None are stated in the provided release excerpt. This is a dependency-hardening patch; standard upgrade and gateway restart apply. Teams using MCP schema validation, A2UI, the Discord embedded app SDK, or IMAP ingestion should prioritize this release.

Release validation caveat: Flaky tests observed during 2026.10.9 validation are tracked in #187490. The release classified them as flakes; a parallel fix on main is required by policy.

v2026.9.36 — gateway-only extended-stable (LTS equivalent)

Release v2026.9.36

  • Gateway-only extended-stable release, described as the project’s current LTS equivalent.
  • Based on OpenClaw from the end of September 2026, plus critical security updates, reliability/performance fixes, and new model support.
  • Best suited to conservative deployments that need a supported, security-maintained baseline rather than the newest stable features.

3. Project Progress

The 192 merged/closed PRs and 174 closed issues indicate meaningful cleanup, though the dataset does not separate merged from closed-only PRs.

Notable closed issues in the active top-50:

  • #178000 — Session-state races were misclassified as reason=unknown, triggering cross-provider model fallback. Closed after being rated diamond lobster / P1.
  • #186813 — In-chat managed update (gateway.update.run) hung indefinitely in epoll_wait on SQLite lock contention. P0, closed.
  • #156635 — Copilot context budget stayed at synthetic 128k fallback after account discovery. Closed.
  • #187468 — Update failure report for 2026.9.8. Closed.

PRs advancing key areas:

  • Update/recovery hardening: #188034 retains authority through fallback publication; #188021 excludes resolved captures from recovery ambiguity; #188024 reports failed scheduled registry observations; #188027 reads named recovery via primary key; #188010 retries installation discovery after returned failures (closed).
  • Gateway responsiveness/performance: #188033 keeps the Gateway responsive during plugin tool discovery; #188030 stops doctor re-reading SQLite inspection copies; #188025 stops GitHub readiness from copying whole agent databases (P1, security-sensitive).
  • Web/UI correctness: #188013 preserves authored CSP in relative HTML previews (security-boundary risk flagged); #188017 fixes duplicate dividers in the session Advanced menu (closed); #188039 adds canonical Unicode matching to workspace rail file search.
  • Channels/integrations: #188003 matches canonically equivalent names in Teams live directory search; #188018 fixes Matrix image replies in progress mode.
  • Memory: #186649 opts topic files into per-entry chunking with a marker.
  • Developer experience: #187962 adds OPENCLAW_DEV_RELOAD_BUNDLED_PLUGINS for bundled plugin code reload in development.

4. Community Hot Topics

The most-commented issues reveal sustained user focus on state durability, memory promotion, and MCP tool reliability.

  1. #164294 — Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes (38 comments, P2).
    The gateway’s own WAL checkpoint on state/openclaw.sqlite is permanently blocked by an in-process reader; consecutiveBlocked grows and checkpointing never completes. Underlying need: predictable SQLite maintenance and bounded WAL growth under real gateway load.

  2. #150635 — Short-term recall retention evicts recalled entries nightly, so dreaming deep phase never promotes (23 comments, P2).
    At the 512-entry cap, nightly ingestion stages zero-recall entries and the deep phase never promotes. Underlying need: coherent memory lifecycle semantics between short-term recall capacity, dreaming, and promotion.

  3. #120385 — Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for scheduled/cron and memory-flush turns; MCP tools missing (22 comments, P2).
    Scheduled jobs fail with “Unknown tool id,” surfaced only as a generic exec failure. Underlying need: tool-catalog parity across interactive, cron, and memory-flush execution paths.

  4. #164923 — One workspace promotes 0/512 while sibling workspaces promote 50–90% (19 comments, P2).
    openclaw memory promote returns no candidates even with thresholds overridden to zero. Underlying need: deterministic, inspectable filtering in multi-workspace memory promotion.

  5. #172837 — Codex nativeSubagentAssignments never removed after completion delivery gives up (18 comments, P1).
    Every new parent thread re-pins and re-sends stale assignments. Underlying need: lifecycle cleanup and retry-exhaustion semantics for native subagents.

PR-side activity: Comment counts were unavailable in the dataset, but several PRs are marked “ready for maintainer look,” including #188003, #188021, #187986, and #184511. The long-running XL PR #181813 (gateway native state owner identity) has been open since 2026-10-23 and is awaiting maintainer review.

5. Bugs & Stability

Active issues updated in the last 24 hours, ranked by severity. Fix PRs are noted where identifiable.

P0 — release-blocking / severe availability

  • #166634 — Late reclamation commit checkpoint failure leaves an agent permanently unavailable after crash recovery; agent refuses chat.history, chat.metadata, models.list, and progress-card requests. 18 comments. No linked fix PR shown.
  • #162211 — Gateway startup blocks the event loop for 40–200s; health monitor misreads the stall as a disconnect and escalates into a restart loop. 14 comments. No linked fix PR shown.
  • #158592 — After macOS sleep/wake, prepared model runtime publication for one agent times out and never recovers; every inbound message fails with “runtime owner was not published” until gateway restart. 11 comments. No linked fix PR shown.
  • #141413 — macOS app omits token for local Gateway using a protected SecretRef; embedded dashboard can authenticate but external connection does not. P0, security review needed, 7 comments, 2 👍.
  • #186813 — Managed update hangs in epoll_wait on SQLite transaction lock contention. Closed; likely addressed, but no specific merge PR is listed in the provided data.

P1 — serious functional/crash-loop regressions

  • #172837 — Codex native subagent assignments leak after delivery gives up; re-pinned on every new parent thread. 18 comments. No fix PR shown.
  • #177656 — Native host exec returns “Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission” without a child result; at least 28 failures on stable 2026.10.5. 17 comments. No fix PR shown.
  • #166017 — mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs default (10 min) is not applied when unset; MCP runtimes are never evicted, spawn broker reaches its 256-child hard cap, and all exec/read/MCP starts fail. 13 comments. Linked fix PR open.
  • #159094 — Gateway owns the state-lifecycle lease but internal workers report another process owns it, closing agent DB execution admission. 14 comments.
  • #126950 — Telegram opaque callback payloads (tgcb1:) silently dropped for non-plugin callers. 11 comments, 1 👍. Linked fix PR open.
  • #163566 — Durable context-engine turns stuck as session-rebound after update repair; session-resource-loader burns ~100s CPU per turn. 10 comments.
  • #167876 — Talk consultations lose caller authority after session setup completes; security review needed. 9 comments, 1 👍.
  • #158070 — Preflight compaction fails with “agent tool caller authority is no longer active” while the run waits in a lane queue, voiding in-flight delivery. 9 comments.
  • #148789 — Model fallback chain exhausts every candidate on a harness-level session failure and misattributes it to the last fallback model. 9 comments.
  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive idles 15+ minutes in plugin-capture stage and never reaches agent DB repair. 8 comments. Related performance PR #188030.
  • #155396 — Ordinary Codex tool turns fail closed on provenance_rejected during final-answer recovery. 8 comments.
  • #160762 — claude-cli + Telegram: a message sent mid-turn is dropped; drained prompt carries the previous message’s body. 7 comments.

P2 — notable friction/correctness

  • #164394 — Control UI WebChat transcript jitters continuously when scrolling into history. 13 comments.
  • #177094 — System-notice delivery mirror displaces the turn’s last answer into collapsed tool steps after restart/reload. 9 comments.
  • #172969 — registerCliBackend without modelProvider is silently dropped; surfaces as “Invalid URL: must be http or https.” 8 comments.
  • #176342 — Stale-lease integrity gates serialize agent startup after unclean shutdown, causing minutes-long unavailability. 7 comments.
  • #186973 — /clear state check renders a stale update-history banner weeks after the run, across gateway restart and reboot. 7 comments.
  • #165433 — chat.send rejects reconnect envelopes with __controlUiReconnectResume when the client is not an Operator UI client. 7 comments.
  • #164690 — claude-cli runs spawn every stdio MCP server twice; each Gateway stdio child carries ~144 MB supervisor wrapper overhead, not configurable. 7 comments.
  • #167667 — ChatGPT Responses tool continuation fails with “Rustponses cannot replay,” surfaced as a generic agent-run error. P1, 6 comments, 1 👍.

Stability assessment: The highest-risk cluster is gateway/session state integrity and crash recovery. Several P0/P1 issues have been open for weeks without linked fix PRs, while update-path and doctor-performance fixes are actively in review. The 2026.10.9 security patch is welcome, but it does not address the core state-lifecycle failures.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active user-requested features, ranked by likely relevance:

  • #6757 — Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool). P2, 9 comments, 2 👍, open since February 2026. High strategic fit with the project’s memory/context work; a strong candidate for roadmap attention.
  • #172547 — Exclude fenced dreaming ranges from memory-search indexing and recall signal. 7 comments. Directly connected to the hot memory-promotion issues; likely to be folded into memory-core fixes.
  • #112638 — session.maintenance enforce mode does not bound the store; thread/channel entries are exempt from reclaim. 8 comments, open since July. Strong reliability/operability signal.
  • #163739 — Make Control UI Ctrl+Shift+A (Archive) configurable; it collides with browser shortcuts. 7 comments, 1 👍. Small, user-facing UX fix.
  • #140244 — Support --prompt-file in openclaw infer model run. 7 comments, 1 👍. Automation-oriented CLI improvement.
  • #154524 — Expose chat messages as headings for screen-reader navigation. 6 comments. Accessibility gap.
  • #147732 — Paragraph-level RTL direction for mixed Persian/Arabic/Hebrew + English messages. 6 comments. Internationalization/UI correctness.
  • #150743 — QQ channel sustainability: Tencent handoff stalled; clarify long-term support. 7 comments. Ecosystem/support-model concern, not a code feature.

Prediction for next version: The strongest near-term signals are memory/recall correctness (multiple high-comment issues plus PR #186649), update/recovery hardening (already a cluster of PRs), MCP runtime lifecycle defaults, and Control UI accessibility/localization fixes. Agent-triggered compaction is the highest-value larger feature but has been pending since February and may need a product decision.

7. User Feedback Summary

Recurring pain points:

  • State and session durability: Users report agents becoming permanently unavailable after crash recovery, WAL checkpoints never completing, stale leases serializing startup, and session-state races triggering cross-provider fallback. These are the most damaging reported experiences because they require gateway restarts or leave agents unusable.
  • Memory/dreaming inconsistency: Multiple reports describe promotion pipelines that silently produce zero candidates, evict recalled entries nightly, or index dreaming output that can never be promoted. Users are clearly relying on memory as a core workflow, not a peripheral feature.
  • Update and recovery reliability: In-chat updates hanging on SQLite locks, doctor --fix idling, failed registry lookups recorded as successes, and package-swap failures. This erodes trust in the upgrade path, especially for stable/LTS users.
  • MCP/resource management: MCP runtimes not evicted at default TTL, spawn broker hitting 256 children, duplicate stdio servers under claude-cli, and ~144 MB wrapper overhead per child. Operators on multi-agent or Docker-sandbox setups feel this acutely.
  • UI/UX friction: WebChat transcript jitter, stale banners, system notices displacing final answers, shortcut collisions, RTL rendering, and screen-reader navigation gaps.
  • Platform-specific issues: macOS Homebrew Node upgrades breaking bare openclaw commands; Android repeatedly querying unknown agent openclaw; QQ channel support uncertainty.

Satisfaction signals: Strong triage volume, rapid closure of several P0/P1 issues, a clear LTS-equivalent release, and a security patch cadence demonstrate responsive maintenance. The “ready for maintainer look” labels and structured rating system suggest a healthy review process.

Dissatisfaction signals: Several P0/P1 issues remain open for weeks without linked fix PRs, and many high-comment issues carry needs-product-decision, needs-maintainer-review, or stale labels. Users are investing significant effort in detailed reproductions; delayed decisions on those reports risk burnout and workarounds.

8. Backlog Watch

Important issues/PRs that are old, high-impact, or waiting on maintainer/product action:

  • #6757 — Agent-triggered context compaction. Open since 2026-02-02, 9 comments, 2 👍, needs product decision. Longest-running high-value feature request in the visible set.
  • #112638 — session.maintenance enforce does not bound the store. Open since 2026-07-22, 8 comments. Operationally important for long-running deployments.
  • #120385 — Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for cron/memory-flush turns. Open since 2026-08-08, 22 comments. High community engagement; affects scheduled automation reliability.
  • #126950 — Telegram opaque callback payloads dropped. Open since 2026-08-21, 11 comments, 1 👍, linked fix PR open. Channel integration blocker.
  • #141413 — macOS app omits token for local Gateway using SecretRef. Open since 2026-09-07, P0, 7 comments, 2 👍, needs security review. High severity with relatively low comment volume—may be under-triaged.
  • #150635 — Dreaming deep phase never promotes due to recall eviction. Open since 2026-09-17, 23 comments, diamond-lobster rating, needs product decision. High user impact and high engagement.
  • #158592 — Sleep/wake runtime publication timeout. Open since 2026-09-26, P0, 11 comments, needs live repro. Severe but reproduction-dependent.
  • #162211 — Startup event-loop block → restart loop. Open since 2026-09-30, P0, 14 comments, needs maintainer review. Release-blocker severity.
  • #166634 — Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable. Open since 2026-10-07, P0, 18 comments. One of the highest-severity open issues.
  • PR #154033 — Codex native tool-output images from raw response items. Open since 2026-09-20, needs proof, security-boundary and message-delivery risk. Long-lived PR with protocol-level implications.
  • PR #181813 — Expose held native state owner identity. Open since 2026-10-23, XL, P2, ready for maintainer look. Relevant to the state-owner/lease confusion cluster.
  • PR #184511 — Commit invitation membership with involvement. Open since 2026-10-26, P2, ready for maintainer look, proof sufficient. Authorization/session correctness.
  • #150743 — QQ channel sustainability and Tencent handoff. 7 comments, open since 2026-09-17. Needs an ecosystem/support decision rather than a code fix.

Bottom line: OpenClaw is shipping quickly and maintaining a credible LTS/security cadence, but its most valuable users are hitting state/session durability and memory-promotion failures that remain unresolved for weeks. The next release cycle should be judged on whether the P0 state-lifecycle cluster (#166634, #162211, #158592) and the memory-promotion cluster (#150635, #164923, #172547) receive concrete fixes rather than further triage.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-10-30 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent OSS landscape is consolidating around a common architectural stack — a gateway process owning session/state, an MCP tool layer, a memory subsystem, and a multi-channel delivery surface — while vendors differentiate on deployment model (single-user vs multi-tenant), language/runtime, and channel reach. Activity is deeply uneven: OpenClaw operates at an order of magnitude above peers (500 issues + 500 PRs touched daily), Hermes/ZeroClaw/QwenPaw cluster at a focused 40–55 items/day, and IronClaw is effectively dormant this window. Across every active project, the dominant engineering theme has shifted from capability to durability and trust: crash-safe state, honest failure reporting, memory provenance, and identity scoping now outrank feature shipping in community engagement. Release cadence is bifurcating — OpenClaw is the only project maintaining both a fast stable channel and an LTS-equivalent, which is becoming a meaningful competitive moat for conservative adopters.

2. Activity Comparison (last 24h)

Project Issues updated (open/closed) PRs updated (open/merged-closed) Release status Health score*
OpenClaw ~500 (174 closed) ~500 (192 merged/closed) 2 releases: v2026.10.9 stable security patch; v2026.9.36 gateway-only LTS 8.5 / 10
Hermes Agent 50 (48 open / 2 closed) 50 (10 merged/closed, 40 open) None 7.5 / 10
IronClaw 0 0 (2 open Dependabot) None 4.5 / 10
QwenPaw 15 (10 closed / 5 open) 40 (13 merged/closed, 27 open) None (pre-2.3.0 beta stabilization) 7.5 / 10
ZeroClaw 50 (17 closed / 33 open) 50 (6 merged/closed, 44 open) None (between v0.8.7 and v0.9.0) 7.0 / 10

*Health score is a derived composite of triage/merge throughput, release cadence, open-backlog severity, and unresolved P0/P1 risk. It is directional, not a maintainer metric. OpenClaw scores highest on throughput and release discipline but carries concentrated P0 state-durability risk; QwenPaw/Hermes score similarly from opposite directions (velocity vs. backlog clearing). IronClaw's score reflects low activity, not instability.

Reading the table: OpenClaw's raw throughput is ~10× the next-largest project. QwenPaw is the most PR-heavy relative to issues (40:15), indicating implementation outpacing intake — a review-bandwidth signature. ZeroClaw shows the widest intake-to-merge gap (44 open vs. 6 closed PRs), its principal structural risk. Hermes is the only project showing backlog-clearing behavior (months-old PRs merged this window).

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers

  • Community scale: ~500 issues + 500 PRs/day vs. 50/50 (Hermes, ZeroClaw) and 15/40 (QwenPaw). The contributor and triage base is an order of magnitude larger, which is why it can sustain 174 issue closures and 192 PR dispositions in a single day.
  • Dual release channel: The only project shipping both a stable security patch (v2026.10.9) and a gateway-only LTS-equivalent (v2026.9.36 with backported security + reliability fixes). This is a concrete differentiator for conservative/enterprise adopters.
  • Process maturity: Structured severity ratings (P0–P2, "diamond lobster"), explicit "ready for maintainer look" states, and a release-validation caveat policy (flaky tests tracked to a parallel main fix) indicate a governance layer peers lack.
  • Integration surface breadth: Channels (Telegram, Matrix, Teams, Discord, QQ, IMAP), Web/UI, Code Mode, A2UI, and an MCP runtime — the widest in the set.

Technical approach differences

  • Gateway-centric, SQLite-backed state: Session lifecycle, state-lifecycle leases, WAL checkpoints, and crash recovery are first-class gateway concerns. This is the source of both its strongest guarantee ambitions and its highest-severity open bugs (#166634, #162211, #158592).
  • Memory/dreaming as a subsystem: Short-term recall caps, nightly "deep phase" promotion, and dreaming-range indexing are unique to OpenClaw among this cohort and drive its top high-comment issues (#150635, #164923).
  • MCP as a runtime with lifecycle management: Session idle TTLs, spawn-broker child caps, and runtime eviction are treated as operational concerns (#166017) rather than just protocol plumbing.

Community size comparison: OpenClaw is the reference implementation and the gravity well of the ecosystem; QwenPaw and ZeroClaw each run at roughly 10% of its daily item volume, and IronClaw is currently inactive. Hermes is the closest analogue in scope but at ~10% of OpenClaw's throughput and without a release channel.
