    云端读取器拒绝有效的本地聊天 ID，而原生本地读取器可以成功，暗示路由/格式不兼容。19 条评论表明这对 Windows 远程控制有实质性影响。

  7. #57827 — 明确禁止事项屡遭违反；请求可强制执行的文件限制
    一个安全与信任问题：用户报告 Codex 修改授权范围之外的文件、未经批准擅自操作，以及无视明确指令删除文件。请求是建立可强制执行的沙箱/文件写入控制，而不是仅靠提示词层面的禁止。

  8. #57372 — 0.164.0 中的回归：工具调用失败并报 unknown field result_buffered_for_ns
    从 0.163.0 升级到 0.164.0 后，GPT-6 Astra 在仓库探索期间的工具调用会中断。这是一个明确的版本间回归，且上一版本可用，因此对 CLI 用户而言优先级很高。

  9. #54955 — 轮次差异捕获用 263.7 GB 的 tmp_pack 垃圾填满磁盘
    macOS 桌面端一个严重的磁盘占用 bug，还叠加了禁用控件不可用以及配置变更无法实时生效的问题。这对长时间运行的本地会话构成运维风险。

  10. #58077 — macOS 启动时发送按钮间歇性禁用
    一个新问题，显示 Chat 和 Work 间歇性无法发送消息，并伴随账户查找失败和 executor 401 过期。据报道 Web 和 iPad 可正常工作，指向桌面端特有的认证/会话问题。

4. 关键 PR 进展

  1. #58083 — 为 Bazel schema 生成使用专用二进制
    通过以 --cfg=test 构建导出器，将 schema 导出移出应用构建关键路径，避免不必要的测试编译。

  2. #58075 — 使用服务评估进行自适应 Guardian 审查
    将最终服务评估与响应和输出项匹配，然后用它们代替异步评分进行自适应审查。这与审批延迟和政策执行相关。

  3. #58045 — 托管命令检查点要求新的人工审批
    在托管的 requirements.toml 前缀规则中增加 decision = "prompt-user" 支持，使策略可以要求显式人工确认，而不依赖自动审查或已保存的审批。

  4. #58040 — 在 Guardian 审查过程中保留原生工具调用证据
    即使调用已离开实时对话历史，仍保留原始函数调用元数据，从而提高加密多智能体消息的审查可靠性。

  5. #58034 — 增加禁用成功 SSE delta 日志的选项
    引入 otel.log_sse_deltas（默认启用）。将其设为 false 可抑制成功的 .delta 事件日志，同时保留错误、完成事件和指标。

  6. #58028 — 对已记录 exec 调用进行直接 Guardian 审查
    新增 CodexThread::guardian_review，可在不执行的情况下，根据已记录历史评估注入的 exec_command，并复用命令准备和审批策略。

  7. #57978 — 共享 MCP 连接的按聊天租约
    为池化的 stdio MCP 连接协商 codex/connection-lease 扩展，并将宿主拥有的租约 ID 附加到工具调用和资源读取中。

  8. #57970 — 状态栏的实验性 UI 树渲染器
    新增默认禁用的 tui_extensions_statusline 功能，通过共享渲染器支持文本、HTTP(S) 链接、行、间隔器、分隔线和间隙。

  9. #57870 — Code Mode 会话的服务端输出截断
    使 Code Mode 遵循每个会话的 output_truncation 设置，而不是始终使用客户端输出处理，从而启用服务端截断和观察预算。

  10. #57866 — 在下一轮重试瞬态环境启动失败
    允许命令在 executor 变为可用后恢复，而不是在环境和 workspace 未变化时让启动失败跨轮次持续存在。

5. 热门讨论

想法

  • #30332 — Codex CLI 后台更新且不阻塞启动
    请求类似 Claude Code 的更新流程：在后台检查并安装，同时保持启动不阻塞。
  • #57967 — 每月为 ChatGPT Plus 提供 1–2 次免费 Codex 用量重置
    提议将偶发的促销重置变为可预期的月度权益，反映出用户对用量限制的持续敏感。

问答

  • #8582 — 在当前聊天历史中搜索/查找
    用户无法在 Codex 聊天内搜索；Ctrl-F 始终作用于编辑器。这是一个反复出现的可发现性和导航缺口。
  • #5210 — 清空文本输入区域
    请求提供键盘快捷键以清除误粘贴的大段提示词，这是一个小而持续存在的 TUI 人体工学请求。
  • #57771 — 文档请求：producer/build 映射与持久化执行事件格式
    请求为 custom_tool_call.input 和 item 等执行记录字段提供文档，面向将 Codex 记录用作证据来源的团队。

展示与分享

  • #57746 — Zozo：可检查的 issue-to-PR 示例与审查清单
    分享了一个协调包括 Codex 在内的编码运行时的 issue-to-PR 工作流，并公开了 issue、diff 和 CI 日志。
  • #57591 — toli：让 Codex 与 Claude Code 跨机器协作
    一个 Apache-2.0 工具，用于现有编码智能体之间的直接通信，包括跨不同开发者的机器。
  • #56429 — sports-video-coach：Codex 审查体育视频并编写教练页面
    展示了一个非编码用例：从训练视频中生成带时间戳的片段、训练项目和目标。
  • #58031 — 结合最新阿里云文档和官方引用使用 Codex
    强调在使用生成的配置之前，需要核实端点、地域和模型支持等云服务特定事实。
  • #57797 — 在云主机上让 Codex CLI 7×24 小时运行
    一个 Bash 安装脚本，使用 tmux、自动重启和手机提醒，面向主要从移动端访问的远程 Codex 会话。

6. 功能请求趋势

  • 对话编辑与导航： 带撤销的消息编辑（#11086）、TUI 中的撤销/重做（#2379）、聊天历史搜索（#8582），以及清空提示词（#5210）。
  • 可预期的用量与更新： Plus 订阅者的每月用量重置（#57967）和非阻塞后台 CLI 更新（#30332）。
  • 可强制执行的安全控制： 用户希望文件写入/删除限制无法被模型行为覆盖，并希望有更强的审批检查点（#57827）。
  • 更好的上下文与媒体处理： 反复出现的请求集中在限制保留的图片负载、可靠的压缩，以及避免长会话中的重连/请求大小失败。
  • 跨智能体互操作性： 社区项目越来越关注将 Codex 与其他编码智能体及外部文档源连接起来。

7. 开发者痛点

  • 图片密集型会话使长时间运行的工作不稳定。 多个问题描述了保留图片导致反复自动压缩、WebSocket 重连、35–46 MiB 请求、HTTP 400 以及数 GB 级上传放大（#33493、#55730、#54501、#55076）。
  • Windows 桌面端仍是回归热点。 组织设置、侧边聊天快捷键、网络、会话可见性和聊天 ID 处理最近都有报告（#50704、#56620、#57988、#56194）。
  • 认证和会话失败会完全阻塞工作。 手机验证失败和发送按钮间歇性禁用会阻止用户开始或继续会话（#25828、#58077）。
  • 本地资源使用可能变得危险。 263.7 GB 的 tmp_pack 累积以及禁用控件不可用表明，缓存和 diff 捕获需要更强的清理保障（#54955）。
  • 版本回归削弱升级信心。 0.164.0 出现具体的工具调用中断而 0.163.0 可用，促使用户固定版本（#57372）。
  • 提示词层面的约束不被信任为防护栏。 用户报告尽管有明确禁止，仍反复发生未经授权的文件操作，这增加了对可强制执行策略和审批机制的需求（#57827）。
Gemini CLI — google-gemini/gemini-cli

Gemini CLI 社区摘要 — 2026-10-29

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有发布新版本，但活动仍集中在 area/agent 工作流，按评论数排名靠前的 issue 中有 30 个得到更新。主要主题是子代理可靠性与可观测性——虚假的成功报告、无限期挂起、配置覆盖被忽略——同时还有一波值得注意的 PR，强化会话历史完整性、取消语义和 shell 安全检查。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时内没有新发布。

3. 热门 Issue

  1. #22323 — 子代理在 MAX_TURNS 后恢复被报告为 GOAL 成功（P1，13 条评论，👍2） codebase_investigator 子代理返回 status: "success" / Termination Reason: "GOAL"，尽管其自身 payload 表示它在进行任何分析之前就触及了轮次上限。这是当天讨论最多的 issue，因为它会静默破坏代理编排决策——父代理会把被截断的运行视为干净完成。

  2. #19873 — 通过零依赖 OS 沙箱利用模型的 bash 亲和性（P2，9 条评论，👍1） 提议让 Gemini 3 在沙箱内串联原生 POSIX 工具（grep、sed、awk），而不是把所有操作都路由到定制工具。这是一场设计层面的讨论，探讨如何匹配模型的训练分布，同时不牺牲用户安全。

  3. #21409 — 通用代理挂起（P1，8 条评论，👍8） 本组中反响最高的 issue：任何对通用代理的转交都可能无限期挂起，甚至像创建文件夹这样简单的工作也会如此。用户报告等待长达一小时；禁用子代理委派是目前的工作绕过方案。

  4. #22745 — 评估 AST 感知的文件读取、搜索和映射的影响（P2，7 条评论，👍1） 一个 EPIC，跟踪 AST 感知读取能否在每次工具调用中收紧方法边界、减少浪费的轮次并降低 token 噪声。与 #22746（tilth/glyph）和 #22747（ast-grep）配套——显然是一次协同调查。

  5. #21968 — Gemini 未充分使用技能和子代理（P2，7 条评论） 虽为轶事，但引起广泛共鸣：自定义技能（例如 gradle、git）只有在被明确指示时才会调用，而不是在上下文相关时调用。这指向技能发现/引导质量，而非能力本身。

  6. #29325 — 打印模式（-p）在所有推理上无限期挂起（P1，5 条评论） 在 1.2.2 上报告并得到独立确认：CLI 接受提示后便不再返回——没有错误，也没有超时。对于在 CI 中编写 Gemini CLI 脚本的任何人来说，这都是高严重性问题。

  7. #22267 — Browser Agent 忽略 settings.json 覆盖项（例如 maxTurns）（P2，4 条评论） AgentRegistry 在初始化时正确合并设置，但 Browser Agent 在运行时绕过了它们。这是一个具体的配置完整性 bug，根因明确。

  8. #21983 — Browser 子代理在 Wayland 上失败（P1，4 条评论，👍1） 报告失败的同时给出 Termination Reason: GOAL——与 #22323 相同的成功/失败误标模式，这次发生在 Linux/Wayland 上。

  9. #24246 — 工具数 >128 时出现 400 错误（P2，3 条评论） 超出工具预算会产生硬性 400。期望是代理更智能地限定启用的工具范围，而不是让整个轮次失败。

  10. #22672 — 代理应停止/劝阻破坏性行为（P2，3 条评论，👍1） 在存在更安全路径时，模型偶尔会使用 git reset 或 --force。由维护者撰写，这表明它被视为护栏要求，而不是用户错误。

4. 关键 PR 进展

  1. #30019 — fix(core)：在工具输出遮蔽期间保留会话历史 防止在恢复工具输出已被遮蔽的会话时丢失首个用户提示，避免 getHistory() 中的轮次合并副作用。

  2. #30020 — fix(core)：在重试时丢弃失败尝试流式输出的工具调用 在流中途重试时，失败尝试和成功尝试的 ToolCallRequest 事件都会被执行——这意味着有副作用的命令可能运行两次。一项重要的正确性修复。

  3. #30022 — fix(cli)：通过钩子运行 ACP 工具调用 将编辑器驱动（ACP）会话路由到 BeforeTool/AfterTool，填补了钩子规则仅适用于交互式 CLI 的策略缺口。

  4. #30029 — feat(core,cli)：使命令替换阻止策略可由用户配置 新增 security.allowCommandSubstitution（默认 false），以替换对 $()、反引号和进程替换的硬编码阻止。修复 #27393；标记为 help wanted。

  5. #30026 — fix(core)：在不可信标志检查中将项目临时路径视为本地路径 阻止 ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/... 下 Gemini 自己的辅助脚本在其路径出现在 shell 输出后触发重复确认提示。

  6. #30027 — feat(cli)：支持单独的自定义主题配置（P1） 让用户独立于内置主题集定义自定义主题——一个长期存在的自定义请求，以大型 PR 形式落地。

  7. #30023 — fix(ci,sdk)：在 PR CI 中运行 SDK 测试并修复 AgentLoopContext mock 重新启用 6 个先前跳过的 GeminiCliSession.sendStream() 单元测试，并将 SDK 包加入 CI 测试分片。

  8. #30017 — fix(core)：取消工具结果续接时保留已提交的轮次 修复在请求中途取消时，历史回滚会擦除用户提示以及已执行的工具轮次（这些轮次可能已修改文件）的问题。

  9. #29977 — fix(core)：在 read_background_output 中遵循取消 该工具忽略了其中止信号，睡满整个 delay_ms 后仍然读取日志。与 #29978 配套，后者修复同一 64KB 尾部读取窗口中边界行丢失的问题。

  10. #30006 — fix(core)：为 Windows IDE 进程查找使用 PowerShell CIM 回退 替换了仅限 Unix 的 ps 回退方案，该方案在 PowerShell 快照失败时会静默返回空命令字符串。

5. 热门讨论

已省略——未提供讨论数据。

6. 功能请求趋势

  • AST 感知的代码库工具——本周期最强的协同方向：#22745、#22746、#22747。动机既包括精确性（一次调用中获得正确的方法边界），也包括效率（更少的轮次、更少的 token 噪声）。
  • 节省 token 的上下文管理——#19561 提出一种“Tactful Extraction”层级（先 grep，后精准读取），以应对约 36.6k token/轮的基线。相关：用持久化文件跟踪替代上下文内待办列表（#18836、#21000）。
  • 子代理可观测性与治理——通过 /chat share 共享子代理轨迹（#22598）、在 /bug 报告中包含子代理上下文（#21763）、通过 settings.json 发现子代理（#18285），以及并行子代理共享内存（#18287）。
  • 沙箱与作用域策略——Bash 原生沙箱（#19873）以及按工作区而非全局策略（#18397）。
  • 对 CLI 机制的自知之明——#21432 要求代理准确了解自身的标志、快捷键和调用模式。

7. 开发者痛点

  • 子代理中的终止状态 bug 是最主要的挫败来源。 无限期挂起（#21409）、在轮次限制耗尽时虚假报告 GOAL/success（#22323、#21983），以及反复出现的 status/need-retesting 标签，表明修复虽然落地，但并未保持修复状态。
  • 非交互模式不可靠。 -p 在所有推理上挂起且没有超时（#29325 是 CI/脚本化使用中最明显的阻塞项。
  • 配置并不总是生效。 设置在初始化时合并，但在运行时被 Browser Agent 忽略（#22267）；符号链接的代理文件完全不会被发现（#20079）。
  • 工作区卫生。 模型会在各个目录中散落临时编辑脚本（#23571），并且可能动用破坏性的 git 操作（#22672）——两者都会增加提交时的摩擦。
  • 交互式提示卡住。 像 create vite 这样的脚手架流程会阻塞在 TUI 提示上而无法继续（#22465）。
  • 平台特定故障——Wayland 浏览器支持以及 Windows/PowerShell 引号和进程检测持续产生一连串 bug。
GitHub Copilot CLI — github/copilot-cli

GitHub Copilot CLI — 社区摘要

日期： 2026-10-29 · 仓库： github/copilot-cli

1. 今日亮点

今日活动主要围绕 MCP 身份验证与企业代理故障（Entra 令牌缓存、OAuth 动态客户端注册、*.ghe.com 代理）展开，同时还有一批新的资源耗尽报告——包括一个长时间运行的并行代理会话中 37 GiB 的内存暴涨。三个长期存在的高影响 Issue 今日被 关闭（#4851 Azure MCP BrokenPipe、#4613 MCP schema 提前注入、#4710 失控的文件搜索线程），表明分诊吞吐持续稳定。与此同时，社区中点赞最高的条目仍然是 Linux 钥匙串（#2165，22 👍）以及长期存在的 403 模型列表 故障（#552，31 条评论）。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时内没有发布新版本。现场报告提到当前版本为 1.0.103 和 1.0.105。

3. 热门 Issue（10）

1. #552 — Failed to list models: 403 unauthorized（OPEN，31 条评论，4 👍）

仓库中评论数最多的单个 Issue。已启用 Copilot CLI 的组织仍然看到空模型列表，因为 CLI 在模型端点收到 403。影响 v0.0.355，并且显然在近一年后仍未解决——这是企业入驻过程中持续存在的权益/权限映射阻塞项。

2. #4802 — PRU 配额被耗尽，很可能与 Assisted Permissions 有关（OPEN，8 条评论）

一位 Copilot Pro（旧版基于请求的 PRU）用户报告称，启用 Assisted Permissions 与在一次事件中耗尽剩余的 234 个 PRU 相关。业务影响很大：一个权限功能似乎会成倍放大高级请求消耗。目前尚无点赞，但它是非认证类运营投诉中最热门的一条。

3. #4851 — Azure MCP 服务器发送 HTTP 请求失败 (CLOSED)（6 条评论，10 👍）

Rust 运行时在验证 Azure API Center MCP registry 时抛出 BrokenPipe——这是一个回归，导致原本可用的配置在一夜之间失效。关闭时获得社区强烈认可（10 👍）；这是一个积极信号，表明 MCP 传输健壮性正在被积极修复。

4. #2165 — Ubuntu 钥匙串支持已损坏（OPEN，5 条评论，22 👍）

本摘要中点赞最高的 Issue。两个 bug：围绕 secret-tool 的文档不正确，以及 Ubuntu 上的钥匙串访问损坏。Linux 用户实际上无法顺畅完成认证流程——点赞数反映了一个广泛但未被充分服务的平台群体。

5. #4017 — MCP OAuth：非第一方 HTTP 服务器从不启动延迟的运行时浏览器流程（OPEN，5 条评论，3 👍）

在 Desktop 应用中，远程 MCP 服务器（Atlassian、incident.io）会取消宿主令牌，然后静默地未能启动浏览器流程。结果：没有认证、没有错误、没有弹窗——最糟糕的故障模式。切换服务器开关也没有效果。根因分析得很漂亮。

6. #2109 — ACP：添加 ask_user / ask_question 扩展方法（OPEN，4 条评论，8 👍）

按点赞数计，这是今日最热门的 功能 请求。ACP 支持目前只暴露 session/request_permission；第三方 ACP 客户端无法接收澄清问题或返回结构化答案。填补这一空白将显著改善自定义客户端与 TUI 的功能对等性。

7. #4555 — ACP：session/prompt 无条件中止会话，杀死后台子代理（OPEN，3 条评论）

copilot --acp --stdio 在提示处理器的第一个动作中调用 session.abort()，取消所有后台子代理任务——交互式 TUI 并不表现出这种行为。这是一个正确性/对等性 bug，使 ACP 模式无法用于多代理编排。

8. #4710 — 失控的 copilot-file-search 线程在空闲时消耗 CPU 并无限占用磁盘 (CLOSED)（3 条评论）

使用 --yolo 时，一个空闲会话占满了一个 CPU 核心，并在 ~/.copilot/log 下写入无限制的诊断日志。报告环境为 1.0.83-3 / Ubuntu 24.04。对于在笔记本或 CI runner 上运行长时间会话的人来说，关闭该 Issue 是个好消息。

9. #4613 — 1.0.80+ 回归：MCP schema 被提前注入，启动 token 约 354K (CLOSED)（3 条评论）

被报告为高严重性：运行时不再延迟加载 MCP 工具 schema，即使对于简单提示，也会将完整的环境目录注入第一个模型请求。这直接转化为延迟和高级请求成本。关闭该 Issue 消除了 1.0.80+ 系列中的一个重大性能回归。

10. #5254 — 1.0.103 主进程达到 37.3 GiB、133M 次 malloc、10.7 GiB 碎片（OPEN，2 条评论）

在一台 32 GiB 的 Apple Silicon Mac 上，一个恢复运行、长时间运行的并行代理会话在约 6h19m 后超出物理内存，导致大量 swap 和间歇性故障。结合 #4710 和 #5205，这指向一个系统性的 长会话资源管理 缺口。

同样值得关注（今日刚提交）： #5289 copilot --cloud 在配置阶段因内部服务器错误而失败；#5288 /copy 现在输出 HTML 而不是 Markdown；#5284 过期的 MCP OAuth DCR 注册被永久复用（invalid_client）；#5286 sandbox 代理不会将令牌转发到 *.ghe.com。

4. 关键 PR 进展

过去 24 小时内没有 PR 更新（0 项）。上述三个关闭项（#4851、#4613、#4710）表明修复通过其他渠道落地。

5. 热门讨论

本时间窗口未提供讨论数据。

6. 功能请求趋势

从今日 Issue 中提炼：

  • ACP 协议完整性 — #2109 ask_user/ask_question、#4555 后台子代理保留。自定义 ACP 客户端是增长最快的集成面，但目前能力落后于 TUI。
  • 确定性权限控制 — #5275 请求在非交互模式下默认拒绝并配合显式允许列表，因为 --deny-tool 总是覆盖 --allow-tool。这与 #4802 的担忧相呼应：Assisted Permissions 在成本/行为方面不透明。
  • BYOK / 提供商可配置性 — #5287 要求为 providers.json 发布 JSON Schema；#5290 报告文档中记载的 --fusion-tier 参数缺失。用户希望对未文档化的配置面进行探查。
  • 企业与数据驻留正确性 — #5280（/login 错误标记 *.ghe.com）、#5286（sandbox 代理 + 用于 GHE 的 gh）、#552（组织权益 → 403）。企业标记和代理行为需要作为一等事项处理。
  • 输出格式控制 — #5288 请求 /copy 重新返回 Markdown，而不是 HTML。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. 身份验证是主要故障域。 Windows 上的 Entra 令牌缓存已损坏（#5236：缓存文件保持 0 字节 → 每个进程都重新提示），macOS 钥匙串 XARA 分区不匹配导致每次启动都提示（#4273），Ubuntu 钥匙串已损坏（#2165），Entra api:// 作用域被拒绝（#5061，已关闭），并且 MCP OAuth DCR 注册永不过期（#5284）。跨平台凭据持久化是最大的摩擦来源。
  2. MCP 会静默失败。 #4017 导致没有认证、没有错误、没有弹窗；#4916 将 base64 text/plain 资源 blob 作为空输出返回给模型；#4851 一夜之间失效。故障模式在很大程度上不可见，导致自我诊断困难。
  3. 长会话会泄漏资源。 37 GiB RSS 增长（#5254）、空闲搜索线程失控（#4710），以及上下文轮转因缺少 checkpoint.md 而崩溃（#5205），都影响了运行多小时或并行代理工作负载的用户。
  4. Windows 落后于其他平台。 CLI 运行时剪贴板复制会失效（#3981），PowerShell 环境变量不会被 shell runner 继承（#5281），并且沙箱预检在企业策略下会因 CreateProcessW 错误 2 而失败（#5285）。
  5. 配置语义会让用户感到意外。 includeCoAuthoredBy: false 不会被 task 子代理继承（#4576，5 👍），使用 GPT-5.6 Luna Max 时压缩会在 50% 触发（#4571，已关闭），启动 token 成本因 MCP schema 被提前注入而膨胀（#4613，已关闭）。静默不生效的配置比缺失功能更快侵蚀信任。
OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode 社区文摘 — 2026-10-29

今日亮点

OpenCode 发布了 v2.2.1，核心亮点是新的 /goal 原语，它可在 TUI 和 Desktop 中将会话转变为持续运行、由审查者验证的目标循环。此版本同时随附 process-daemon/@opencode/pty 升级至协议 7。与此同时，问题分诊量仍主要由 Zen 免费额度配额投诉占据（#59387 已膨胀至 98 条评论），此外还有一波针对较旧缺陷报告的 pending close 清理。

版本发布

v2.2.1

  • 持续朝着目标推进：在 TUI 或 Desktop 中使用 /goal <objective> 可让会话持续运行，直到审查者确认目标已达成。控制面包括 /goal pause、/goal resume 和 /goal clear。
  • PR：anomalyco/opencode#59437

process-daemon v0.3.2

  • opencode-pty 0.3.2（协议 7）由 packages/process-daemon 构建，并以 @opencode/pty@0.3.2 发布至 npm。影响终端/PTY 使用者；协议升级值得有意固定版本。

热点问题

  1. #59387 — Zen 免费额度主帖（98 条评论，👍9） — 免费额度故障的集中入口：“Free usage exceeded”、永远不会触发的重置计时器，以及 Desktop 版本拒绝订阅。评论数高反映的是每位用户未解决的配额状态，而不是某个可复现的单一缺陷。

  2. #18654 — 无法在 OpenCode Zen 中更改或删除邮箱（14 条评论，👍20） — 本组中反响最高的条目。在 GitHub 更改邮箱会创建重复的 Zen 身份，且没有面向用户的补救措施。虽被标记为 pending close，但 👍 数表明账户生命周期确实存在摩擦。

  3. #48743 — MCP 预启动/预热 + 重连路径（10 条评论） — 在装有 14 个以上本地 stdio MCP 服务器的 Windows Desktop 上，会话启动时由于并发冷启动，所有服务器都会被标记为 failed。服务器本身是健康的；问题出在监管进程。提供预热/重连接口将修复一整类配置场景。

  4. #48657 — Snapshot.capture() 卡住时会话始终无法排空（8 条评论） — git add --all --pathspec-from-file=- 在大型未跟踪且未被 gitignore 的目录树上挂起，阻塞 llm.stream()，并使执行声明被永久持有。这是没有超时、也没有用户可见诊断的硬挂起。

  5. #48497 — 持久记忆系统（/teach、/recall、/learn、/memory）（7 条评论） — 提议提供一等公民的长期记忆，而不是每个会话都重新推导上下文。已作为分诊关闭，但这一请求方向反复出现。

  6. #49042 — Agent 循环在零用户输入下运行 500+ 步（6 条评论） — 模型输出最终文本后仍失控地自动继续。没有步数上限，也没有防护。这与今天的 /goal 发布直接相关：持久循环需要持久的安全护栏。

  7. #24981 — 在 opencode 配置中显式配置代理（6 条评论，👍8） — 自 4 月以来仍未关闭。仅靠环境变量代理（HTTPS_PROXY 等）无法覆盖按提供商路由，也无法覆盖通过 GUI 启动的 Desktop 会话。

  8. #59817 — shell/<projectID> 上的 mkdir EEXIST 静默回退到主目录（3 条评论，reproduced） — 占用 project-ID 路径的文件导致每个请求都返回 500，并且 TUI 会悄悄在 $HOME 中启动会话。静默回退才是危险之处——它可能在错误目录中运行工具。

  9. #48542 — 压缩写入的 Anthropic 提示缓存从未被读取（3 条评论） — 7 天内 70 次压缩写入了 1,278,055 个缓存 token，读取次数为 0。缓存写入按高价计费，因此这是直接、可量化的支出浪费。

  10. #59916 — opencode run 中按 Ctrl-C 后 bash 工具命令仍在运行（3 条评论） — 在 bash 工具调用期间收到 SIGINT/SIGTERM 时，OpenCode 退出，但子进程继续执行；使用 --continue 时，模型会被告知它“被中断”，导致状态与现实不同步。在 CI 的 timeout 和编辑器集成下尤其糟糕。

同样值得关注： #59909（Termux 上粘贴会冻结，且随粘贴大小加剧）、#48740（Zen /v1/responses 在工具输出包含图片时返回 422——会让截图会话瘫痪）、#49034（Windows 上的 v2 等待后台服务超时）。

重点 PR 进展

  1. #60028 — feat(core)：Code Mode 谓词门控调度触发 — 调度可接受 if: { type: "code", code, allow }，在每次运行前求值，且不调用模型。该程序只能看到允许列表中的工具以及 state、now 和 runs，并返回 { wake, state, message? }。基于调度 PR #59401 构建——这是“昂贵 Agent 之前的廉价门控”模式。

  2. #60219 — fix(core)：在会话步骤中自动选择工具 — 使 OpenAI 兼容请求在普通步骤中发送 tool_choice: "auto"，修复了会拒绝省略该字段请求的 vLLM 网关。关闭 #60202。

  3. #60228 — chore(protocol)：重新生成 OpenAPI 文档 — Effect 4.0.6 升级（#59630）改变了生成的 schema，导致 check:generated 在 dev 上失败，并阻塞每个 PR 必需的 unit (linux) 检查。差异很小（三个整数字段上的 maximum: 9007199254740991），但影响范围很大——合并后可为所有人解除 CI 阻塞。

  4. #60208 — feat(session-ui)：将用户消息操作收进菜单 — 将每条消息的页脚折叠为 Rewind to here + 一个 More actions（…）菜单，菜单内含时间戳、Fork from here 和 Copy message。减少长时间线中的视觉噪音。

  5. #60209 — feat(merman)：渲染 Mermaid 类图 — classDiagram 围栏此前在 TUI 中渲染为原始代码。为 merman 增加类图渲染器（引用 #40508）。

  6. #60222 — fix(tui)：保留捕获的附件和源路径 — 保留 #59833 的保证：Agent 会收到粘贴图片和 PDF 的原始路径，同时仍发送捕获的内容。关闭 #60210。

  7. #60216 — fix(app)：停止在排队提示增长动画期间丢帧 — 移除提交键处理器中每帧时间线重设样式和强制布局，这些操作会在 M5 Pro 上导致丢帧。这是更广泛 UI 性能清理工作线的代表。

  8. #60125 — fix(core)：保留无路径的 MCP OAuth 资源 — 自定义提供商校验会丢弃诸如 https://example.com 这样的无路径资源。关闭 #58956，并解除对根域名签发方背后受 OAuth 保护的 MCP 服务器的阻塞。

  9. #60001 — feat(app)：重新设计目标胶囊 — 重新设计 goal 插件的输入区胶囊和弹出层（叠加在 #60000 上，该 PR 增加了 ComposerPill.icon）。这是 v2.2.1 /goal 发布的 UI 部分。

  10. #55765 — fix(app)：在非拉丁键盘布局上匹配快捷键 — 当字面绑定未命中时，Ctrl/Meta 快捷键会回退到按键的物理位置；精确的自定义绑定仍然优先。关闭 #55676——这是西里尔文/阿拉伯文/CJK 布局长期存在的可访问性缺口。

同样已合并/推进中： #56010（交互式 plugin add/remove CLI）、#57090（按比例更新 Code Mode 目录的部分内容）、#60212（TUI 中语法高亮的 shell 命令）、#60223（站点页脚中的实时 /status 链接）。

功能请求趋势

  • 持久记忆与可复用上下文 — /teach、/recall、/learn、/memory（#48497）是最清晰的表述，但同样的需求也以 AGENTS.md 变通方案和长生命周期会话中反复重新预热的形式出现。预计这会与 /goal 的会话生命周期工作汇合。
  • 网络/代理可配置性 — #24981 要求在 opencode config 中提供代理设置，而不是仅依赖环境变量。企业环境和 GUI 启动环境是主要驱动力。
  • Zen 的账户生命周期 — 邮箱更改/删除（#18654）以及重复身份清理。与计费相邻，且反复获得点赞。
  • MCP 生命周期管理 — 预热/预启动与重连（#48743），以及无路径 OAuth 资源保留（#60125）。诉求正从“支持 MCP”转向“监管 MCP”。
  • Desktop/TUI UI 缩放与密度 — 在大显示器上模型选择器宽度上限约为 284px（#48789）；标题栏中为推理摘要和展开的 shell/编辑部分提供快速切换（#48671）。
  • 为附加的 TUI/ACP 提供会话级模型/Agent 选择 — #48759，来自通过 ACP 驱动同一运行时的嵌入方。这是高级用户/嵌入场景的信号，而非大众需求。

开发者痛点

  • 免费额度配额状态是唯一最响亮的投诉。 #59387（98 条评论）以及 #59911 和 #60224 都描述了同一种故障形态：出现一条带有重置时间戳的限额消息，但该时间戳永远不会到来。用户无法自行诊断，因此每个实例都会变成一个支持讨论串。
  • 没有超时的挂起。 #48657（在巨大的未跟踪目录树上执行 git add）和 #59909（Termux 粘贴，开销随输入大小增长）都是 O(n) 或更差的停顿，没有进度信号，也无法取消。TUI 没有“已经卡住”的提示手段。
  • 失控的 Agent 循环。 #49042 报告了 500+ 次自动继续步骤，既无用户输入也无防护。随着 /goal 现已发布，显式的步骤/预算上限显然是后续工作。
  • 缓存经济性不可见且不正确。 #48542（1.28M 个缓存写入 token，0 次读取）和 #48624（glm-5.3-flash 显示零缓存读取，而 deepseek-v4.1-flash 正常缓存）都意味着用户为从未受益的缓存付费——却没有暴露的指标来察觉这一点。
  • 信号处理与孤儿子进程。 #59916 在退出后仍让 bash 命令继续运行，并且记录一个错误的“已中断”状态，导致恢复后与现实偏离。这种模式对 CI 和编辑器集成很不友好。
  • 改变执行上下文的静默回退。 #59817 在 mkdir 返回 EEXIST 时悄悄将会话迁移到 $HOME——改变工具运行位置的错误应当大声失败。
  • 配置严格性不对称。 #49027 将未知的 Agent 配置字段原样转发到上游提供商请求中，产生 invalid_request_error；#48555 在建议了正确名称之后，仍因模型名称大小写混合而拒绝子 Agent。配置校验在两个方向上都不一致——对外过于宽松，对内过于脆弱。
  • Windows Desktop 后台服务可靠性。 #49034（托管服务启动超时）、#48715（sidecar 在内存压力下以 0xC0000409 崩溃）和 #48743（MCP 冷启动失败）构成一个一致的 Windows 稳定性问题簇。

本周期未提供 Discussion 数据，因此省略该部分。

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi 社区文摘 — 2026-10-29

今日亮点

过去 24 小时没有新版本发布；活动主要集中在一个长期存在的 Windows 可用性讨论帖（#7547，目前 91 条评论）以及一组全屏/TUI 渲染性能报告上。修复方面，一批已关闭的 PR 处理了会话存储语义、终端控制序列处理、pi.exec 缓冲和环境守护进程终止清理，而 Bedrock Mantle 路由和 Anthropic 服务端消息线程仍在审查中。

发布

过去 24 小时内无发布。

热门 Issue

  1. #7547 — [Windows] 你如何在 Windows 上使用 Pi？遇到了哪些问题？（91 条评论，👍2）
    这是 Windows 支持的集中汇总帖。其动机具有明确的战略性：受支持的运行路径太多，导致不清楚应该修 bug、改进文档，还是交给扩展。它是数据集中互动量最高的 issue，也是判断 Windows 投入方向的最佳信号。

  2. #9549 — 大型会话记录每帧重新渲染；调整尺寸会重新输出整个会话记录（17 条评论，👍1）
    在具有 2 个逻辑核心的 Windows Terminal 上，大型会话记录会占满一个核心。该问题附带 agent 辅助测量结果，并通过 pi -ne 验证，因此可操作性异常强。它指向全屏渲染循环架构，而非一次性 bug。

  3. #7739 — 设定启动时间预算，以对标 jcode 的延迟和内存占用（12 条评论）
    提议基于基准测试制定一个具体预算，对标 jcode（10 次交互式 PTY 启动，Linux）。这表明社区希望将启动延迟视为可跟踪、可防回归的指标，而不是临时关注的问题。

  4. #9656 — 在 Windows + Zellij 的全屏模式下，鼠标滚轮滚动的是提示历史而非会话记录（11 条评论，👍5）
    这是此处开放 bug 中点赞数最高的。复现路径很窄（Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi；不使用复用器时正常，在 Linux+tmux 上正常），这强烈表明问题出在复用器/终端能力检测上。

  5. #9884 — 配置的默认模型有时在启动时被回退模型替换（7 条评论）
    在 20 次启动中复现 4 次：来自运行时发现扩展目录的 defaultProvider/defaultModel 被静默替换为内置的 deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro。启动状态不确定对固定模型的团队而言是信任问题。

  6. #10954 — OpenCode Go Claude（anthropic-messages）：工具列表变更后重放 thinking block 时出现 400（6 条评论）
    与 #10324 属于同一类故障，但发生在不同的传输通道上，且 block_binding 仅在 supportsMidConvoEffort 时发送。对于任何通过第三方中继路由 Anthropic 兼容流量的人都很重要；该问题由 AI 披露并经实验验证。

  7. #10386 — Durable：托管编码代理扩展（AgentSession 支持的运行时或 hook 对等能力）（6 条评论，👍1）
    请求提供由 AgentSession 支持的运行时，或 ExtensionAPI hook 对等能力，以便 Durable 能作为一等扩展运行。这代表了对与核心能力匹配的扩展接口的更广泛诉求。

  8. #10616 — 扩展 pi.exec 在 Windows 上执行 .cmd 命令失败（npm、npx、pnpm）（5 条评论）
    pi.exec("npm", ["--version"]) 返回退出码 1 且 stdout 为空，而 bash 工具执行成功。这是一个清晰、独立的 Windows 扩展 API 缺陷，对扩展生态有明显影响。

  9. #10770 — .pi/agent/sessions 的默认权限应为 0700（5 条评论，inprogress）
    新建的会话目录可被同组/所有用户读取。已标记为进行中；这是一个直截了当的隐私加固请求，对共享机器和 CI runner 很重要。

  10. #11567 — 长会话中打字变慢：getSessionName() 在每次渲染时扫描每个条目（2 条评论，今日提交）
    在约 40 万个条目时，按键到渲染的 p50 为 21 ms，而空状态下为 1.5 ms；性能分析将 94% 的繁忙 CPU 归因于每次渲染时由页脚调用的 SessionManager.getSessionName()。这是一个新提交、剖析充分且修复路径明确的回归问题。

同样值得关注： #11529（MCP 服务器重连时，来自 Map 的工具排序会破坏提示缓存）和 #11527（每个请求新建 BedrockRuntimeClient，强制进行 SSO 凭据往返）。

关键 PR 进展

  1. #11565 — fix(tui)：在常规模式下停止写入 OSC 133 提示符标记（已关闭）
    常规 TUI 模式会发出 OSC 133 A/B/C 标记；显示 OSC 7501 状态的终端（Rex、iTerm2 3.7.5+）将 133;A 解释为新的 shell 提示符，并丢弃工作指示器。解决 #11519。

  2. #11561 — fix(coding-agent)：将会话目录中的会话视为默认存储（已关闭）
    当会话的 cwd 与其文件夹名不一致时，usesDefaultSessionDir() 会返回 false，因此 /resume 会静默地只列出一部分会话。修复了一个令人困惑的会话发现 bug。

  3. #11562 — fix(coding-agent)：在 cwd 的默认目录中启动新会话（开放）
    作为 #11561 的配套改动：/new、/fork 和 /clone 目前会继承已打开文件的文件夹，并将其视为自定义 --session-dir。使新会话存储与实际工作目录保持一致。

  4. #11556 — fix(coding-agent)：让 SDK 流为摘要解析认证（已关闭）
    来自 createAgentSession 的会话将已解析的访问令牌作为 options.apiKey 传给压缩/分支/bug 报告摘要，绕过了 modelRuntime.streamSimple 的认证解析。对使用 OAuth 的 SDK 嵌入方很重要。

  5. #11546 — fix(coding-agent)：将 pi.exec 输出上限设为 256 MiB（已关闭，关闭 #11360）
    新增 ExecOptions.maxBuffer，默认取 256 MiB 与运行时字符串限制中的较小值；超限命令会被终止，并返回 truncated: true 和非零退出码。防止输出过多的子进程导致内存失控。

  6. #11545 — Anthropic 消息线程（开放）
    使用 Anthropic 的服务端消息线程 beta，在会话 ID 和缓存启用时只发送新消息，同时仍构建完整请求用于比较。对于长会话，可能显著降低 token/成本。

  7. #11544 — fix(env)：守护进程被终止时杀掉其命令（已关闭）
    Connection.close() 在守护进程来得及运行 kill_all 之前发送了 SIGTERM，导致命令继续运行。这是本地 Unix 守护进程路径的干净清理修复。

  8. #11543 / #11541 — fix(coding-agent)：在 stripAnsi 中剥离私有参数 CSI 序列（已关闭）
    stripAnsi 将 <、=、> 视为 CSI 终止字节，因此像 ESC[<35;59;1M 这样的鼠标报告会把参数以字面文本形式泄漏到工具输出中。合并了两个实现；属于底层问题，但会影响会话记录的整洁性。

  9. #11348 — fix(tui,coding-agent)：在所有滚动列表中处理选择翻页键（已关闭，修复 #7629）
    对 #7680 进行 rebase 并缩小范围：在选择组件、自动补全和代理选择器中遵循 tui.select.pageUp/pageDown，并通过显式全屏捕获标志让活动选择优先于会话记录滚动。

  10. #11372 — fix(ai)：将 Converse 不提供的 Bedrock 模型路由到 Bedrock Mantle（开放）
    针对 Bedrock API key 处理 #5363：列出的 16 个模型（GPT-5.4–GPT-6.1、gpt-oss、Grok 4.3/4.6、Gemma 4）仅在 Mantle 上可用，Mantle 是 OpenAI 兼容端点，而目前它们会因无效的 Converse 模型标识符而失败。堆叠的后续 PR #8572/#8573 增加了 SigV4/IAM 认证和 Anthropic Messages 路由。

热门讨论

展示与分享

  • #11503 — pi-rs：无头核心的 Rust 移植——逐原子验证行为对等（+ 一项 DeepSeek API 兼容性发现）（1 条评论，👍1）
    社区对 pi 0.74.2 无头核心的 Rust 重实现：agent 循环、七个内置工具、会话 JSONL、CLI 界面和系统提示，采用 MIT 许可证，并在设计上致谢 pi。包含一项 DeepSeek API 兼容性发现。它既是对等性测试的产物，也表明对非 Node 运行时的需求。

功能请求趋势

  • 将 Windows 作为一等平台。 最集中的一组：使用路径整合（#7547）、.cmd/npx 执行（#10616）、感知复用器的滚动（#9656），以及低核心数 Windows 终端上的渲染开销（#9549）。
  • 将性能作为有预算、可度量的属性。 启动延迟对标 jcode（#7739）、每帧会话记录重新渲染（#9549），以及渲染路径上的 O(entries) 工作（#11567），都把性能视为需要防范的回归，而不仅仅是要优化的对象。
  • 更深入的扩展 API。 hook 对等能力 / 由 AgentSession 支持的运行时（#10386）、用于门控和截断的可返回 tool_result 结果（#11553）、命名空间作用域的 tool_search（+docs read_page，#11558）、延迟运行时重载（#7948），以及按工具控制 MCP 暴露的开关（#11526）。
  • 提供商与目录正确性。 Bedrock Claude 的提示缓存元数据（#11528）、Converse 拒绝的模型的 Mantle 路由（#11372），以及可配置的 OAuth/Copilot 超时（#11549）。
  • 隐私与凭据卫生。 0700 会话目录（#10770），以及将 deviceId 移出可共享的全局设置（#10187）。
  • 会话存储语义。 默认目录解析和 /resume 可见性（#11561、#11562）——小修复，却带来不成比例的 UX 影响。

开发者痛点

  • Windows 支持分散在多条运行路径上。 这个有 91 条评论的汇总帖明确道出了根本挫败感：用户无法判断哪种 Windows 配置是“官方认可”的，扩展作者则会遇到平台特定的损坏（pi.exec 执行 .cmd、Zellij 复用、终端状态标记）。
  • 长会话会降低交互性。 两份独立报告（#9549、#11567）将变慢归因于每次渲染都执行的工作——完整会话记录重新发送和每次渲染扫描会话名。在 40 万个条目时，21 ms 对 1.5 ms 的按键延迟是一个具体上限。
  • 提示缓存很容易被意外失效。 Map 中的工具插入顺序（#11529）和 Bedrock 上缺失的 promptCache 元数据（#11528）会静默地将缓存轮次变为全价轮次。
  • 启动配置不确定。 配置的默认模型在 20% 的启动中被回退模型替换（#9884），削弱了团队的可复现性。
  • 提供商适配器会暴露上游怪癖。 通过中继重放 thinking block（#10954）、每个请求构建 Bedrock 客户端从而强制 SSO 往返（#11527）、默认输出预算过大触发 HTTP 402（#11517），以及固定的 15s/5s OAuth 超时（#11549）。
  • 会话存储令人意外。 会话存放在以原始 cwd 命名的文件夹中，导致 /resume 隐藏部分会话，/new 继承错误目录（#11561、#11562）。
  • 子进程与守护进程生命周期的边界情况。 无界的 pi.exec 输出（#11360 → #11546）、辅助线程耗尽时 panic（#11433），以及守护进程关闭时命令成为孤儿（#11544），都是“一直能用，直到不能用”的故障模式。
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code 社区摘要 — 2026-10-29

1. 今日亮点

v0.26.3 发布线已覆盖 CLI、Desktop 和 TypeScript SDK。生成的 UI 卡片现在能在导航和分屏视图之间保留输入与状态，并且仅在支持 MCP Apps 的客户端上渲染实时结果。与此同时，Issue 跟踪器主要被 CI 和发布基础设施相关工作占据：一个长期存在的 Managed Agent 门禁失败已累积 79 条评论，而新报告的 P1 配置回归（contextWindowSize 被静默移除）是今日对用户影响最大的新 bug。

2. 发布

  • v0.26.3 — 主要稳定版。源 feed 中的发布说明仅为占位符（qwen-release-notes:v1），因此实质性变更可通过下方随附的 Desktop 和 nightly 条目查看。
  • desktop-v0.26.3 — 新增托管会话权限规则和 Auto approval（#15448），并加固 CLI 中的 serve token 处理。

  • 重点变更： 生成的 UI 卡片在导航和分屏视图之间保留输入和状态，在初次计算后显示实时视图，并且仅对能够渲染 MCP Apps 的客户端开放（#15611、#15787）。

3. 热门 Issue

  1. #15855 — contextWindowSize 被自动移除 [P1, bug, configuration, need-information] · 3 条评论 · 今日新增。使用本地 OpenAI 兼容后端（Ollama，128k 窗口）的用户报告称，其配置的上下文限制被从设置中剥离，这可能导致意外截断或上下文溢出。本时间窗口内最高严重级别的新用户可见 bug。
  2. #14724 — 主 CI 失败：Managed Agent 门禁，未识别到测试 [bug, autofix/skip] · 79 条评论 · 自 2026-10-19 起开放。仓库中讨论最热烈的单一线程；机器人不断追加 commit 标记，却始终无法收敛到具体的测试归因，而这正是跟踪器本应防止的失败模式。
  3. #13078 — 每日依赖 CVE 审计失败 [needs-triage, ci-cd] · 35 条评论 · 一个持续一个月的反复失败。无论原因是真实的高危安全公告，还是 npm audit 端点不稳定，该信号已连续 30 天不可用，构成供应链风险。
  4. #15861 — Web Shell 宿主目录选择器冒烟测试确定性超时 [P1, testing, ready-for-agent] · 2 条评论 · 今日新开。与 PR 无关的失败意味着每位贡献者都要多付出一轮重新归因的成本；报告者明确将其称为对无关 PR 的额外负担。
  5. #15052 — 当待处理运行被替换时，保留独立的 main E2E 验证 [P2, ci-cd, ready-for-human] · 14 条评论 · 即使设置 cancel-in-progress: false，按 ref 作用域的并发也可能取消较早的待处理运行，因此中间的 main SHA 会失去独立验证。这对任何依赖逐 commit 绿色状态的人都很重要。

5. 热门讨论

源 feed 未提供讨论数据，因此本节省略。

6. 功能请求趋势

  • Web Shell / Desktop 易用性是主导产品主题。 Session Overview 和 Split View 的键盘快捷键（#13175，已关闭）、已归档行上的内联 Export/Restore（#15866）、侧边栏分类标题对齐（#15867）、宿主提供的目录选择器（#15186，已关闭），以及 macOS 守护进程 PATH 扩展（#12690，已关闭），都指向打磨外壳，而非增加核心能力。
  • 会话管理正确性。 无工作区会话在 Session Overview 中缺失（#11878，已关闭）以及磁盘恢复后分支操作消失（#13782，已关闭）均已解决；拆分、归档和恢复会话仍是活跃的摩擦点。
  • 提供商/模型灵活性。 在 OpenAI 兼容端点上动态发现和切换模型（#1206）仍是最明确未满足的诉求，今日本地 Ollama 用户的 contextWindowSize 回归（#15855）进一步强化了这一点。
  • IDE 与远程开发覆盖。 VS Code companion 仍需覆盖转发端口宿主门禁、IPv6 CSP 以及 Remote-SSH/WSL 运行（#12059）。
  • Skills 生命周期成熟度。 来自用户作用域 Skill 激活 PR（#15622）的后续工作表明，该功能正在交付，但仍在积累契约与生命周期改进。
  • 本地化。 浏览器区域设置回退（所有非 zh-CN 都折叠为 en）已在 Goal 卡片中提出（#13391，已关闭）——i18n 范围仍只有两个区域设置。

7. 开发者痛点

  • CI 噪声正在挤占真实信号。 机器人提交的 “no test identified” Issue（#14724 有 79 条评论，#15173 有 19 条，另有若干逐 commit 的 Managed Agent 门禁报告）产生了大量评论，却无法收敛到归因；而“变绿即关闭”的报告仍需手动驳回。
  • 确定性的、与 PR 无关的测试失败会阻塞所有人。 #15861 使 Web Shell 冒烟测试通道在无关 PR 上失败，迫使每次变更都要重新归因。
  • 发布流水线延迟与容量。 发布后扇出仍在 GitHub 托管 runner 上等待 37–50 分钟（#15465），而专用发布主机仍未置备（#15461）。
  • 逐 SHA 验证可能被静默丢失。 main E2E 上的并发替换意味着中间 commit 可能永远得不到独立结论（#15052）。
  • macOS runner 成本压力。 反复提出的将 Darwin 验证移至夜间的提议（#15783）反映了贡献者在 PR 周转中感受到的队列/成本权衡。
  • 安全审计已亮红灯一个月。 每日依赖 CVE 审计（#13078）已产生 35 条评论却未解决，使团队无法确定是否仍有真实的安全公告未处理。
  • 配置并不总是可信。 静默丢弃设置既以修复形式出现（fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped，#15794），也作为新的 P1 报告出现（#15855）——用户希望 CLI 暴露而不是吞掉它无法应用的配置。
  • 运行时环境脆弱性。 历史上因 RHEL 10 缺少 full-ICU Intl.Segmenter 导致的崩溃（#11747，已关闭）凸显了一类反复出现的宿主运行时不兼容问题，且缺乏可操作的诊断信息。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-10-29

Generated: 2026-10-29 14:08 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool AI CLI Comparison Report — 2026-10-29

All figures below are digest-reported observations, not full-repo totals. “N/A” means no count was provided in the digest, not that the channel is inactive. No tool in this set was identified as having Issues/PRs disabled upstream.

1. Ecosystem Overview

AI CLI tools are converging on agentic development workspaces: MCP integration, session persistence, cost/quota visibility, long-running goals, and approval-based safety are now core competitive surfaces. Release cadence is uneven — OpenCode and Qwen Code shipped releases, Codex shipped Rust alphas, while Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, and Pi shipped nothing in the last 24 hours — but issue traffic remains high across all tools. The most severe recurring risks are silent data/config loss, auth and MCP credential lifecycle failures, prompt-cache/token waste, and Windows/desktop parity gaps. Competition is shifting from raw model access toward operational reliability, enterprise governance, and cross-platform consistency.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues / issue activity PRs Discussions Release status
Claude Code 50 issues updated; top thread #27302 has 289 comments / 435 👍 2 updated N/A No release
OpenAI Codex Total not reported; 10 hot issues highlighted; #36040 has 99 comments 10 key PRs highlighted 10 items: 2 Ideas, 3 Q&A, 5 Show-and-tell 2 Rust alphas: 0.166.0-alpha.6, alpha.5.1
Gemini CLI 30 top issues updated in area/agent 10 key PRs highlighted N/A No release
GitHub Copilot CLI 10 hot issues highlighted; #552 has 31 comments 0 updated N/A No release
OpenCode 10 hot issues highlighted; #59387 has 98 comments 10 key PRs highlighted, plus 4 additional noted N/A v2.2.1; @opencode/pty@0.3.2
Pi 10 hot issues highlighted; #7547 has 91 comments 10 key PRs highlighted 1 discussion No release
Qwen Code 10 hot issues highlighted; #14724 has 79 comments 10 key PRs highlighted N/A v0.26.3, desktop, nightly, TypeScript SDK

3. Shared Feature Directions

  • Cost, quota, and prompt-cache transparency
    Claude Code wants persistent usage indicators and fewer avoidable cache writes (#80261, #105564). Codex users want predictable monthly resets (#57967). Copilot CLI reports PRU burn and eager MCP schema injection inflating startup tokens (#4802, #4613). OpenCode has 1.28M cache-write tokens with zero reads (#48542) and a 98-comment free-tier quota thread (#59387). Pi reports prompt-cache invalidation from tool ordering (#11529) and missing Bedrock cache metadata (#11528). Gemini CLI is targeting token-frugal context management (#19561).
    Shared need: visible spend, cache-hit/miss metrics, bounded image/context retention, and controls that prevent invisible token waste.

  • Session identity, memory, and lifecycle control
    Claude Code needs path-independent project identity and safer retention (#101522, #41458, #74682). Codex is adding message editing/undo and chat navigation (#11086, #2379, #8582). Gemini CLI is hardening session-history preservation and cancellation semantics (#30019, #30017). OpenCode is exploring persistent memory (/teach, /recall, /memory) and now ships /goal. Pi is fixing default session-directory and /resume semantics (#11561, #11562). Qwen Code is polishing session overview, archive, export, and restore flows.
    Shared need: durable, portable sessions; explicit retention; cross-machine project identity; predictable resume/archive behavior.

  • MCP supervision and auth lifecycle
    Claude Code has auth/MCP reliability issues around 401 helper calls and worktree-scoped MCP server reaping (#105408, #105857). Copilot CLI has MCP OAuth DCR expiry, silent auth failures, and GHE proxy gaps (#4017, #5284, #5286). OpenCode needs MCP pre-spawn/warm-up and reconnect (#48743). Codex is adding per-chat leases for shared MCP connections (#57978). Pi sees MCP reconnects invalidating prompt cache through tool-order changes (#11529).
    Shared need: MCP is moving from “support it” to “supervise it” — warm-up, reconnect, credential rotation, lease isolation, and enterprise proxy compatibility.

  • Enforceable safety and permission controls
    Codex users report prompt-level prohibitions being violated and want enforceable file restrictions (#57827); Codex PRs add Guardian review and fresh human approval checkpoints. Gemini CLI has maintainer-authored asks to discourage destructive git operations and improve sandboxing (#22672, #19873). Copilot CLI requests default-deny with explicit allowlists in non-interactive mode (#5275). OpenCode has a silent $HOME fallback when project directories fail (#59817). Pi wants private 0700 session directories (#10770).
    Shared need: policy-level sandboxing, file-scope enforcement, approval checkpoints, and loud failure instead of silent fallback.

  • Platform and observability parity
    Claude Code lacks OpenTelemetry on the web surface and has Windows Remote Control regressions (#32364, #105658). Codex has recurring Windows desktop regressions (#50704 and related). Gemini CLI has Wayland and Windows/PowerShell issues. Copilot CLI has Windows clipboard, PowerShell env inheritance, and sandbox preflight failures. OpenCode has a Windows background-service cluster. Pi’s 91-comment Windows thread is the clearest platform-fragmentation signal. Qwen Code has CI/Web Shell and Remote-SSH coverage gaps.
    Shared need: first-class Windows/Wayland support, desktop/web parity, and telemetry that works across CLI, web, and IDE surfaces.

  • Long-running agent control and observability
    OpenCode shipped /goal but also has a 500+ step runaway loop report (#49042). Gemini CLI’s top issue is subagent MAX_TURNS reported as success (#22323), plus generalist-agent hangs (#21409). Codex is adding Guardian review and approval checkpoints. Claude Code has routine-session sprawl and hanging cloud routines.
    Shared need: step/budget ceilings, cancellation that actually stops child processes, subagent trajectory visibility, and reviewer-verified completion rather than optimistic status reporting.

4. Differentiation Analysis

  • Claude Code targets enterprise and high-volume power users. Its strongest signal is identity, MCP/auth reliability, OTel parity, Connector multi-account support, and cost control. It has the heaviest issue engagement in this set but low PR throughput today, suggesting a mature product with a large reliability backlog.

  • OpenAI Codex spans CLI, desktop, cloud, and mobile remote control. Its technical direction includes Rust alpha builds, Guardian review/approval infrastructure, MCP connection leases, and Code Mode output truncation. It is especially focused on policy enforcement and desktop/remote workflows, but image-heavy context and Windows desktop regressions are major friction points.

  • Gemini CLI is the most explicitly subagent- and orchestration-centric. It is investing in AST-aware codebase tooling, token-frugal context management, sandboxing, and subagent observability. Its weakness is terminal-state correctness: false success reporting, indefinite hangs, and non-interactive -p mode reliability directly threaten CI/scripting use.

  • GitHub Copilot CLI targets GitHub enterprise workflows. Differentiation is ACP protocol completeness, MCP auth, GHE/proxy behavior, permission semantics, and BYOK/config introspection. It has strong enterprise pain around auth persistence — Entra, macOS keychain, Ubuntu keychain, and MCP OAuth — and zero PR updates today, with fixes landing through other channels.

  • OpenCode is the fastest-shipping open-source-style option in this set. v2.2.1 adds persistent /goal loops, while PRs add Code Mode predicate gates, Mermaid rendering, message-action menus, and protocol/CI fixes. Its adoption friction is Zen free-tier quota state, cache economics, and Windows background-service reliability.

  • Pi is the most terminal/extension-focused tool. Its community emphasizes Windows usability, fullscreen TUI performance, extension API parity, session-storage semantics, and provider routing for Bedrock/Anthropic-compatible traffic. A community Rust port (pi-rs) signals demand for a non-Node runtime and behavioral parity testing.

  • Qwen Code targets Qwen and local/OpenAI-compatible backends, with CLI, Desktop, Web Shell, and TypeScript SDK surfaces. It is shipping releases and managed-session permissions, but its issue tracker is dominated by CI attribution noise, release-host capacity, and a new P1 config regression where contextWindowSize is silently removed.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Highest visible engagement: Claude Code has the largest single thread (#27302, 289 comments) and 50 updated issues. Codex has the highest-comment new-regression signal (#36040, 99 comments). OpenCode’s quota thread (#59387, 98 comments), Pi’s Windows thread (#7547, 91 comments), and Qwen’s CI gate thread (#14724, 79 comments) are the loudest per-project signals.

PR throughput: Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen Code each highlighted roughly 10 key PRs. Claude Code had 2 updated PRs; Copilot CLI had 0. This does not mean Claude/Copilot are inactive — both show heavy triage and issue activity — but their visible fix throughput is lower in this window.

Rapid iteration: OpenCode and Qwen Code are shipping releases while actively changing UX and infrastructure. Codex is iterating through Rust alphas and safety/review PRs. Gemini CLI is in a substantial fix wave around session history, cancellation, shell security, and tool-call correctness. Pi is landing many focused maintenance fixes but had no release.

Maturity profile: Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot CLI have enterprise-scale adoption but still show serious auth, identity, proxy, and platform-parity debt. OpenCode and Qwen Code are iterating quickly but show quota, CI, and release-infrastructure maturity gaps. Pi is community-driven and maintenance-heavy, with platform fragmentation as its main ceiling. Gemini CLI’s agent architecture is ambitious, but subagent reliability and non-interactive mode are not yet stable enough for conservative CI adoption.

6. Trend Signals

  • Agent loops are becoming first-class, and so are their safety rails. OpenCode’s /goal launch alongside a 500+ step runaway report shows the pattern: persistent objectives require budget ceilings, pause/resume, reviewer verification, and cancellation guarantees. Gemini’s false GOAL/success reports and Codex’s Guardian approval work point the same direction.

  • Context is now a cost, correctness, and reliability surface. Image retention, auto-compaction, prompt-cache invalidation, startup schema injection, and session-start context rewrites are all recurring cost leaks. Developers should expect cache metrics, context-budget controls, image pruning, and compaction observability from serious tools.

  • MCP has shifted from integration feature to operational burden. The next competitive differentiator is MCP lifecycle management: warm-up, reconnect, OAuth/DCR expiry, token rotation, per-chat leases, and enterprise proxy support. Silent MCP failures are especially damaging because users cannot self-diagnose them.

  • Identity and session portability are enterprise blockers. Multi-account Connectors, path-independent project identity, cross-machine memory, /resume visibility, and retention guarantees are recurring asks. Tools that key sessions to filesystem paths or local keychains will struggle in containerized, multi-worktree, and multi-machine workflows.

  • Safety must be enforceable, not prompt-level. Across Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, and Pi, users are asking for sandboxing, default-deny permissions, file-scope restrictions, approval checkpoints, and loud failures. Prompt instructions alone are no longer trusted as guardrails.

  • Platform parity is a adoption gate. Windows, Wayland, desktop background services, terminal rendering, and enterprise auth/proxy behavior generate disproportionate pain. Teams evaluating AI CLIs should include Windows and enterprise-proxy test matrices, not just macOS/Linux happy paths.

  • Provider and local-model flexibility matters. Qwen Code’s local Ollama contextWindowSize regression, Pi’s Bedrock/Mantle and Anthropic routing work, Copilot CLI’s BYOK/config requests, and OpenCode’s proxy configuration demand all show that users want model/provider choice without hidden config semantics.

Reference value for developers: prioritize observable, cancellable agent loops; measurable context and cache economics; durable session identity; managed MCP lifecycle; enforceable permission policy; and cross-platform/enterprise-auth testing. These are now stronger predictors of production readiness than feature-count comparisons alone.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report

Source: github.com/anthropics/skills · Data as of 2026-10-29

Data caveat: the PR export shows Comments: undefined and 👍: 0 for all 20 PRs, so ranking below uses observable proxies — cross-referenced issues, revision/update recency, and the centrality of the skill being touched. All 20 PRs in the export are OPEN; no merges are recorded in this snapshot.

1. Top Skills Ranking (most-discussed PRs)

1. PR #1298 — skill-creator: isolate trigger evals, fix Windows & runtime failures Author: MartinCajiao · Created 2026-06-10 · Updated 2026-09-16 · OPEN Touches the meta-skill that generates and evaluates every other Skill. Fixes false trigger-eval misses caused by competing per-worker probes, select() on subprocess pipes failing on Windows, and unrelated tools aborting scans — critically, runtime failures currently register as "non-triggers," which silently passes negative examples and corrupts optimization. This is the direct counterpart to Issue #556 (0% trigger rate), making it the highest-leverage PR in the queue. Status: open, long-running (~3 months), still revised.

2. PR #1742 — mcp-builder: support mcp>=2 streamable_http_client + custom headers Author: Kuldeeep18 · Created 2026-09-08 · Updated 2026-10-08 · OPEN In mcp>=2.0.0, streamablehttp_client was renamed to streamable_http_client, and custom headers moved to create_mcp_http_client / http_client instead of a direct kwarg. Closes #1668. A hard breakage for anyone scaffolding MCP servers on current SDKs — this is ecosystem-compatibility maintenance, not a cosmetic fix. Status: open, actively revised.

3. PR #1980 — webapp-testing: remove shell=True from with_server.py Author: Pcmhacker-piro · Created 2026-10-06 · Updated 2026-10-25 · OPEN Removes subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True) used to support cd <dir> && <command> chains, closing a command-injection vector (CWE-78) reachable from unsanitized agent/user command strings. The most recently updated PR in the set and part of a clear security-hardening wave (see Issues #492, #1394). Status: open, recent activity.

4. PR #1997 — skill-creator: parse YAML frontmatter scalars correctly Author: BichengWang · Created 2026-10-10 · Updated 2026-10-19 · OPEN parse_skill_md manually strips quotes and joins continuation lines, so eval and description-optimization commands receive metadata that diverges from the actual SKILL.md — e.g. "review my draft." loses its closing quote and escapes. Silent metadata drift degrades description optimization. Status: open, recent.

5. PR #1681 — skill-creator: direct execution of package_skill.py Author: Kuldeeep18 · Created 2026-08-27 · Updated 2026-10-24 · OPEN python skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py <path> fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts.quick_validate'; docstrings and CLI help also carry stale paths. Blocks the standalone packaging workflow that most third-party Skill authors use. Status: open, actively revised.

6. PR #525 — Add pyxel skill for retro game development Author: kitao · Created 2026-03-05 · Updated 2026-10-23 · OPEN Guides creation, debugging, and verification of Python retro games: headless input-driven runs, direct frame inspection, task-specific state checks, plus references on Pyxel behavior and presentation. Authored by Pyxel's own maintainer. The longest-lived and still-updated new-Skill PR in the set. Status: open, ~8 months old, still maintained.

7. PR #1245 — Add notion-spec-to-implementation + quantitative-resume-auditor Author: mrdesouzaphd-cmyk · Created 2026-06-02 · Updated 2026-10-15 · OPEN Bundles two Skills: one decomposes Notion product/tech specs into implementation tasks with acceptance criteria and progress tracking; the other audits resumes against quantitative criteria. Represents the "spec → executable task graph" workflow-automation direction. Status: open, recently updated.

8. PR #1975 / #1976 / #1977 — correctness trio Author: gerardrecinto · Created 2026-10-06 · Updated 2026-10-18–10-27 · OPEN Three small, well-scoped fixes landing together: pptx rejects --cols < 1 at argparse instead of after a LibreOffice render (fixes #1809); webapp-testing reports textarea/select tags correctly instead of as text (fixes #1891); algorithmic-art's wrapAround() now actually wraps negatives via modulo (fixes #1897). Signals a contributor doing disciplined issue-triage cleanup. Status: all open.

Also notable: #1792 (docx: report LibreOffice timeout as an error and verify output), #1734 (detect orphaned docx comments), #538 (case-sensitive file references in pdf/SKILL.md — an 8-month-old one-line-class fix), #514 (document-typography: orphan/widow control, numbering alignment).

Pattern: the top of this ranking is dominated by fixes to bundled Skills — 4 of the top 5 touch skill-creator, mcp-builder, or webapp-testing — not by net-new Skill submissions.

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

① Trust boundary & namespace security — the single loudest thread Issue #492 (46 comments, 3 👍) is by far the most-discussed item in the entire dataset: community Skills distributed under the anthropic/ namespace impersonate official Anthropic Skills, so users grant elevated permissions to code they believe is first-party. Related hardening: #1394 (display-path XSS in the skill-creator eval-viewer via non-attribute-safe escapeHtml).

② Evaluation & triggering reliability Issue #556 (13 comments, 7 👍): run_eval.py yields a 0% trigger rate across all queries — no query ever invokes the Skill/Read tool. #1390: mcp-builder/evaluation.py fabricates a tool error for every call and scores 0/N invisibly. Demand: make the measurement layer truthful before scaling Skill authoring.

③ Distribution & org-level sharing Issue #228 (17 comments, 8 👍): users must download .skill files, Slack them, and have colleagues manually upload via Settings → Capabilities. A shared library or share link is requested. #189 (9 👍): document-skills and example-skills ship identical content, causing duplicate Skills and wasted context.

④ Context/token economics Issue #1487: claude-api eagerly injects ~156k tokens, exhausting the window in one tool call. #202: skill-creator reads as developer documentation rather than an operational skill — verbose tone is a token-efficiency tax. Demand is shifting from "does it work" to "does it fit."

⑤ Metadata/discovery quality Issue #2064: theme-factory's description says what the skill does but not when to use it — a systemic frontmatter-authoring gap that directly limits trigger rates.

⑥ Proposed new Skill directions (directional signal, lower volume) #1329 compact-memory (symbolic notation for compact agent state); #412 agent-governance (policy enforcement, threat detection, trust scoring, audit trails); #1385 Reasoning Quality Gate Pipeline (pre-task calibration → adversarial review → delivery verification). Common thread: agent self-management and output quality control, not domain tooling.

3. High-Potential Pending Skills (new Skills not yet merged)

PR Skill Updated Why it may land
#525 pyxel — retro game dev 2026-10-23 Maintainer-authored, continuously updated for ~8 months, concrete verification methodology (headless frame inspection)
#1245 notion-spec-to-implementation + quantitative-resume-auditor 2026-10-15 Two-for-one bundle; spec→task decomposition is a high-leverage workflow gap
#1703 md2video-audio — Markdown → MP4 with voiceover 2026-09-15 Fully specified pipeline (Marp slides → TTS → render); zero-cost positioning
#1771 proofcore-contract-auditor — Solidity/Rust static analysis 2026-09-16 Only Web3/Smart-contract Skill proposed; vendor-backed, but TON/Merkle anchoring raises scope-review questions
#1615 scnet-hpc — SSH/Slurm HPC operations 2026-08-24 Profile-based cluster ops; niche but well-scoped, activity has cooled
#486 odt — OpenDocument create/fill/parse 2026-04-14 Fills a real gap vs. the existing docx/pptx/pdf trio; stalled ~6 months, needs a rebase to revive

Stalled-but-valuable: #514 document-typography addresses a defect class affecting every generated document (orphan word wrap, widow headers, numbering misalignment) yet has been quiet since 2026-03-13; #210 rewrites frontend-design for single-conversation actionability.

Review-bandwidth bottleneck: the oldest open fix in this set is #538 (2026-03-06) — eight case-sensitivity mismatches breaking pdf/SKILL.md on case-sensitive filesystems. Trivial to merge, open ~8 months. This suggests merge throughput, not contributor supply, is the constraint.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's demand is concentrated on the reliability and trustworthiness of the Skills toolchain itself — that skill-creator's evaluation harness actually triggers and scores honestly, that bundled Skills keep working against current SDKs, and that the anthropic/ namespace can't be impersonated — rather than on any new Skill category.

Methodology note: PR comment counts and reaction counts were unavailable (undefined / 0) in the source export, so PR ranking reflects cross-referenced issues, update recency, and skill centrality. Issue-based trends are ranked by actual comment counts.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-10-29

1. Today's Highlights

No releases shipped in the last 24 hours, but issue activity is heavy (50 issues updated) and skews toward auth/MCP reliability and cost control. The long-running multi-account Connector request (#27302) remains the community's most-engaged thread at 289 comments and 435 👍, while a new data-loss report (#41458) and a prompt-cache cost regression (#105564) are drawing fresh attention from power users. Web/desktop parity gaps — OpenTelemetry configuration, routine session lifecycle, and Windows Remote Control — round out today's signal.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #27302 — Support multiple Connector accounts (OPEN, 289 comments, 435 👍) The single highest-engagement issue in the repo. Users want the same Connector bound to multiple accounts simultaneously in Claude and Claude Code on the web. The volume of 👍 signals this is a blocker for agencies and multi-tenant developers.

  2. #41458 — cleanupPeriodDays: 99999 ignored, 490 sessions deleted (OPEN, regression, data-loss) An explicit retention setting is being silently overridden, destroying session history on macOS. Labeled data-loss + regression, this is the most severe correctness issue in today's batch — it undermines trust in any config-driven retention guarantee.

  3. #80261 — Persistent usage-limit indicator in desktop app (OPEN, 12 comments, 29 👍) Usage limits are buried; developers want an always-visible quota signal on the main screen. Steady support reflects how cost anxiety now shapes day-to-day workflow.

  4. #32364 — OpenTelemetry configuration in Claude Code on the Web (OPEN, 9 comments, 37 👍) OTel is available in the CLI but not in the web surface, breaking observability parity for teams that standardize on claude.ai/code. High 👍-to-comment ratio suggests quiet but broad enterprise demand.

  5. #101522 — Path-independent project identity + memory sync (OPEN, 8 comments) Projects are keyed by filesystem path slug, so the same repo appears as several unrelated projects across machines, containers, and worktrees. A foundational ask that would fix a whole class of memory fragmentation bugs.

  6. #95764 — Opus 5 returns inter-tool prose as summarized thinking blocks (OPEN, 8 comments) Since 2026-09-11, prose between tool calls arrives as a server-written summary, dropping code blocks and leaving the model believing the user saw content they never did. A subtle model/TUI contract regression with real debugging consequences.

  7. #74682 — Auto-archive routine run sessions (OPEN, 8 comments) Hourly routines generate ~18 stale tabs per day with no cleanup. Small ergonomics request, but the volume-driven tab sprawl makes desktop routines hard to use at scale.

  8. #105564 — Second turn re-writes ~17k session-start context to prompt cache (OPEN, 2 comments) Every new session pays one avoidable full-context cache write. Low comment count but high practical impact — this is a direct, recurring cost leak on Windows.

  9. #105408 — apiKeyHelper not re-run on 401 under Vertex with SKIP_VERTEX_AUTH=1 (OPEN, 27 👍) Gateway setups lose credential rotation: an expired token never triggers the helper. The 27 👍 on a one-day-old issue shows how many teams run Vertex through gateways.

  10. #105857 — Project-scoped stdio MCP server killed as stale in git worktree sessions (OPEN) MCP servers connect successfully (~0.4s) then get reaped ~2.5s later under .claude/worktrees/<name>. Blocks a common agentic-worktree workflow and points at a path-identity bug adjacent to #101522.

Also worth watching: #105958 (cloud routines hang on unanswered control_request — 0/4 runs execute), #105658 (Windows Remote Control sessions exit ~4s after spawn since CLI 2.1.308), #101916 (no integrity protection for resumed session transcripts).

4. Key PR Progress

Only 2 pull requests were updated in the last 24 hours, so the full set is listed below rather than a top 10.

  1. #32751 — fix(hookify): map stop/prompt events to correct field names (OPEN) Fixes #32153. Hookify rules using the simple pattern syntax with event: stop or event: prompt never fire, because config_loader.py maps them to field='content', which rule_engine._extract_field() cannot resolve for Stop/UserPromptSubmit events. Restores a silently dead hook path.

  2. #32755 — feat(plugins): add edit-verifier plugin for post-edit verification (OPEN) Addresses #32658. Adds a PostToolUse hook that verifies Edit-tool outcomes instead of assuming success — catching whitespace mismatches and already-modified targets that currently fail silently while the model proceeds on a false premise.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this period; section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Multi-account & identity flexibility — Binding multiple accounts to one Connector (#27302), path-independent project identity (#101522), and cross-machine memory sync form a single "identity is too rigid" cluster.
  • Observability parity across surfaces — OpenTelemetry in Claude Code on the Web (#32364) is the leading example of CLI capabilities missing from the web/cloud runtime.
  • Cost & quota transparency — Persistent usage indicators (#80261), session-limit vs. Agent SDK accounting (#104738), and cache-write waste (#105564) all ask for the same thing: make spend legible and predictable.
  • Session lifecycle control — Auto-archive for routine runs (#74682), integrity protection for resumed transcripts (#101916), and non-destructive retention (#41458).
  • Desktop/keybinding customization — Rebinding or disabling ⌘K (#105956) and persistent quota UI signal a push for a configurable desktop surface.
  • Web/cloud reliability — Routines that hang on permission control requests (#105958) and Android download naming (#105955).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent data loss beats performance concerns. cleanupPeriodDays being ignored (#41458) and unverified transcript integrity (#101916) erode the assumption that local session history is durable.
  • Auth and token state is fragile around MCP. Stale needs_auth states clearing shared Keychain tokens (#105957), refresh-token corruption on macOS (#105456), and apiKeyHelper not firing on 401 (#105408) all point to a credential lifecycle that doesn't survive retries, gateways, or multi-session sharing.
  • Cost leaks are small, frequent, and invisible. A 17k-token cache rewrite on turn two (#105564) and token spikes on failed MCP calls to disabled servers (#105670) are the kind of per-session overhead users cannot see or prevent.
  • Model instruction adherence degrades over long sessions. Reports of CLAUDE.md rules being ignored (#105604, closed as duplicate), scope creep (#103836), and memory rules followed only ~72% of the time when just the MEMORY.md index is in context (#105867) suggest memory architecture, not prompt wording, is the bottleneck.
  • MCP lifecycle breaks in non-standard repo layouts. Worktree-scoped stdio servers being reaped (#105857) and the built-in claude-artifacts server 404ing on every session start (#105488).
  • Platform-specific regressions keep landing on Windows. Remote Control session exits (#105658), Cowork rejecting plain-ASCII path handling (#105954), and the cache regression above all share a platform:windows label.
  • Long-tail process pain: bot-closed duplicate reports without fixes (#95268, reopened slash-menu regression) remain a recurring community complaint about triage quality.
OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-10-29

1. Today's Highlights

Two Rust alpha builds shipped (0.166.0-alpha.6 / alpha.5.1) with no detailed changelog. Community attention is dominated by a cluster of image-heavy context and compaction failures causing WebSocket disconnects, oversized requests, and repeated auto-compaction across macOS and Windows. Windows desktop regressions and long-standing UX requests (message editing, undo/redo, chat search) remain highly visible.

2. Releases

  • rust-v0.166.0-alpha.6 — Release
    Alpha release only; no release notes beyond the version bump.
  • rust-v0.166.0-alpha.5.1 — Release
    Alpha patch release; no substantive changelog provided.

No stable release was published in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #36040 — iOS Remote only lists projects with recent chats

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #58083 — Use a dedicated binary for Bazel schema generation
    Moves schema export off the application build critical path by building the exporter with --cfg=test, avoiding unnecessary test compilation.

  2. #58075 — Use serving assessments for adaptive Guardian review
    Matches final serving assessments to responses and output items, then uses them instead of asynchronous scoring for adaptive review. Relevant to approval latency and policy enforcement.

  3. #58045 — Managed command checkpoints requiring fresh human approval
    Adds decision = "prompt-user" support in managed requirements.toml prefix rules, allowing policies to require explicit human confirmation independent of automatic review or saved approvals.

  4. #58040 — Preserve native tool-call evidence through Guardian review
    Keeps original function-call metadata available even after the call leaves live conversation history, improving review reliability for encrypted multi-agent messages.

  5. #58034 — Add an option to disable successful SSE delta logs
    Introduces otel.log_sse_deltas (default enabled). Setting it to false suppresses successful .delta event logs while preserving errors, completions, and metrics.

  6. #58028 — Direct Guardian review of recorded exec calls

  7. #57978 — Per-chat leases for shared MCP connections
    Negotiates a codex/connection-lease extension for pooled stdio MCP connections and attaches host-owned lease IDs to tool calls and resource reads.

  8. #57970 — Experimental UI tree renderer for the status line
    Adds a disabled-by-default tui_extensions_statusline feature supporting text, HTTP(S) links, rows, spacers, dividers, and gaps through a shared renderer.

  9. #57870 — Server-side output truncation for Code Mode sessions
    Makes Code Mode honor each session's output_truncation setting instead of always using client-side output handling, enabling server truncation and observation budgets.

  10. #57866 — Retry transient environment startup failures on the next turn
    Allows commands to recover after an executor becomes available, rather than persisting a startup failure across turns when the environment and workspace are unchanged.

Ideas

Q&A

Show and tell

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Predictable usage and updates: Monthly usage resets for Plus subscribers (#57967) and non-blocking background CLI updates (#30332).
  • Enforceable safety controls: Users want file-write/delete restrictions that cannot be overridden by model behavior, plus stronger approval checkpoints (#57827).
  • Better context and media handling: Repeated requests center on bounding retained image payloads, reliable compaction, and avoiding reconnect/request-size failures in long sessions.
  • Cross-agent interoperability: Community projects increasingly focus on connecting Codex with other coding agents and external documentation sources.

  • Image-heavy sessions destabilize long-running work. Multiple issues describe retained images causing repeated auto-compaction, WebSocket reconnects, 35–46 MiB requests, HTTP 400s, and multi-gigabyte upload amplification (#33493, #55730, #54501, #55076).

Gemini CLI Community Digest — 2026-10-29

1. Today's Highlights

No releases shipped in the last 24 hours, but activity remained concentrated in the area/agent workstream, where 30 of the top issues by comment count were updated. The dominant themes are subagent reliability and observability — false success reporting, indefinite hangs, and configuration overrides being ignored — alongside a notable wave of PRs hardening session-history integrity, cancellation semantics, and shell-security checks.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #22323 — Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS is reported as GOAL success (P1, 13 comments, 👍2) The codebase_investigator subagent returns status: "success" / Termination Reason: "GOAL" even though its own payload says it hit the turn cap before doing any analysis. This is the most-discussed issue of the day because it silently corrupts agent orchestration decisions — parent agents treat a truncated run as a clean completion.

  2. #19873 — Leverage model's bash affinity via zero-dependency OS sandboxing (P2, 9 comments, 👍1) Proposes letting Gemini 3 chain native POSIX tools (grep, sed, awk) inside a sandbox rather than routing everything through bespoke tools. A design-level discussion about matching the model's training distribution without sacrificing user security.

  3. #21409 — Generalist agent hangs (P1, 8 comments, 👍8) The highest-reacted issue in the set: any deferral to the generalist agent can hang indefinitely, even for trivial work like folder creation. Users report waiting up to an hour; disabling subagent delegation is the current workaround.

  4. #22745 — Assess impact of AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping (P2, 7 comments, 👍1) An EPIC tracking whether AST-aware reads can tighten method bounds per tool call, cut wasted turns, and reduce token noise. Paired with #22746 (tilth/glyph) and #22747 (ast-grep) — clearly a coordinated investigation.

  5. #21968 — Gemini does not use skills and sub-agents enough (P2, 7 comments) Anecdotal but widely echoed: custom skills (e.g. gradle, git) are only invoked when explicitly instructed, not when contextually relevant. Points at skill-discovery/steering quality rather than capability.

  6. #29325 — Print mode (-p) hangs indefinitely on all inference (P1, 5 comments) Reported on 1.2.2 and independently confirmed: the CLI accepts the prompt, then never returns — no error, no timeout. High severity for anyone scripting Gemini CLI in CI.

  7. #22267 — Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (e.g. maxTurns) (P2, 4 comments) AgentRegistry merges settings correctly at init, but the Browser Agent bypasses them at runtime. A concrete configuration-integrity bug with an obvious root cause.

  8. #21983 — Browser subagent fails on Wayland (P1, 4 comments, 👍1) Reports Termination Reason: GOAL alongside a failure — the same success/failure mislabeling pattern as #22323, this time on Linux/Wayland.

  9. #24246 — 400 error with >128 tools (P2, 3 comments) Exceeding the tool budget produces a hard 400. Expectation is that the agent scopes enabled tools more intelligently rather than failing the whole turn.

  10. #22672 — Agent should stop/discourage destructive behavior (P2, 3 comments, 👍1) The model occasionally reaches for git reset or --force where a safer path exists. Maintainer-authored, which signals this is being treated as a guardrail requirement rather than a user error.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #30019 — fix(core): preserve session history during tool output masking Prevents the first user prompt from being lost when resuming sessions whose tool outputs were masked, avoiding turn coalescing side effects in getHistory().

  2. #30020 — fix(core): drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry On mid-stream retries, both the failed and successful attempt's ToolCallRequest events were being executed — meaning side-effecting commands could run twice. A significant correctness fix.

  3. #30022 — fix(cli): run ACP tool calls through hooks Routes editor-driven (ACP) sessions through BeforeTool/AfterTool, closing a policy gap where hook rules only applied to the interactive CLI.

  4. #30029 — feat(core,cli): make command substitution block user-configurable Adds security.allowCommandSubstitution (default false) to replace the hardcoded block on $(), backticks, and process substitution. Fixes #27393; marked help wanted.

  5. #30026 — fix(core): treat project temp paths as local in untrusted flag checks Stops Gemini's own helper scripts under ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/... from triggering repeated confirmation prompts after their paths appear in shell output.

  6. #30027 — feat(cli): support separate custom theme configuration (P1) Lets users define custom themes independently of the built-in set — a long-standing customization request landing as a large PR.

  7. #30023 — fix(ci,sdk): run SDK tests in PR CI and fix AgentLoopContext mock Re-enables 6 previously skipped GeminiCliSession.sendStream() unit tests and adds the SDK package to the CI test shard.

  8. #30017 — fix(core): keep committed turns when cancelling a tool-result continuation Fixes history rollback that erased the user prompt and already-executed tool turns (which may have modified files) when cancelling mid-request.

  9. #29977 — fix(core): honor cancellation in read_background_output The tool ignored its abort signal, sleeping the full delay_ms and reading the log anyway. Paired with #29978, which fixes dropped boundary lines in the same 64KB tail-read window.

  10. #30006 — fix(core): use PowerShell CIM fallback for Windows IDE process lookup Replaces a Unix-only ps fallback that silently returned an empty command string when the PowerShell snapshot failed.

5. Hot Discussions

Omitted — no discussion data was provided.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • AST-aware codebase tooling — The strongest coordinated direction this cycle: #22745, #22746, #22747. Motivation is both precision (correct method bounds in one call) and efficiency (fewer turns, less token noise).
  • Token-frugal context management — #19561 proposes a "Tactful Extraction" hierarchy (grep first, surgical reads later) against a ~36.6k token/turn baseline. Related: replacing in-context todo lists with persistent file-backed tracking (#18836, #21000).
  • Subagent observability & governance — Shareable subagent trajectories via /chat share (#22598), subagent context in /bug reports (#21763), discovery via settings.json (#18285), and parallel subagent shared memory (#18287).
  • Sandboxing & scoped policy — Bash-native sandboxing (#19873) and per-workspace policy instead of global policy (#18397).
  • Self-awareness of CLI mechanics — #21432 asks the agent to know its own flags, hotkeys, and invocation patterns accurately.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Terminal-state bugs in subagents are the top frustration. Indefinite hangs (#21409), false GOAL/success reporting on turn-limit exhaustion (#22323, #21983), and repeated status/need-retesting tags suggest fixes land but aren't staying fixed.
  • Non-interactive mode is unreliable. -p hanging on all inference with no timeout (#29325 is the clearest blocker for CI/scripted use.
  • Config doesn't always win. Settings merged at init but ignored at runtime by the Browser Agent (#22267); symlinked agent files aren't discovered at all (#20079).
  • Workspace hygiene. The model litters temp edit scripts across directories (#23571) and can reach for destructive git operations (#22672) — both increase friction at commit time.
  • Stuck interactive prompts. Scaffolding flows like create vite block on TUI prompts instead of proceeding (#22465).
  • Platform-specific breakage — Wayland browser support and Windows/PowerShell quoting and process detection continue to generate a steady tail of bugs.

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-10-29

Today's Highlights

OpenCode shipped v2.2.1, headlined by the new /goal primitive that turns a session into a persistent, reviewer-verified objective loop in both the TUI and Desktop. The release landed alongside a process-daemon/@opencode/pty bump to protocol 7. Releases

v2.2.1

  • Keep Working Toward a Goal: /goal <objective> in the TUI or Desktop keeps the session running until a reviewer confirms the objective is met. Control surface includes /goal pause, /goal resume, and /goal clear.
  • PR: anomalyco/opencode#59437

process-daemon v0.3.2

  • opencode-pty 0.3.2 (protocol 7) built from packages/process-daemon, published to npm as @opencode/pty@0.3.2. Affects terminal/PTY consumers; a protocol bump is worth pinning deliberately.

Hot Issues

  1. #59387 — Zen free tier master thread (98 comments, 👍9) — The canonical funnel for free-tier failures: "Free usage exceeded," reset timers that never fire, and Desktop versions rejecting subscriptions. The high comment count reflects unresolved per-user quota state rather than a single reproducible bug.

  2. #18654 — Cannot change or remove email in OpenCode Zen (14 comments, 👍20) — Highest-reaction item in the set. GitHub email changes create duplicate Zen identities with no user-facing remediation. Marked pending close, but the 👍 count signals real account-lifecycle friction.

  3. #48743 — MCP pre-spawn/warm-up + reconnect path (10 comments) — On Windows Desktop with 14+ local stdio MCP servers, all of them get marked failed at session start from concurrent cold starts. The servers are healthy; the supervisor isn't. A warm-up/reconnect API would fix a whole class of setups.

  4. #48657 — Session never drains when Snapshot.capture() stalls (8 comments) — git add --all --pathspec-from-file=- hangs on a large untracked, non-gitignored tree, blocking llm.stream() and leaving the execution claim held forever. A hard hang with no timeout or user-visible diagnostic.

  5. #48497 — Persistent memory system (/teach, /recall, /learn, /memory) (7 comments) — Proposes first-class long-term memory rather than re-deriving context each session. Closed as triage, but the request direction recurs repeatedly.

  6. #49042 — Agent loop runs 500+ steps with zero user input (6 comments) — Runaway auto-continue after the model emits final text. No step ceiling, no guard. Pairs directly with today's /goal release: persistent loops need persistent safety rails.

  7. #24981 — Explicit proxy configuration in opencode config (6 comments, 👍8) — Still open since April. Env-var-only proxying (HTTPS_PROXY, etc.) doesn't cover per-provider routing or GUI-launched Desktop sessions.

  8. #59817 — mkdir EEXIST on shell/<projectID> silently falls back to home dir (3 comments, reproduced) — A file occupying the project-ID path causes 500s on every request, and the TUI quietly starts sessions in $HOME. Silent fallback is the dangerous part — it can run tools in the wrong directory.

  9. #48542 — Compaction writes Anthropic prompt cache that is never read (3 comments) — 70 compactions over 7 days wrote 1,278,055 cache tokens with 0 reads. Cache writes bill at a premium, so this is direct, quantifiable spend waste.

  10. #59916 — opencode run Ctrl-C leaves the bash tool command running (3 comments) — On SIGINT/SIGTERM during a bash tool call, OpenCode exits but the child keeps executing; on --continue the model is told it was "interrupted," desynchronizing state from reality. Especially bad under CI timeout and editor integrations.

Also worth watching: #59909 (paste freezes on Termux, scales with paste size), #48740 (Zen /v1/responses 422 when a tool output contains an image — bricks screenshot sessions), #49034 (v2 on Windows times out waiting for the background service).

Key PR Progress

  1. #60028 — feat(core): Code Mode predicate gates schedule firing — Schedules can take if: { type: "code", code, allow } evaluated before each run with no model call. The program sees only allowlisted tools plus state, now, and runs, and returns { wake, state, message? }. Builds on the scheduling PR #59401 — this is the "cheap gate before expensive agent" pattern.

  2. #60219 — fix(core): select tools automatically during session steps — Makes OpenAI-compatible requests send tool_choice: "auto" on normal steps, fixing vLLM gateways that reject requests omitting the field. Closes #60202.

  3. #60228 — chore(protocol): regenerate OpenAPI document — The Effect 4.0.6 upgrade (#59630) changed the generated schema, so check:generated was failing on dev and blocking every PR's required unit (linux) check. Small diff (maximum: 9007199254740991 on three integer fields), high blast radius — merges unblock CI for everyone.

  4. #60208 — feat(session-ui): user message actions into a menu — Collapses per-message footers to Rewind to here + a More actions (…) menu with timestamp, Fork from here, and Copy message. Reduces visual noise in long timelines.

  8. #60125 — fix(core): preserve pathless MCP OAuth resources — Custom provider validation was dropping a pathless resource such as https://example.com. Closes #58956 and unblocks OAuth-protected MCP servers behind root-domain issuers.

  • MCP lifecycle management — Warm-up/pre-spawn and reconnect (#48743), plus pathless OAuth resource preservation (#60125). The ask is shifting from "support MCP" to "supervise MCP."
