  • Session-scoped model/agent selection for attached TUI/ACP — #48759, from embedders driving the same runtime via ACP. A power-user/embedding signal rather than a mass request.

Developer Pain Points

  • Free-tier quota state is the single loudest complaint. #59387 (98 comments) plus #59911 and #60224 all describe the same failure shape: a limit message with a reset timestamp that never arrives. Users can't self-diagnose, so every instance becomes a support thread.
  • Hangs without timeouts. Both #48657 (git add on huge untracked trees) and #59909 (Termux paste, cost scaling with input size) are O(n)-or-worse stalls with no progress signal or cancellation. The TUI has no "this is stuck" affordance.
  • Runaway agent loops. #49042 reports 500+ auto-continued steps with no user input and no guard. With /goal now shipping, an explicit step/budget ceiling is an obvious follow-up.
  • Cache economics are invisible and wrong. #48542 (1.28M cache-write tokens, 0 reads) and #48624 (glm-5.3-flash showing zero cache reads while deepseek-v4.1-flash caches normally) both amount to users paying for caching they never benefit from — with no surfaced metrics to notice it.
  • Signal handling and orphaned child processes. #59916 leaves bash commands running after exit and records a false "interrupted" state, so resume diverges from reality. This pattern is hostile to CI and editor integrations.
  • Silent fallbacks that change execution context. #59817 quietly relocates a session to $HOME when mkdir returns EEXIST — errors that alter where tools run should fail loudly.
  • Config strictness asymmetry. #49027 forwards unknown agent config fields verbatim into upstream provider requests, producing invalid_request_error; #48555 rejects a subagent for mixed-case model names after suggesting the correct name. Config validation is inconsistent in both directions — too permissive outward, too brittle inward.
  • Windows Desktop background service reliability. #49034 (startup timeout for the managed service), #48715 (sidecar 0xC0000409 crashes under memory pressure), and #48743 (MCP cold-start failures) form a consistent Windows stability cluster.

No Discussion data was provided for this period, so that section is omitted.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-10-29

Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours; activity was dominated by the long-running Windows usability thread (#7547, now 91 comments) and a cluster of fullscreen/TUI rendering performance reports. On the fix side, a wave of closed PRs addressed session-storage semantics, terminal control-sequence handling, pi.exec buffering, and environment-daemon teardown, while Bedrock Mantle routing and Anthropic server-side message threads remain in review.

Releases

None in the last 24 hours.

Hot Issues

  1. #7547 — [Windows] How do you use Pi on Windows? What issues are you seeing? (91 comments, 👍2)
    The central sink thread for Windows support. The motivation is explicitly strategic: too many supported run paths make it unclear whether to fix bugs, improve docs, or delegate to extensions. Highest-engagement issue in the dataset and the best signal for where Windows investment should go.

  2. #9549 — Large transcripts re-render every frame; resize re-emits the whole transcript (17 comments, 👍1)
    On Windows Terminal with 2 logical cores, a large transcript saturates a core. Reported with agent-assisted measurements and verified with pi -ne, making it unusually actionable. Points at fullscreen render-loop architecture rather than a one-off bug.

  3. #7739 — Set a startup-time budget targeting jcode-comparable latency and memory (12 comments)
    Proposes a concrete benchmark-backed budget against jcode (10 interactive PTY launches, Linux). Signals community interest in treating startup latency as a tracked, regression-guarded metric rather than an ad hoc concern.

  4. #9656 — Mouse wheel scrolls prompt history instead of transcript in fullscreen on Windows + Zellij (11 comments, 👍5)
    Highest upvote count among open bugs here. Narrow repro (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi; works without multiplexer, works on Linux+tmux), which strongly suggests multiplexer/terminal capability detection is the culprit.

  5. #9884 — Configured default model sometimes replaced by a fallback at startup (7 comments)
    Reproduced 4/20 startups: defaultProvider/defaultModel from a runtime-discovered extension catalog is silently swapped for the built-in deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro. Nondeterministic startup state is a trust problem for teams pinning models.

  6. #10954 — OpenCode Go Claude (anthropic-messages): 400 on replayed thinking block after tool list change (6 comments)
    Same failure class as #10324 but on a different transport, with block_binding only sent for supportsMidConvoEffort. Important for anyone routing Anthropic-compatible traffic through third-party relays; AI-disclosed and experimentally verified.

  7. #10386 — Durable: host coding-agent extensions (AgentSession-backed runtime or hook parity) (6 comments, 👍1)
    Requests either an AgentSession-backed runtime or ExtensionAPI hook parity so Durable can run as a first-class extension. Represents the broader ask for extension surfaces that match core capability.

  8. #10616 — Extension pi.exec fails for .cmd commands on Windows (npm, npx, pnpm) (5 comments)
    pi.exec("npm", ["--version"]) returns exit 1 with empty stdout, while the bash tool succeeds. A clean, isolated Windows extension-API defect with an obvious impact on the extension ecosystem.

  9. #10770 — Default permissions of .pi/agent/sessions should be 0700 (5 comments, inprogress)
    Fresh session directories are created group/world-readable. Marked in progress; a straightforward privacy hardening request that matters for shared machines and CI runners.

  10. #11567 — Typing slows down in long sessions: getSessionName() scans every entry on each render (2 comments, filed today)
    At ~400k entries, key-to-render p50 is 21 ms vs 1.5 ms empty; profiling attributes 94% of busy CPU to SessionManager.getSessionName() called from the footer on every render. A newly filed, well-profiled regression with a clear fix path.

Also worth watching: #11529 (tool ordering from a Map busts the prompt cache when MCP servers reconnect) and #11527 (a new BedrockRuntimeClient per request, forcing SSO credential round trips).

Key PR Progress

  1. #11565 — fix(tui): stop writing OSC 133 prompt markers in regular mode (closed)
    Regular TUI mode emitted OSC 133 A/B/C markers; terminals displaying OSC 7501 status (Rex, iTerm2 3.7.5+) interpreted 133;A as a new shell prompt and dropped the working indicator. Resolves #11519.

  2. #11561 — fix(coding-agent): treat sessions in the sessions directory as default storage (closed)
    usesDefaultSessionDir() returned false whenever a session's cwd differed from its folder name, so /resume silently listed only a subset. Fixes a confusing session-discovery bug.

  3. #11562 — fix(coding-agent): start new sessions in the cwd's default directory (open)
    Companion to #11561: /new, /fork, and /clone currently inherit the opened file's folder and treat it as a custom --session-dir. Aligns new-session storage with the actual working directory.

  4. #11556 — fix(coding-agent): let the SDK stream resolve auth for summaries (closed)
    Sessions from createAgentSession passed a resolved access token as options.apiKey for compaction/branch/bug-report summaries, bypassing modelRuntime.streamSimple's auth resolution. Important for SDK embedders using OAuth.

  5. #11546 — fix(coding-agent): cap pi.exec output at 256 MiB (closed, closes #11360)
    Adds ExecOptions.maxBuffer, defaulting to the smaller of 256 MiB and the runtime string limit; oversized commands are terminated with truncated: true and a nonzero exit code. Prevents runaway memory from chatty subprocesses.

  6. #11545 — Anthropic message threads (open)
    Uses Anthropic's server-side message-threads beta to send only new messages when a session id and caching are active, while still building the full request for comparison. Potentially significant token/cost reduction for long sessions.

  7. #11544 — fix(env): kill the daemon's commands when it is terminated (closed)
    Connection.close() sent SIGTERM before the daemon could run kill_all, leaving commands running. Clean teardown fix for the local Unix daemon path.

  8. #11543 / #11541 — fix(coding-agent): strip private-parameter CSI sequences in stripAnsi (closed)
    stripAnsi treated <, =, > as CSI final bytes, so mouse reports like ESC[<35;59;1M leaked parameters into tool output as literal text. Two implementations merged; low-level but affects transcript cleanliness.

  9. #11348 — fix(tui,coding-agent): handle selection page keys in all scrolling lists (closed, fixes #7629)
    Rebases and narrows #7680: honors tui.select.pageUp/pageDown across selection components, autocomplete, and agent selectors, with an explicit fullscreen capture flag so active selections take precedence over transcript scrolling.

  10. #11372 — fix(ai): route Bedrock models Converse does not serve through Bedrock Mantle (open)
    Addresses #5363 for Bedrock API keys: 16 listed models (GPT-5.4–GPT-6.1, gpt-oss, Grok 4.3/4.6, Gemma 4) are only available on Mantle, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and currently fail as invalid Converse model identifiers. Stacked follow-ups #8572/#8573 add SigV4/IAM auth and Anthropic Messages routing.

Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11503 — pi-rs: a Rust port of the headless core — behavioral parity verified atom by atom (+ a DeepSeek API compat finding) (1 comment, 👍1)
    A community Rust reimplementation of pi 0.74.2's headless core: agent loop, seven built-in tools, session JSONL, CLI surface, and system prompt, MIT-licensed with design credit to pi. Includes a DeepSeek API compatibility finding. Notable as both a parity-testing artifact and a signal of demand for a non-Node runtime.

Feature Request Trends

  • Windows as a first-class platform. The dominant cluster: usage-path consolidation (#7547), .cmd/npx execution (#10616), multiplexer-aware scrolling (#9656), and rendering cost on low-core Windows terminals (#9549).
  • Performance as a budgeted, measurable property. Startup latency vs. jcode (#7739), per-frame transcript re-rendering (#9549), and O(entries) work on the render path (#11567) all frame performance as regressions to be guarded, not just optimized.
  • Deeper extension APIs. Hook parity / AgentSession-backed runtimes (#10386), returnable tool_result results for gating and truncation (#11553), namespace-scoped tool_search (+docs read_page, #11558), deferred runtime reloads (#7948), and per-tool MCP exposure toggles (#11526).
  • Provider and catalog correctness. Prompt-cache metadata for Bedrock Claude (#11528), Mantle routing for models Converse rejects (#11372), and configurable OAuth/Copilot timeouts (#11549).
  • Privacy and credential hygiene. 0700 session directories (#10770) and moving deviceId out of shareable global settings (#10187).
  • Session storage semantics. Default-directory resolution and /resume visibility (#11561, #11562) — small fixes with outsized UX impact.

Developer Pain Points

  • Windows support is fragmented across run paths. The 91-comment sink thread makes the root frustration explicit: users cannot tell which Windows setup is "blessed," and extension authors hit platform-specific breakage (pi.exec with .cmd, Zellij multiplexing, terminal status markers).
  • Long sessions degrade interactivity. Two independent reports (#9549, #11567) trace slowness to work done on every render — full transcript re-emission and per-render session-name scans. The 21 ms vs. 1.5 ms keystroke latency at 400k entries is a concrete ceiling.
  • Prompt caching is easy to invalidate accidentally. Tool insertion order in a Map (#11529) and missing promptCache metadata on Bedrock (#11528) silently convert cached turns into full-price ones.
  • Nondeterministic startup configuration. A configured default model being replaced by a fallback in 20% of starts (#9884) undermines reproducibility for teams.
  • Provider adapters leak upstream quirks. Replayed thinking blocks over relays (#10954), per-request Bedrock client construction forcing SSO round trips (#11527), oversized default output budgets triggering HTTP 402 (#11517), and fixed 15s/5s OAuth timeouts (#11549).
  • Session storage is surprising. Sessions live in folders named after the original cwd, causing /resume to hide sessions and /new to inherit the wrong directory (#11561, #11562).
  • Subprocess and daemon lifecycle edge cases. Unbounded pi.exec output (#11360 → #11546), panics on helper-thread exhaustion (#11433), and orphaned commands on daemon shutdown (#11544) are all "works until it doesn't" failure modes.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-29

1. Today's Highlights

The v0.26.3 release line landed across CLI, Desktop, and the TypeScript SDK, with generated UI cards now preserving inputs and state across navigation and split views and rendering live results only on MCP Apps–capable clients. Meanwhile, the issue tracker is dominated by CI and release-infrastructure work: a long-running Managed Agent gate failure has accumulated 79 comments, and a newly reported P1 config regression (contextWindowSize being silently removed) is the most user-impacting new bug of the day.

2. Releases

  • v0.26.3 — Main stable release. Release notes in the source feed are placeholder-only (qwen-release-notes:v1), so the substantive changes are visible through the bundled Desktop and nightly entries below.
  • desktop-v0.26.3 — Adds managed session permission rules and Auto approval (#15448) and hardens serve token handling in the CLI.
  • v0.26.3-nightly.20261028.ca204559a7 — Includes fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped (#15794) and managed-mode documentation updates.
  • sdk-typescript-v0.1.25 — Bundles CLI 0.26.3 (built from the same source ref as the SDK).
  • Highlighted change: Generated UI cards retain inputs and state across navigation and split views, display live views after the initial calculation, and are gated to clients that can render MCP Apps (#15611, #15787).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #15855 — contextWindowSize gets automatically removed [P1, bug, configuration, need-information] · 3 comments · New today. Users running local OpenAI-compatible backends (Ollama, 128k window) report their configured context limit is stripped from settings, which can cause unexpected truncation or context overflow. Highest-severity new user-facing bug in this window.
  2. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified [bug, autofix/skip] · 79 comments · Open since 2026-10-19. The single loudest thread in the repo; the bot keeps appending commit markers without converging on a test attribution, which is exactly the failure mode the tracker is supposed to prevent.
  3. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed [needs-triage, ci-cd] · 35 comments · A month-long recurring failure. Whether the cause is a real high-severity advisory or a flaky npm audit endpoint, the signal has been unusable for 30 days, which is a supply-chain risk.
  4. #15861 — Web Shell host-directory-picker smoke times out deterministically [P1, testing, ready-for-agent] · 2 comments · Opened today. A PR-independent failure means every contributor pays a re-attribution round; the reporter explicitly frames it as a tax on unrelated PRs.
  5. #15052 — Preserve independent main E2E validation when pending runs are replaced [P2, ci-cd, ready-for-human] · 14 comments · Ref-scoped concurrency can cancel older pending runs even with cancel-in-progress: false, so intermediate main SHAs lose independent validation. Important for anyone relying on per-commit green status.
  6. #15461 — Isolate the release-only host from the shared runner pool [P2, ci-cd, ready-for-human] · 7 comments · The opt-in route to ecs-qwen-release-host was merged but the machine was never provisioned, so publish still competes for GitHub-hosted capacity. Directly tied to release latency.
  7. #15783 — Move routine macOS/Darwin validation to overnight runs [P3, ci-cd, need-discussion] · 4 comments · Proposes a repo-wide policy: overnight Asia/Shanghai macOS runs on main, Linux-only for PRs. A cost/capacity decision that would affect contributor feedback loops.
  8. #11665 — Responses cleanup can break reasoning/tool-call adjacency [P2, core, CLOSED] · 5 comments · A subtle correctness bug: replayed reasoning items and their function_call must be treated as one unit, but cleanup handled them separately. Closure is a meaningful reliability win for OpenAI Responses–compatible providers.
  9. #1206 — Dynamic multi-model support for OpenAI-compatible APIs [feature-request] · 3 comments, 2 👍 · Open since 2025-12-10. Users want to discover and switch among models from a single endpoint rather than hardcoding one. The longest-lived product request in this batch.
  10. #15866 — Show Export and Restore inline on archived session rows [P3, ui, web-shell] · 2 comments · Opened today. Small but representative of a steady stream of Web Shell ergonomics requests around session lifecycle actions.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15620 — feat(channels): Microsoft Teams extension and host ingress · Adds Teams support for personal chats, explicit group mentions, channel-thread isolation, and ordered final-text replies, usable standalone or embedded via createTeamsIngress. Largest new integration surface in this batch.
  2. #15865 — feat(managed): live message paging in WebShell · Reads the latest 100 materialized items directly from SQL (including sessions without a published snapshot), pages older messages on scroll-up, and keeps live traffic on the existing event stream.
  3. #15863 — fix(cli): separate instruction files from auto memory in context usage · Splits the context-usage breakdown into "Instruction files" (project/user/extension/language) vs. "Auto memory" (policy + catalog snapshots) across API, SDK types, and terminal output. Makes context budgeting auditable.
  4. #15849 — feat(web-shell): extend one-click update coverage · Extends the daemon one-click update to pnpm/yarn/bun global installs and to npm prefixes that require sudo, using a user-scoped isolated staging prefix.
  5. #15837 — fix(cli): reply to SDK initialize only after config is ready · Closes a race where the SDK control response could be sent before SDK MCP servers and staged SDK-only config were in place. Important for SDK embedders.
  6. #15835 — fix(web-shell): keep "+ Add session" clickable when the catalog is empty · The button was disabled exactly in the case the reload-on-open effect exists for, making the picker unreachable. Straightforward Split View usability fix.
  7. #13445 — feat: render plan approval as markdown and capture plans as Todos · Long-running draft replacing raw <pre> output in ToolApproval.tsx and turning approved plans into Session Workflow Todos. Notable as one of the older still-open feature PRs.
  8. #14577 — fix(web-shell): prune split panes whose session left the active catalog · Treats the daemon's 409 session_archived as terminal, so an archived session's pane no longer stays empty and retries forever.
  9. #15854 — perf(release): reuse verified native audio prebuilds across releases · Fingerprints audio build inputs and reuses prior official main artifacts when identical, avoiding five target rebuilds per release. Direct answer to release-time complaints.
  10. #15864 — fix(ci): skip source TUI gates for Companion-only changes · Skips TUI parity/no-flicker jobs for VSCode-Companion-only PRs while still running them for manifests, bundler config, scripts/, and mixed changes.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in the source feed, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Web Shell / Desktop ergonomics is the dominant product theme. Keyboard shortcuts for Session Overview and Split View (#13175, closed), inline Export/Restore on archived rows (#15866), sidebar category header alignment (#15867), host-supplied directory pickers (#15186, closed), and macOS daemon PATH extension (#12690, closed) all point at polishing the shell rather than adding core capability.
  • Session management correctness. No-workspace sessions missing from Session Overview (#11878, closed) and branch actions disappearing after disk restore (#13782, closed) were both resolved; splitting, archiving, and restoring sessions remain active friction areas.
  • Provider/model flexibility. Dynamic discovery and switching of models on OpenAI-compatible endpoints (#1206) remains the clearest unmet ask, reinforced by today's contextWindowSize regression for local Ollama users (#15855).
  • IDE and remote-development coverage. The VS Code companion still needs coverage for forwarded-port host gating, IPv6 CSP, and Remote-SSH/WSL runs (#12059).
  • Skills lifecycle maturity. Follow-up work from the user-scope Skill activation PR (#15622) shows the feature is shipping but still accumulating contract and lifecycle refinements.
  • Localization. Browser-locale fallback (everything non-zh-CN collapsing to en) was raised for Goal cards (#13391, closed) — the i18n surface is still only two locales.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI noise is crowding out real signal. Bot-filed "no test identified" issues (#14724 at 79 comments, #15173 at 19, plus several per-commit Managed Agent gate reports) generate high comment volume without converging on attribution, and closed-when-green reports keep needing manual dismissal.
  • Deterministic, PR-independent test failures block everyone. #15861 makes the Web Shell smoke lane fail on unrelated PRs, forcing re-attribution on every change.
  • Release pipeline latency and capacity. Post-publish fan-out still waits 37–50 minutes on GitHub-hosted runners (#15465), and the dedicated release host remains unprovisioned (#15461).
  • Per-SHA validation can be silently lost. Concurrency replacement on main E2E means an intermediate commit may never get an independent verdict (#15052).
  • macOS runner cost pressure. Repeated proposals to move Darwin validation overnight (#15783) reflect a queue/cost tradeoff contributors feel in PR turnaround.
  • Security auditing has been red for a month. The daily dependency CVE audit (#13078) has produced 35 comments with no resolution, leaving teams unsure whether a real advisory is outstanding.
  • Configuration is not always trustworthy. Silently dropped settings appeared both as a fix (fix(config): report controls that were silently dropped, #15794) and as a new P1 report (#15855) — users want the CLI to surface, not swallow, config it cannot apply.
  • Runtime environment fragility. Historical crashes from missing full-ICU Intl.Segmenter on RHEL 10 (#11747, closed) highlight a recurring class of host-runtime incompatibility without actionable diagnostics.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-29

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-29 14:08 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-29

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 在 2026-10-29 的分诊吞吐量非常高：过去 24 小时内有 500 个 issue 和 500 个 PR 更新，其中 224 个 PR 已合并/关闭，276 个仍开启；142 个 issue 已关闭，358 个仍开启/活跃。未发布新版本，最近的稳定版验证参考是 2026.10.9（Issue #187490），扩展稳定版 2026.9.36 的回合并仍活跃。活动集中在发布工程、CI/测试稳定化，以及一批 Web UI 资源效率修复；而 issue 队列主要由网关启动、崩溃恢复和会话状态缺陷占据。最突出的健康担忧是严重性集中：仅在按评论数排序的前 50 个样本中就至少有七个 P0 issue，其中若干标记为 clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr，表明存在大量缺乏明确修复方案的稳定化积压。总体评估：维护和分诊速度快，但稳定性债务偏高，且今日零发布产出。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时内未发布新版本，“Latest Releases”信息流为空。

来自 issue/PR 元数据的上下文（并非发布公告）：

  • 稳定版线似乎是 2026.10.9，由 #187490 中的发布验证不稳定测试跟踪引用。
  • 2026.10.8 的复盘阻塞项正在 #187249 中处理（发布验证工具）。
  • 扩展稳定版 2026.9.36 正在接收定向回合并：#187252（无状态推理回放保护）和 #187701（实时测试豁免键控）。

今日无破坏性变更或迁移说明可报告。

3. 项目进展

过去 24 小时有 224 个 PR 已合并/关闭。前 30 个样本中可见的值得关注项：

已落地修复（已关闭 PR）：

  • #187646 — 原生 Codex 辅助进程现在会在 Stop 时被清理，防止会话中止后产生孤儿子命令（修复 #187598）。
  • #187687 — Web UI 在隐藏标签页中停止轮询存储维护进度；返回时刷新一次。
  • #187701 — 发布验证豁免已正确按扩展稳定版线设置键值。

值得关注的在途工作（已开启 PR）：

  • MCP 能力缺口： #187699 使配置的 MCP 工具可通过 tools.invoke / HTTP /tools/invoke 工作（当前尽管出现在 tools.effective 中，却返回 not_found）。这消除了一处明显的功能与实现不一致。
  • Web UI 效率批次（vincentkoc）： #187691（在隐藏标签页释放 Markdown worker）、#187693（暂停 Updates 倒计时）、#187686（暂停 Logbook 轮询）。
  • 渠道修复： #147886（Feishu 已记录的 markdown.tables 模式，标记为 merge-risk: compatibility）、#187555（Discord 取消时中止信号传播）、#187199（Mattermost Unicode 规范化）、#187711（Telegram 转发富消息防抖）。
  • 平台正确性： #187703 在系统时钟变化时保持缓存新鲜度；#187177 让 Claude 迁移在 JSON 格式错误时明确失败，而不是静默跳过设置。
  • 记忆子系统： #136482（XL）提议将记忆索引发布移入有界 worker，以减少 SQLite 争用和重建索引泄漏——自 2026-09-02 开启，仍为 needs proof。

已关闭 issue： #178000（会话状态竞态被误分类为模型回退）、#136386（cron exec 允许列表拒绝）、#187468（package-swap 更新失败）。

4. 社区热点话题

评论量是今天主要的互动信号；👍 数量普遍接近零，表明互动以讨论和调试为主，而非广泛的用户投票。

条目 评论数 重要性
#160959 — P0：网关在捕获大型外部插件时阻塞数分钟 64 样本中互动最高的问题。这是 2026.9.6 因插件生成捕获（#144252）引入的回归，会在启动时和运行时重新发布时阻塞事件循环。标记为 no-new-fix-pr + needs-maintainer-review。
#164294 — P2：状态 DB WAL 自动检查点永不完成 38 检查点被进程内读取器永久阻塞（17,091 个日志帧，866 个已检查点）。这是持久化层设计问题，对 P2 而言互动异常高。
#150635 — 短期召回驱逐阻碍 dreaming 提升 21 记忆架构缺陷：512 条目上限 + 每夜零召回摄取阻止深度阶段提升。
#120385 — 用于 cron/记忆刷写轮次的 Code Mode 目录不完整 21 MCP 工具缺失（“Unknown tool id”）仅表现为通用 exec 失败；作者于 2026-10-21 更正了原始范围。
#166634 — P0：检查点失败导致 agent 在崩溃恢复后不可用 18 SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired 会永久阻塞 chat.history、models.list 等。
#172837 — P1：Codex nativeSubagentAssignments 永不移除 17 在投递放弃后，分配条目会在每个新的父线程上重新固定并重新发送。
#177656 — P1：主机 exec 完整性准入错误 17 在稳定版 2026.10.5 上至少 28 次失败；子效果未证实。
#44309 — 单向 A2A 派发模式 15 最古老的高互动功能请求（2026-03-12）；仍为 needs-product-decision。

底层需求：最集中的问题不是功能，而是负载、崩溃以及时钟/睡眠事件下的运行时可靠性。用户运行着带大型插件树、数 GB SQLite 状态和长时间运行会话的网关；当前故障模式是事件循环饥饿、WAL/检查点争用以及崩溃后不可恢复状态。第二组是记忆/召回正确性（#150635、#157827、#148033），表明 dreaming/RAG 流水线需要设计评审，而非点状修复。

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点（不满驱动因素）：

  • 启动与恢复可靠性是主要抱怨。多名用户描述网关启动需数分钟、进入重启循环，或在崩溃/睡眠后使 agent 永久 UNAVAILABLE（#160959、#162211、#166634、#158592、#181459、#176342）。这是生产阻塞问题，而非表面问题。
  • **潜在数据丢失：**Telegram 消息在轮次中途被丢弃并替换为上一条消息正文（#160762）；#126950、#142037、#156070、#149985 也带有消息丢失标签。
  • **长会话的成本/性能：**Anthropic 缓存卡在约 46k 工具+系统前缀，每轮约 377–386k cache_create（#140129）——直接的成本抱怨。
  • **资源泄漏：**MCP 子进程填满 256 上限（#166017）；Codex 子 agent 分配累积（#172837）；待处理输入永不过期（#141295）。
  • **配置/入门摩擦：**Windows Codex 入门（#185819）、缺少 modelProvider 的 registerCliBackend 被静默丢弃（#172969），以及迁移在 JSON 格式错误时静默成功（#187177 / 底层问题）。

积极信号 / 满意度：

  • 用户正在提交高质量、深度埋点的报告（许多被评为 🦞 diamond lobster / 🐚 platinum hermit，附源码级复现和日志），这表明技术投入度高的用户群愿意帮助分诊。
  • 多名报告者明确验证修复并更正自己早先的假设（#120385、#143784），显示出协作式维护文化。
  • Web UI 和可访问性打磨请求（#163739、#154524、#147732、#177094）表明用户正从“它能不能用”转向日常主力工具的易用性——一个成熟度信号。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告 — 个人 AI Agent 与助手开源生态

数据日期： 2026-10-29 · 项目： OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw

1. 生态概览

2026-10-29 的开源个人 AI Agent 格局分化为一个超大规模参考实现（OpenClaw，24h 内触及 500 个 Issue + 500 个 PR）和一簇发布列车驱动、中等规模的项目（ZeroClaw、QwenPaw、Hermes），后者各自正在稳定一个特定的架构命题。窗口内没有任何项目发布版本——每个活跃项目都处于加固或 beta 预览阶段，这表明生态正围绕可靠性而非功能速度进行整合。五大项目中，主导投资领域已从“agent 能做什么”转向会话持久性、多租户隔离、插件供应链信任和静默故障消除——这是技术栈从演示级走向生产级的经典信号。值得注意的是，活跃度极不均衡：IronClaw 实际上闲置，而 OpenClaw 的运行量约为其 500×，这意味着“生态健康度”必须按项目解读，而非按总量解读。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相较同行的优势

  • 社区规模： 一天内触及 500 个 Issue + 500 个 PR，约为每个同行吞吐量的 10–500×。它拥有最深的分诊流水线（带标签的严重度、clawsweeper 自动化、专门的发布验证 Issue）——此处唯一具备正式化发布验证与 extended-stable 回移流程的项目（#187490、#187252、#187701）。
  • 广度： MCP 工具调用、多渠道（Telegram、Discord、Feishu、Mattermost）、Codex/Claude 迁移、memory/dreaming/RAG 子系统——本集合中最广的表面。
  • 参考地位： 它是事实上的“核心参考”，同行的 bug 分类也呼应其子系统。

技术路线差异

  • 以 Gateway 为中心的架构，配有大事件循环和进程内插件捕获——这既是其能力广度的来源，也是其最大 P0 的来源（#160959 事件循环阻塞、#162211 40–200s 启动卡顿、#164294 WAL checkpoint 饥饿）。
  • 大规模下基于 SQLite 的会话/状态存储（#181459 报告 3.5 GB 数据库）——同行还处在这条曲线的更早阶段，尚未触及同样的持久化上限。

社区规模对比

OpenClaw 次大规模（ZeroClaw/Hermes） 比例
每日 PR 吞吐量 500 50 10×
每日合并 PR 数 224 14 16×
参与度高的长线程 Issue（最高项评论数） 64 34 ~2×

评估： OpenClaw 拥有无可匹敌的漏斗顶端参与度和最成熟的流程，但其 P0 稳定性债务现在已是其决定性风险——事件循环饥饿、崩溃恢复不可用、WAL checkpoint 失败，恰好在信任最重要的规模上构成生产阻塞。

成熟度信号 参与度最高、P0 债务最高 参与度高、关闭吞吐低 信号低、受治理门控 快速当日 issue→fix 循环、首次贡献者 关闭吞吐纪律最佳、安全积压仍开放

关键结论： 这些项目并非在同一轴线上竞争。OpenClaw 在广度和社区上竞争；ZeroClaw 在安全隔离；QwenPaw 在打包/垂直部署；Hermes 在多交互面可移植性；IronClaw 在极简主义和精选。这是健康的差异化，但也意味着每个项目都有其他项目覆盖的盲点——例如 ZeroClaw 的 RBAC 成熟度 vs OpenClaw 的渠道广度。

6. 社区势头与成熟度

活跃度分层

层级 项目 特征
T1 — 超大规模 OpenClaw 10× 同行吞吐；流程成熟；承载稳定性债务；今日零发布产出
T2 — 高速稳定化 ZeroClaw、QwenPaw 活跃发布列车（v0.9.0、2.3.0-beta）；同期关闭健康；贡献者落地修复
T3 — 高参与、受接收限制 Hermes Agent 社区质量强（深度复现，在 #18715 上 43👍）但 PR 关闭率 10%——约束是关闭吞吐，不是兴趣
T4 — 闲置 / 受治理门控 IronClaw 1 个 Issue，0 个 PR；贡献漏斗因策略答复受阻（#8161）

势头解读

  • 快速迭代： OpenClaw（500/500，但主要是分诊 + 修复）、ZeroClaw（14 次合并）、QwenPaw（12 次合并 + 同日 6 次关闭）。
  • 稳定化： ZeroClaw（v0.9.0 加固）和 QwenPaw（2.3.0 beta）是最清晰的“发布高质量版本”轨迹。
  • 有停滞风险： Hermes——45/50 个 PR 和 48/50 个 Issue 仍开放；multiplexed-secret 系列（#130663/#146428/#146483/#146484）是单一根因修复，会实质性改善其比例。
  • 休眠： IronClaw——低信号既非正面也非负面，只是缺席。

7. 趋势信号

从社区反馈中提取的行业级模式，按信号强度排序：

  1. 会话可移植性现在已是预期原语，而非功能。 用户将 Desktop→远程 serve→Telegram→Slack 当作一个逻辑会话运行（Hermes #139818/#41220；OpenClaw #158592；ZeroClaw 跨交互面重命名恢复 #10373）。开发者启示：将恢复/身份设计为一等、与交互面无关的契约——而非按交互面分别写逻辑。

  2. 多租户与按发送方/按 agent 隔离是基本门槛。 最高严重度的开放项集中于此：ZeroClaw #9647（S0）、#5982（RBAC）；Hermes UnscopedSecretError 系列；OpenClaw SecretRef 认证。启示：密钥作用域和所有权归属必须在运行时边界强制执行，而非配置层。

  3. 静默故障是头号信任摧毁者。 每个项目都有系统“继续运行如同健康”的报告——图片丢失、cron 投递丢失、配置段被删除、插件加载误报。启示：结构化错误/原因码和显式警告是竞争差异化因素，而非润色。

  4. 插件供应链完整性是新的攻击面。 Manifest/组件生成不匹配（ZeroClaw #11562）、加载器崩溃（QwenPaw #8473）、安装 staging 残留（ZeroClaw #11792）、MCP 工具/实现不匹配（OpenClaw #187699）。启示：签名 manifest、生成版本固定和安装事务正成为预期。

  5. 资源占用和成本是一等投诉。 690MB 导入副作用（QwenPaw #8490）、Anthropic 缓存前缀膨胀（OpenClaw #140129）、ACP token 重复计数（Hermes #146475）、分离的廉价记忆模型（QwenPaw #7719）。启示：成本可观测性和惰性导入卫生应进入发布检查清单。

  6. Provider 注册表正在硬化为治理问题。 IronClaw 明确精选 providers.json（#8161，引用 Novita 关闭）；ZeroClaw/Hermes/QwenPaw 都在处理 Provider PR。启示：生态正分裂为“精选核心 + 外部 Provider 机制”，这有利于拥有成文纳入策略的项目。

  7. 打包/冻结构建 QA 是发布门禁，而非事后补丁。 QwenPaw 的 beta 发布时缺少必需资源；OpenClaw 和 ZeroClaw 都在处理仅 CLI/入门引导构建问题。启示：CI 必须构建并对冻结产物做冒烟测试，而不仅是源代码。

  8. 本地优先 / 隐私保护推理是可信需求向量。 本地 TTS（Hermes #145492）、本地 Piccolo 评分（QwenPaw #8463）、隐私 Provider 注册表压力（IronClaw）、Obscurify 集成（ZeroClaw #12085）。启示：隐私正成为产品品类，而不仅是 Provider 选项。

给决策者的结论： OpenClaw 同时是生态的引擎和最高风险组件；ZeroClaw 和 QwenPaw 是发布就绪度最健康的故事；Hermes 是强社区但受分诊瓶颈限制；IronClaw 休眠且受策略门控。2026-11 的跨领域技术任务明确——持久会话身份、强制隔离、显式失败、可信插件供应链。

5. Bug 与稳定性

没有新披露的崩溃被归为 agent 核心循环上的数据丢失，但多份报告描述了静默失败和永久状态损坏，这些问题实际上更严重。排序如下：

严重 — 数据丢失 / 不可恢复状态

  • #146498 写入部分配置视图会静默删除所有未包含的配置段，既没有跨进程锁，也没有备份。无修复 PR——影响面大。

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点

  • 会话连续性是第一大抱怨点。 用户在进程重启、home 目录移动、多路复用迁移和入口变化后失去可恢复性——而且往往没有恢复路径。
  • 静默失败比显式失败更糟。 Cron 投递连续数天丢失（#146483），MCP 审批在没有提示的情况下被拒绝（#135522），配置段在无警告下被删除（#146498）。用户在标题中反复强调“静默”。
  • 升级回归。 v0.22.4 破坏了 --source desktop（#142991）；多路复用迁移破坏了恢复（#143150）；0.22.5 的 cron 投递重构破坏了插件覆盖（#146484）。
  • 平台缺口。 Windows kanban 卡死（#145156），Linux desktop 透明度/CPU 问题（#145370、#141574），反向代理 dashboard（#90068）。
  • 计量透明度。 ACP 用量重复计数（#146475）和跨模型凭据冷却（#146385）会影响按 prompt 计量或付费的用户。

观察到的用例

  • 一台网关主机服务多个配置档（#146483 中有 13 个配置档；#143150 中有多配置档 Docker）。
  • 远程 hermes serve + 带 basic auth 的本地 Desktop 客户端（#139818）。
  • CLI 工作流中的本地模型（Qwen3.5:9B、GPT-OSS:20B）（#110120）。
  • 通过 Telegram 进行移动端延续（#41220），通过 Slack 进行团队协作（#120618）。
  • 厂商主动完成的集成工作（aimlapi，#146493）。

满意度信号。 报告异常详细且以复现为导向，第三方正在构建集成——这是一个健康信号。不满主要集中在信任上：状态消失、消息消失、配置在无通知的情况下缩减。

4. 社区热点话题

1. #8161 — “你们会接受 Obscurify.ai 作为命名提供商吗？”（开放）

  • 作者：tonydavis629（自述为该提供商的运营者）
  • 创建/更新时间：2026-10-28 · 评论：0 · 反应：0

这是唯一活跃的讨论串，尽管零互动，却默认成为“最热”条目。其实质内容比其指标更重要：

  • 作者引用了已关闭的 Novita PR（#1115），当时给出的理由是提供商列表“不应扩张到包含每一个提供商”。贡献者正将这一先例视为一项隐式策略。
  • 作者以注册表已包含注重隐私的条目（例如 Tinfoil）为由，论证将 Obscurify.ai 归入同一类别是合理的。

深层需求： 贡献者缺乏针对 providers.json 的成文、可预期的准入标准。所问的问题实际上不是“Obscurify.ai 好不好？”，而是“纳入规则是什么？”——这是治理/文档层面的缺口，而非技术问题。这个问题每多一天未获答复，潜在贡献者就面临着据称 Novita 所遭遇的同样的白白投入风险。

请关注 #8161 上维护者的回复，这是最清晰的路线图信号。

7. 用户反馈总结

观察到的痛点：

  • 静默失败侵蚀信任。 #8150（图片被丢弃且无警告）、#8488（Visual Compact 静默失效）和 #8464（压缩因不透明的 400 失败）都有一个共同主题：系统在降低输出质量的同时仍表现得一切正常。用户明确要求提供警告/日志，而不仅仅是修复。
  • 资源占用很重要。 #8490 中仅仅是打开一个设置页就导致 690 MB 的永久 RSS 增长，这对自托管/桌面用户是严重抱怨；而修复来自一位首次贡献者的 PR，说明社区有动力提供帮助。
  • Beta 打包质量。 两位独立报告者在 2.3.0-beta.1 上遇到安装/构建层面的损坏（插件加载器、PyInstaller 资源），这比核心逻辑 bug 更能影响对 beta 的观感。
  • 配置一致性。 #8464 与 #8358 都涉及UI 显示的内容与运行时实际行为之间的差异——这是多 provider、多模型产品中反复出现的满意度风险。
  • 部署/运维基础。 #7740（Hub 模式管理员密码重置）与 #8481（默认语言环境变量）来自为团队运行 QwenPaw 的运维人员，而非单用户——产品正被用于托管部署，却缺乏相应的管理员能力。
  • 高级用户工作流缺口。 #4129（/rewind）与 #4356（只读防护路径）表明用户在进一步推进 agent 自主性，需要可逆性与最小权限控制才能感到安全。

满意度信号： #8464 当日快速周转（issue → 修复 PR → 关闭）、#8150 在开启 20 天后得到响应式分诊，以及多位首次贡献者（#8491、#8345、#8400、#8494），表明贡献管道健康且友好。

运行时与会话可靠性

  • PR #11523 — 已关闭
    修复守护进程在一轮对话中途被杀后，会话永久停留在 running 状态的问题。关闭 Issue #11432。

Web 仪表盘与 ZeroCode 用户体验

  • PR #11571 — 已关闭
    在聊天 hydration 替换本地状态时，保留正在发送中的用户提示词。关闭 Issue #11517。
  • PR #11511 — 已关闭
    使 ZeroCode Config 的保存/取消行为保持一致。关闭 Issue #11486。
  • PR #12100 — 未关闭
    后续修复：在实体启用开关切换后，保持 FieldForm 草稿状态同步。

构建、CI 与仅 CLI 支持

  • PR #11269 — 已关闭
    阻止 metrics 和 embedded-web 隐式启用完整网关。关闭 Issue #11969。
  • PR #11973 — 已关闭
    在不带网关的构建中，恢复删除/重命名时的 agent 所属状态级联。关闭 Issue #11970。
  • PR #11974 — 已关闭
    仅在构建网关时运行依赖网关的测试。
  • PR #11988 — 已关闭
    在 SARIF 上传前丢弃被 nosemgrep 抑制的发现项。关闭 Issue #11987。
  • PR #11975 — 未关闭 和 PR #11976 — 未关闭
    增加仅 CLI 构建指南，并通过产物大小棘轮补充 CI 覆盖。

安全与渠道

  • PR #11968 — 已关闭
    按 RFC 6749 对 OIDC 注册的 Basic 凭据进行表单编码。关闭 Issue #11957。
  • PR #11979 — 已关闭
    仅在投递完成后记录渠道回复成功，防止被拒绝的发送产生虚假成功记录。

提供商、文档与依赖

  • PR #11404 — 已关闭
    稳定 macOS 测试中 fake Grok fixture 的时序。
  • PR #11980 和 PR #11963 — 已关闭
    关闭了支持 v0.9.0 组合工作的运行时架构文档提案。
  • PR #12018 — 已关闭
    依赖升级，包含 35 个 Rust crate 更新。
  • PR #12102 — 未关闭
    新的 Dependabot 升级，包含 34 项更新。

4. 社区热点

快照中未填充 PR 评论数，因此以下排名由 issue 评论数驱动。

条目 活跃度 潜在需求
Issue #5982 — 多租户部署的按发送方 RBAC 11 条评论 多租户隔离与最小权限访问。讨论已将范围收窄为在现有 agent/risk-profile 模型上构建发送方角色；#11068 中已有草稿。
Issue #10999 — 证明可从发布二进制安装 Discord 插件 9 条评论 可信的插件分发以及从已发布制品安装。已在 v0.8.6 上验证真实的 Discord 入站/出站投递，但该 issue 仍受阻。
Issue #6998 — 经 schema 校验的记忆整合 7 条评论 跨提供商记忆可靠性。当前提示内 JSON 解析在不同模型上很脆弱；用户需要有界回退和 schema 校验。
Issue #9647 — 知识图谱缺少按 agent 归属 5 条评论 单一共享知识图谱使任何 agent 都能读取或修改另一个 agent 的数据。这是一个 S0 安全/数据丢失问题。
Issue #11416 — Slack 的“is thinking…”状态自 v0.8.5 起缺失 5 条评论 Slack 线程中的渠道 UX 回归；用户希望在 agent 回合期间看到可见的进度指示。
Issue #11332 — 渠道、webhook、gateway 回合跳过技能审查/创建 4 条评论 学习循环在所有入口点保持一致，而不仅是 CLI/cron 运行。

分析： 社区最强烈推动的是 安全隔离与运营信任——多租户 RBAC、按 agent 的内存/知识所有权，以及插件安装完整性。第二个集群是 跨渠道与跨界面的 UX 一致性：Slack 进度指示、Web 聊天状态保留，以及 CLI 之外的技能学习行为。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重性/风险排序：

严重性 条目 状态 备注/修复 PR
S0 / P1 Issue #9647 — 知识图谱没有按 agent 归属；任何 agent 都能读取/修改另一个 agent 的知识 未关闭 高风险数据隔离缺陷。未显示修复 PR。
S1 Issue #11957 — OIDC 注册在 Basic 头中发送原始客户端凭据 已关闭 由 PR #11968 修复。
P1 Issue #9394 — gateway.pairing_dashboard 被接受但未读取；配对码永不过期 未关闭 v0.9.0 的安全加固。未显示修复 PR。
S2 / P2 Issue #11332 — 渠道/webhook/gateway 回合从不运行技能审查和创建 未关闭 CLI/cron 之外的学习循环退化。
S2 / P2 Issue #11562 — 插件发现可能在更新期间将某一代的 manifest 与另一代的组件配对 未关闭 在宽松/禁用签名模式下的插件完整性问题。
S2 / P2 Issue #11820 — 插件实例设置/出站的 config set 仅写入磁盘，永远不会到达运行中的守护进程 未关闭 运行时与配置不一致。
S2 / P2 Issue #11336 — plugin info / plugin list --verify 对运行时拒绝的插件报告 [loads] 未关闭 误导性的 CLI 诊断信息。
S2 Issue #11517 — 回合期间重新加载 Web 聊天会从屏幕和 localStorage 中丢弃提示词 已关闭 由 PR #11571 修复。
S2 Issue #11432 — 被杀死的守护进程使会话永远标记为 running 已关闭 由 PR #11523 修复。
P2 Issue #11416 — Slack 思考状态自 v0.8.5 起缺失 未关闭，进行中 渠道 UX 回归。
S3 / P3 Issue #11360 — 包锁文件可被其他本地账户读取 未关闭 可用性/安全加固。
S3 / P3 Issue #11358 — plugin migrate 在没有包锁的情况下移动包 未关闭 并发/插件完整性。
S3 Issue #11792 — 中断的插件安装会留下废弃的暂存目录 未关闭 清理/运维卫生。

稳定性解读： 当日关闭了若干有意义的回归问题，尤其是围绕会话状态和 Web 聊天的。然而，插件状态完整性和跨 agent 内存隔离仍是最大的未解决稳定性/安全主题。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

可能的 v0.9.0 范围

显式标记为 release:v0.9.0 且已经收到活跃 PR 的条目：

  • 运行时组合与基于能力的构造函数：Issue #10993、PR #11174。
  • 仅 CLI 构建与 feature-graph 正确性：PR #11975、PR #11976。
  • OIDC 与网关配对的安全修复：Issue #9394、PR #11968。
  • 无网关时的 agent 生命周期正确性：Issue #11970、PR #11973。

已接受但受阻或搁置

  • Issue #10997 — 在引导期间安装并激活所选插件。受阻。
  • Issue #10998 — 交付最小核心工具集和二进制大小证据。受阻。
  • Issue #10999 — 发布/证明可从发布二进制安装 Discord 插件。受阻。
  • Issue #6998 — 经 schema 校验的记忆整合。搁置。

较新的功能信号

  • Issue #11890 — 整合证据门禁：在写入 Core 前，将记忆更新标记为持久/瞬态并引用用户文本。
  • Issue #11561 — 在插件宿主内检查更新新增的插件权限。
  • Issue #11793 — 仅所有者可访问的数据目录，以及检测组/所有用户可写的根目录。
  • PR #12085 — 将 Obscurify.ai 添加为类型化的 OpenAI 兼容提供商。
  • Issue #5982 — 按发送方 RBAC，已接受但架构意义重大；除非进一步收窄，否则可能在 v0.9.0 之后。

预测： v0.9.0 将主要是一个 加固与架构版本——运行时组合、仅 CLI 正确性、插件/安全信任边界，以及网关功能分离——而不是一个广泛的功能版本。RBAC 和高级记忆整合更可能在组合与隔离基础稳定之后跟进。

7. 用户反馈总结

用户报告的主要痛点：

  • 多租户隔离不足。 #5982 和 #9647 都指向同一担忧：agent 可以以过多共享权限运行。用户希望按发送方设置角色，并按 agent 拥有内存/知识。
  • 插件安装和升级行为难以信任。 用户报告了误导性的 plugin info 输出（#11336）、manifest/组件代际不匹配（#11562）、锁文件权限问题（#11360），以及废弃的暂存目录（#11792）。
  • 跨提供商和模型的记忆整合很脆弱。 #6998 描述了原始 JSON 解析失败、Markdown 代码围栏、额外文本和无效字段。#11890 要求在将瞬态信息提升为长期记忆前提供更强证据。
  • 渠道行为不一致。 Slack 用户在 v0.8.5 之后失去了“is thinking…”指示器（#11416），而且技能学习循环不会为渠道/webhook/gateway 回合运行（#11332）。
  • CLI 与运行中的守护进程可能不一致。 #11820 报告 config set 更新了磁盘但未到达实时守护进程，这是一个重要的运维体验问题。
  • 配置用户体验正在改善。 通过 PR #11511 关闭 #11486，解决了 ZeroCode 保存/取消行为不一致的问题。

满意度信号： 项目响应及时——许多报告的问题在同一时期获得修复或接受状态更新。不满集中在 安全隔离、插件信任和界面一致性，而不是项目整体响应速度。

8. 待办积压观察

需要维护者关注的长期或重要事项：

条目 年龄/状态 为何重要
Issue #5982 — 按发送方 RBAC 创建于 2026-04-22；未关闭、已接受，11 条评论 多租户部署的基础。范围已收窄，但实现仍待完成。
Issue #6998 — 经 schema 校验的记忆整合 创建于 2026-05-29；搁置 跨提供商的记忆可靠性仍是用户反复关注的问题。
Issue #9394 — 配对仪表盘未读取；配对码永不过期 创建于 2026-07-26；P1，release:v0.9.0 安全敏感且带发布标签，但仍未关闭，且没有可见的修复 PR。
Issue #9647 — 知识图谱缺少按 agent 归属 创建于 2026-08-01；S0/P1 快照中最高严重性的未关闭 issue；直接影响数据隔离。
Issue #10162 — 插件安装在配置初始化前持久化包 创建于 2026-08-20；进行中 全新安装路径已部分处理；已安装后的重新初始化行为仍未解决。
Issue #10373 — 在 CLI 和网关之间共享 agent 重命名恢复 创建于 2026-08-26；P1 后续 持久状态迁移的跨界面一致性。
Issue #10993 / PR #11174 — 运行时组合边界 自 2026-09-20 / 2026-09-26；大型 PR 未关闭 关键的 v0.9.0 架构工作；XL PR 需要仔细审查。
Issue #10997 和 Issue #10998 — 插件引导和最小核心工具集 自 2026-09-20；受阻 两者都属于同一 v0.9.0 发布列车阶段，且仍受阻。
Issue #11416 — Slack 思考状态回归 自 2026-10-02；进行中 可见的渠道 UX 回归；似乎正在积极处理。

底线： 项目吞吐量健康，v0.9.0 加固正在明显推进，但开放积压仍包含 三个高影响安全/隔离事项——#9647、#9394 和 #5982——在项目将其宣传为可安全用于多租户或共享 agent 部署之前，应优先处理它们。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-29

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-29 14:08 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-29

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw saw very high triage throughput on 2026-10-29: 500 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with 224 PRs merged/closed against 276 still open, and 142 issues closed against 358 open/active. No new release was published, and the most recent stable validation reference is 2026.10.9 (Issue #187490), with extended-stable 2026.9.36 backports still active. Activity is concentrated in release engineering, CI/test stabilization, and a batch of Web UI resource-efficiency fixes, while the issue queue is dominated by gateway startup, crash-recovery, and session-state defects. The headline health concern is severity concentration: at least seven P0 issues appear in the top-50-by-comments sample alone, several tagged clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr, indicating a large stabilization backlog without identified fixes. Overall assessment: high-velocity maintenance and triage, but elevated stability debt and zero release output today.

2. Releases

No new releases were published in the last 24 hours, and the "Latest Releases" feed is empty.

Context from issue/PR metadata (not a release announcement):

  • Stable line appears to be 2026.10.9, referenced by release-validation flake tracking in #187490.
  • 2026.10.8 retrospective blockers are being addressed in #187249 (release-validation tooling).
  • Extended-stable 2026.9.36 is receiving targeted backports: #187252 (stateless reasoning replay guard) and #187701 (live-test waiver keying).

No breaking changes or migration notes to report today.

3. Project Progress

224 PRs were merged/closed in the last 24h. Notable items visible in the top-30 sample:

Fixes landed (closed PRs):

  • #187646 — native Codex helper processes are now settled on Stop, preventing orphaned child commands after session abort (fixes #187598).
  • #187687 — Web UI stops polling storage maintenance progress in hidden tabs; refreshes once on return.
  • #187701 — release validation waivers keyed correctly for the extended-stable line.

Notable in-flight work (open PRs):

  • MCP capability gap: #187699 makes tools.invoke / HTTP /tools/invoke work for configured MCP tools (currently returns not_found despite appearing in tools.effective). This closes a visible feature/implementation mismatch.
  • Web UI efficiency batch (vincentkoc): #187691 (release Markdown workers in hidden tabs), #187693 (pause Updates countdown), #187686 (pause Logbook polling).
  • Channel fixes: #147886 (Feishu documented markdown.tables mode, flagged merge-risk: compatibility), #187555 (Discord abort-signal propagation on cancellation), #187199 (Mattermost Unicode normalization), #187711 (Telegram forwarded rich-message debounce).
  • Platform correctness: #187703 preserves cache freshness across wall-clock changes; #187177 makes Claude migration fail loudly on malformed JSON instead of silently skipping settings.
  • Memory subsystem: #136482 (XL) proposes moving memory-index publication into a bounded worker to reduce SQLite contention and reindex leaks — open since 2026-09-02 and still needs proof.

Closed issues: #178000 (session-state races misclassified as model fallback), #136386 (cron exec allowlist denial), #187468 (package-swap update failure).

4. Community Hot Topics

Comment volume is the dominant engagement signal today; 👍 counts are near-zero across the board, suggesting discussion-heavy debugging rather than broad user voting.

Item Comments Why it matters
#160959 — P0: Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins 64 Highest-engagement issue in the sample. A 2026.9.6 regression from plugin generation capture (#144252) that blocks the event loop at startup and on runtime republish. Tagged no-new-fix-pr + needs-maintainer-review.
#164294 — P2: state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes 38 Checkpoint permanently blocked by an in-process reader (17,091 log frames, 866 checkpointed). Persistence-layer design issue with unusually high engagement for a P2.
#150635 — short-term recall eviction blocks dreaming promotion 21 Memory architecture defect: 512-entry cap + nightly zero-recall ingestion prevents deep-phase promotion.
#120385 — Code Mode catalog incomplete for cron/memory-flush turns 21 MCP tools missing ("Unknown tool id") surfaced only as a generic exec failure; author corrected the original scope on 2026-10-21.
#166634 — P0: checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable after crash recovery 18 SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired permanently blocks chat.history, models.list, etc.
#172837 — P1: Codex nativeSubagentAssignments never removed 17 Assignment entries re-pin and re-send on every new parent thread after delivery gives up.
#177656 — P1: host exec integrity-admission error 17 ≥28 failures on stable 2026.10.5; child effects unproven.
#44309 — one-way A2A dispatch mode 15 Oldest high-engagement feature ask (2026-03-12); still needs-product-decision.

Underlying needs: the top cluster is not about features — it is about runtime reliability under load, crash, and clock/sleep events. Users are operating gateways with large plugin trees, multi-GB SQLite state, and long-running sessions; the current failure modes are event-loop starvation, WAL/checkpoint contention, and unrecoverable post-crash states. A second cluster is memory/recall correctness (#150635, #157827, #148033), suggesting the dreaming/RAG pipeline needs design review rather than point fixes.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity, from the top-50 sample. "No fix PR" reflects the clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr tag.

P0 — Critical

  1. #160959 — Gateway event loop blocked for minutes by external/workspace plugin capture (2026.9.6 regression). No fix PR identified. Highest comment count in the dataset (64).
  2. #162211 — Startup blocks event loop 40–200s; health monitor misreads the stall as a disconnect and escalates into a restart loop (2026.9.7, macOS/launchd). Needs live repro.
  3. #166634 — Post-crash agent permanently UNAVAILABLE after reclamation checkpoint expiry. Not reproducible on main.
  4. #158592 — After host sleep/wake, model runtime publication times out and never recovers; all inbound messages fail until gateway restart.
  5. #160762 — Telegram + claude-cli: mid-turn message dropped entirely; drained prompt carries the previous message body (data/message loss). Needs info.
  6. #185819 — Windows quick-start Codex onboarding fails activation with inactive harness runtime artifact after successful device auth (2026.10.7).
  7. #141413 — macOS app omits auth token for local Gateway when gateway.auth.token is a protected SecretRef; tagged needs-security-review. 2 👍.

P1 — High

  • #166017 — mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs default not applied when unset; MCP runtimes never evicted; spawn broker hits 256-child cap and all exec/read/MCP starts fail. Linked fix PR open.
  • #126950 — Telegram opaque tgcb1: callback payloads silently dropped for non-plugin callers. Linked fix PR open.
  • #177656 — Native host exec returns shared-state integrity-admission error without child result; ≥28 failures on 2026.10.5. No fix PR.
  • #172837 — Codex subagent assignments leak and re-send indefinitely. No fix PR.
  • #181459 — 3.5 GB agent DB makes startup a gamble (18s open, 4–6 min startup, then commit checkpoint expired); embeddings stored 3×. Related to #166634.
  • #176342 — Stale-lease integrity gates serialize agent startup after unclean shutdown, causing minutes-long unavailability.
  • #148789 — Model fallback chain exhausts all candidates on harness-level session failure and misattributes to last fallback.
  • #155396 — Codex tool turns fail closed on provenance_rejected during final-answer recovery.
  • #167667 — ChatGPT Responses tool continuation fails with "Rustponses cannot replay."

P2 but notable

  • #164294 — WAL checkpoint never completes (38 comments; likely a root cause contributor to #166634/#181459).
  • #163566 — session-resource-loader burns 80–150s CPU per turn after update+repair (2026.9.7).
  • #187490 — Flaky tests observed during 2026.10.9 stable validation; policy requires parallel fixes on main.

Regression theme: versions 2026.9.6–2026.10.7 introduced several event-loop/latency regressions (#160959, #162211, #163566). This is the single biggest stability signal in the digest.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

User-requested features visible today:

  • #44309 — One-way dispatch mode for A2A handoffs without reply-back ping-pong. 15 comments, 7+ months old, awaiting product decision. Strong candidate for a sessions_send semantics extension.
  • #140244 — --prompt-file <path> for openclaw infer model run (avoids OS argv limits for large automation prompts).
  • #163739 — Make Control UI Ctrl+Shift+A (Archive) configurable; currently collides with browser shortcuts and cannot be remapped.
  • #154524 — Expose chat messages as headings for screen-reader navigation.
  • #141295 — TTL/manual clear for interrupted/cancelled pending inputs, which currently inject stale context into every turn after compaction.
  • #141973 — tools.exec.notifyOnExit should support a failure-only/user-requested-only mode and stop relaying SIGTERM-at-drain exits.
  • #150743 — QQ channel long-term support clarification after the Tencent handoff stalled (ecosystem/sustainability concern, not a bug).

Prediction: With #187699 already open, MCP tool invocation via tools.invoke is the most likely capability to land in the next patch/minor. The hidden-tab polling batch (#187686/#187687/#187691/#187693) appears staged for the next 2026.10.x. One-way A2A dispatch (#44309) and Control UI shortcut configurability (#163739) require product decisions and are unlikely in the immediate next version.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction drivers):

  • Startup and recovery reliability is the dominant complaint. Multiple users describe gateways that take minutes to start, enter restart loops, or leave agents permanently UNAVAILABLE after crash/sleep (#160959, #162211, #166634, #158592, #181459, #176342). This is production-blocking, not cosmetic.
  • Latent data loss: Telegram messages dropped mid-turn and replaced with the previous message body (#160762); message-loss labels also on #126950, #142037, #156070, #149985.
  • Cost/performance of long sessions: Anthropic cache stuck at ~46k tools+system prefix with ~377–386k cache_create per turn (#140129) — a direct cost complaint.
  • Resource leaks: MCP child processes fill the 256 cap (#166017); Codex subagent assignments accumulate (#172837); pending inputs never expire (#141295).
  • Configuration/onboarding friction: Windows Codex onboarding (#185819), silent drop of registerCliBackend without modelProvider (#172969), and migration silently succeeding on malformed JSON (#187177 / underlying issue).

Positive signals / satisfaction:

  • Users are engaging in high-quality, deeply instrumented reports (many rated 🦞 diamond lobster / 🐚 platinum hermit, with source-level repros and logs), which indicates a technically invested user base willing to help triage.
  • Several reporters explicitly verify fixes and correct their own earlier hypotheses (#120385, #143784), showing collaborative maintenance culture.
  • Web UI and accessibility polish requests (#163739, #154524, #147732, #177094) suggest users are moving beyond "does it work" toward daily-driver ergonomics — a maturity signal.

8. Backlog Watch

Important items with long dwell time or missing maintainer action:

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Agent & Assistant Open-Source Ecosystem

Data date: 2026-10-29 · Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The open-source personal AI agent landscape on 2026-10-29 is bifurcated between one hyper-scale reference implementation (OpenClaw, 500 issues + 500 PRs touched in 24h) and a cluster of mid-scale, release-train-driven projects (ZeroClaw, QwenPaw, Hermes) each stabilizing a specific architectural thesis. No project shipped a release in the window — every active project is in a hardening or beta-preview phase, which suggests the ecosystem is consolidating around reliability rather than feature velocity. Across all five projects, the dominant investment area has shifted from "what the agent can do" to session durability, multi-tenancy isolation, plugin supply-chain trust, and silent-failure elimination — the classic signals of a stack moving from demo-grade to production-grade. Notably, activity is extremely uneven: IronClaw is effectively idle while OpenClaw runs ~500× its volume, meaning "ecosystem health" must be read per-project rather than in aggregate.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs peers

  • Scale of community: 500 issues + 500 PRs touched in one day is roughly 10–500× the throughput of every peer. It has the deepest triage pipeline (labeled severities, clawsweeper automation, dedicated release-validation issues) — the only project here with a formalized release-validation and extended-stable backport process (#187490, #187252, #187701).
  • Breadth: MCP tool invocation, multi-channel (Telegram, Discord, Feishu, Mattermost), Codex/Claude migration, memory/dreaming/RAG subsystems — the widest surface in the set.
  • Reference status: It is the de facto "core reference," and peers' bug taxonomies echo its subsystems.

Technical approach differences

  • Gateway-centric architecture with a large event loop and in-process plugin capture — the source of both its capability breadth and its biggest P0s (#160959 event-loop blocking, #162211 40–200s startup stalls, #164294 WAL checkpoint starvation).
  • SQLite-backed session/state store at scale (3.5 GB DBs reported in #181459) — peers are earlier in this curve and have not yet hit the same persistence ceiling.

7. Trend Signals

Industry-level patterns extracted from community feedback, ranked by signal strength:

  1. Session portability is now an expected primitive, not a feature. Users run Desktop→remote serve→Telegram→Slack as one logical session (Hermes #139818/#41220; OpenClaw #158592; ZeroClaw cross-surface rename recovery #10373). Developer implication: design resume/identity as a first-class, surface-agnostic contract — not per-surface logic.

  2. Multi-tenancy and per-sender/per-agent isolation are table stakes. Highest-severity open items cluster here: ZeroClaw #9647 (S0), #5982 (RBAC); Hermes UnscopedSecretError family; OpenClaw SecretRef auth. Implication: secret scoping and ownership attribution must be enforced at the runtime boundary, not the config layer.

  3. Silent failure is the #1 trust destroyer. Every project has reports where the system "continues as if healthy" — dropped images, dropped cron deliveries, deleted config sections, misreported plugin loads. Implication: structured error/reason codes and explicit warnings are a competitive differentiator, not polish.

  4. Plugin supply-chain integrity is the new attack surface. Manifest/component generation mismatch (ZeroClaw #11562), loader crashes (QwenPaw #8473), install staging debris (ZeroClaw #11792), MCP tool/impl mismatch (OpenClaw #187699). Implication: signed manifests, generation pinning, and install transactions are becoming expected.

  5. Resource footprint and cost are first-class complaints. 690MB import side-effects (QwenPaw #8490), Anthropic cache prefix bloat (OpenClaw #140129), ACP token double-counting (Hermes #146475), separate cheap memory models (QwenPaw #7719). Implication: cost observability and lazy-import hygiene belong in the release checklist.

  6. Provider registries are hardening into governance questions. IronClaw explicitly curating providers.json (#8161, citing Novita closure); ZeroClaw/Hermes/QwenPaw all fielding provider PRs. Implication: the ecosystem is splitting into "curated core + external provider mechanism," which favors projects with a documented inclusion policy.

  7. Packaging/frozen-build QA is a release gate, not an afterthought. QwenPaw's beta shipped without required assets; OpenClaw and ZeroClaw both fielding CLI-only/onboarding build issues. Implication: CI must build and smoke-test the frozen artifact, not just source.

  8. Local-first / privacy-preserving inference is a credible demand vector. Local TTS (Hermes #145492), local Piccolo scoring (QwenPaw #8463), privacy-provider registry pressure (IronClaw), Obscurify integration (ZeroClaw #12085). Implication: privacy is emerging as a product category, not just a provider option.

Bottom line for decision-makers: OpenClaw is the ecosystem's engine and highest-risk component simultaneously; ZeroClaw and QwenPaw are the healthiest release-readiness stories; Hermes is a strong community bottlenecked on triage; IronClaw is dormant and policy-gated. The cross-cutting technical mandate for 2026-11 is clear — durable session identity, enforced isolation, loud failures, and trustworthy plugin supply chains.

  • Satisfaction/dissatisfaction: no explicit satisfaction data; no complaints about bugs or behavior. The mild friction is process-related, not product-related.

8. Backlog Watch

  • #8161 — open, 0 comments, ~1 day old with no maintainer response. Not yet "long-unanswered," but it is blocking a volunteer's contribution decision and is the only item in flight; a short policy answer has outsized leverage today.
  • #1115 (Novita provider PR, closed) — worth a maintainer-authored summary of the closure rationale. Its reasoning is already being cited by new contributors as de facto policy, which means the precedent is circulating without an authoritative, linkable statement.

Recommended maintainer action: respond to #8161 with either (a) acceptance criteria for providers.json entries, or (b) a pointer to the intended external-provider path — and consider converting that answer into documentation to stop the same question recurring.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-10-29

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw is in an intensive 2.3.0-beta stabilization cycle: 38 PRs were touched in the last 24 hours (26 open, 12 merged/closed) against 13 issue updates (7 open, 6 closed), with no new release published. Throughput is high, but the open-issue set is dominated by beta packaging and runtime regressions — most notably #8473 (all 12 backend plugins fail to load on 2.3.0-beta.1) and #8488 (desktop build ships without visual-compression assets). The maintainers closed two long-running bugs/enhancements today (#8464, #8150) and merged the matching conversation-model fix (#8465), showing responsive triage on high-signal reports. Overall health is active but release-blocked: the 2.3.0 beta still has at least two high-severity, unfixed defects, while architectural work (plugin-based local model management, Piccolo scoring, separate memory-write models) continues in parallel.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours, and no release history was provided. (Section omitted per data availability.)

3. Project Progress

Merged / Closed PRs today (6 visible in the top-20 sample; 12 total)

PR Scope Impact
#8465 fix(models) XL Honors conversation-level model settings across all runtime paths, including slash-command dispatch Fixes #8464 — /compact now uses the session model (M2) instead of the persisted agent default (M1)
#8358 fix(providers) M Aligns Console "thinking" defaults with actual OpenAI-compatible wire parameters (thinking_enabled, effort levels) Removes a silent config/behavior mismatch for custom Chat Completions models
#8492 fix(security) M Prevents false-positive approvals for Code Mode in JEV mode Security guard correctness — fewer spurious approval prompts without weakening review
#8253 feat(website) XXXL Bilingual JSON-driven evaluation leaderboard at /evaluation/ with SVG cost/performance chart and Pareto frontier Community-facing benchmark transparency
#8494 feat(airport-sms) S Scaffolds packages/airport_sms with CI Enables a new vertical SMS-agent package boundary
#8495 feat(airport-sms) XXXL Full SMS Agent stack (PR01–PR15: smoke, governance, console, WeCom) Large domain-specific feature landing

Closed Issues today

  • #8464 (bug, 4 comments) — /compact ignored session model switch; resolved by #8465.
  • #8150 (bug, 3 comments) — Feishu inbound rich-text images silently dropped.
  • #4356 (enhancement) — finer-grained file guard / read-only paths.
  • #4129 (enhancement) — /rewind-style rollback for files and context.
  • #7740 (enhancement) — Hub-mode admin password reset.
  • #8459 (enhancement) — easier access to unread push messages in Console.

Takeaway: the day's merged work clusters around configuration correctness (model resolution, thinking parameters) and security review accuracy, plus one major docs/site feature. Two multi-month enhancement requests (#4356 from May, #4129 from May) finally closed, suggesting backlog grooming is happening alongside beta work.

4. Community Hot Topics

  1. #8464 — 4 comments (most active issue) · CLOSED Manual /compact ignored the session-level model override and always used agent.json's active_model; with a strict provider (400 on unsupported params), compaction failed regardless of which model the user selected. The underlying need is one consistent model-resolution path for normal turns, slash commands, and background jobs — a class of bug that recurs whenever a new entry point bypasses AgentBuilder. Fixed same-day by #8465.

  2. #8150 — 3 comments · CLOSED Feishu inbound post messages with embedded images delivered text but silently dropped the images — no download, no warning. The need here is channel parity and observable failure: users expect multimodal inbound content to match outbound capabilities (see the referenced #2792 for the outbound direction). Silent truncation is worse than an explicit error because agents answer with incomplete context.

  3. #8488 — 2 comments · OPEN Windows PyInstaller desktop build of 2.3.0-beta.1 omits visual_compression/assets, so every eligible model call raises FileNotFoundError: atlas-gray-native.ts and Visual Compact silently no-ops. Signals a packaging-manifest gap between source and frozen builds.

  4. #8473 — 2 comments · OPEN All 12 backend plugins fail at startup due to unguarded importlib.invalidate_caches() in module_isolation.py:220. The reporter explicitly notes it is the same root cause as #8265 at a new call site — a regression pattern rather than a one-off.

Note: PR comment counts were reported as undefined in the dataset, so PR hotness is inferred from review labels (Under Review) and size rather than engagement.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity, based on user impact and blast radius:

Severity Issue Status Fix PR?
Critical #8473 — 2.3.0-beta.1: all backend plugins fail to load (12/12) at server startup; TypeError from unguarded importlib.invalidate_caches() in module_isolation.py:220. Same root cause as #8265 at a new call site. OPEN Likely #8497 (tolerate cache-refresh failures) and #8345 (don't abort plugin install) — both open, overlapping
High #8488 — Desktop/PyInstaller build omits visual_compression atlases → FileNotFoundError on every eligible model call; Visual Compact silently no-ops. OPEN None visible in provided data
High #8490 — GET /api/workspace/local-whisper-status does a real import whisper, pulling torch + CUDA into the server process (~690 MB RSS, never released) merely to render a settings page. OPEN ✅ #8491 (first-time contributor, avoids the import in the probe)
Medium #8464 — /compact used the wrong model, causing hard 400 failures with strict providers. CLOSED ✅ #8465 merged/closed
Medium #8150 — Feishu inbound images silently dropped (data loss with no warning). CLOSED Not visible in sample
Low #8486 — Console tool-call <> icon clipped on the left edge (missing container padding); visible at higher zoom. OPEN None

Pattern worth flagging: three of the five open/high bugs (#8473, #8488, #8490) are specific to the 2.3.0-beta.1 install paths (frozen desktop build, plugin loader, optional-dependency probing). This points to a QA gap in packaging and lazy-import hygiene rather than core agent logic. Also relevant: #8496 (open) addresses max_tokens vs max_completion_tokens collisions causing HTTP 400 on scroll-summary requests — another provider-compatibility stability fix in flight.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Open requests:

  • #8478 — Sync bundled DOCX/PPTX/XLSX skills with Anthropic's July 2026 Office skills update while keeping QwenPaw adaptations. Signals that skill freshness is now a competitive expectation.
  • #8481 — QWENPAW_LANGUAGE-style env var to set the default language during initial Docker setup. Small, deployment-oriented, high leverage for international/enterprise rollouts.
  • #8498 — "install easily" question (template-only body); low signal, likely docs/onboarding gap.
  • Closed today: #4356 (granular file-guard read-only paths), #4129 (/rewind backup/rollback), #7740 (Hub admin password reset), #8459 (unread push-message access). Their closure implies these are either implemented or consciously deferred.

Roadmap signals from open PRs:

  • #8499 (WIP, XXXL) — extract local model management into a Plugin Provider (downloads, llama.cpp install, service lifecycle). Architectural direction: a thinner host with pluggable providers, preserving existing configs/model files.
  • #8463 (XL) — run local Piccolo models with bidirectional candidate scoring for JEV tool review and ReMe compaction. Local, privacy-preserving replacements for hosted review models.
  • #7719 (XL, Under Review) — separate, cheaper model for ReMeLight memory writing (auto_memory / auto_dream / daily_paper / auto_fin). Direct cost-control request from heavy users.
  • #8485 — "Install app" button for Extension apps in Console.

Prediction for the next version (2.3.0 final): plugin-loader hardening (#8497/#8345), desktop asset bundling (#8488), lazy whisper probing (#8491), conversation-scoped model settings (#8465), provider token-limit compatibility (#8496). Larger items (#8499 local-model plugin extraction, #8463 Piccolo, #7719 memory model) look like 2.3.x/2.4 material given their XXXL/XL size and open review state.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points observed:

  • Silent failures erode trust. #8150 (images dropped with no warning), #8488 (Visual Compact no-ops), and #8464 (compaction fails with opaque 400s) all share a theme: the system continues as if healthy while degrading output. Users are explicitly asking for warnings/logging, not just fixes.
  • Resource footprint matters. #8490's 690 MB permanent RSS increase from merely opening a settings page is a serious complaint for self-hosted/desktop users; the fix being a first-time contributor's PR suggests the community is motivated to help.
  • Beta packaging quality. Two independent reporters on 2.3.0-beta.1 hit install/build-level breakage (plugin loader, PyInstaller assets), which colors perception of the beta more than core logic bugs would.
  • Configuration consistency. #8464 and #8358 both concern what the UI shows vs what the runtime does — a recurring satisfaction risk in a multi-provider, multi-model product.
  • Deployment/ops basics. #7740 (admin password reset in Hub mode) and #8481 (default language env var) come from operators running QwenPaw for teams, not single users — the product is being used in managed deployments and lacks corresponding admin affordances.
  • Power-user workflow gaps. #4129 (/rewind) and #4356 (read-only guarded paths) show users pushing agent autonomy further and needing reversibility and least-privilege controls to feel safe.

Satisfaction signals: rapid same-day turnaround on #8464 (issue → fix PR → close), responsive triage on #8150 after a 20-day open period, and multiple first-time contributors (#8491, #8345, #8400, #8494) indicate a healthy, approachable contribution pipeline.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention, ordered by staleness × importance:

Item Age Why it matters
#7719 feat(memory) XL, Under Review ~47 days (since 2026-09-12) Cost-control feature with clear demand; long review latency risks contributor drop-off
#7835 fix(memory) M, Under Review ~42 days (since 2026-09-17) Stops auto-memory-recall payload leaking into channel output; overlaps conceptually with #8457 — two competing approaches to the same defect, needs a decision
#8308 test(api) XS ~11 days Trivial test-alignment PR stuck open; cheap win for CI reliability
#8309 fix(cli) M, Under Review ~11 days Ollama model discovery before activation — onboarding blocker for local-model users
#8345 fix(plugins) S, first-time ~9 days Overlaps #8497; consolidate to avoid duplicate/conflicting fixes for #8473
#8400 fix(skill) XS, first-time ~6 days The built-in make-skill is blocked by QwenPaw's own security scanner — a self-inflicted false positive that undermines trust in the scanner
#8463 feat(models) XL ~1 day Not stale yet, but large and strategically important (local Piccolo inference); watch for review capacity
#8473 plugin load failure 1 day Same root cause as #8265 at a new call site — needs a systemic fix (guard all invalidate_caches() call sites), not a per-site patch

Recommendation for maintainers: (1) designate one canonical fix for the invalidate_caches class of failures and close the duplicate; (2) resolve the #7835 vs #8457 memory-injection design split; (3) bundle #8488 and #8491 into the 2.3.0 release checklist so the beta does not ship with a silently disabled compression feature and a 690 MB import side effect.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-29

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw remained highly active on 2026-10-29: 50 issues and 50 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, including 14 PRs merged/closed and 9 issues closed, with no new release. The day’s closed work concentrated on v0.9.0 hardening: runtime session recovery, web chat state retention, OIDC credential handling, feature-graph cleanup, CLI-only builds, and plugin/CLI correctness. The active queue is dominated by high-risk security and architecture work around multi-tenancy, plugin trust boundaries, and memory isolation. Overall project health is strong on throughput and release readiness, but several long-running P1/S0 security issues remain open and need sustained maintainer attention.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. The latest referenced published build in issue discussion is v0.8.6, while multiple PRs and issues are tagged release:v0.9.0, indicating active preparation for the next release.

3. Project Progress

Runtime and session reliability

Web dashboard and ZeroCode UX

Providers, docs, and dependencies

    Dependency bump with 35 Rust crate updates.

    New Dependabot bump with 34 updates.

4. Community Hot Topics

PR comment counts were not populated in the snapshot, so ranking below is driven by issue comment counts.

Item Activity Underlying need
Issue #5982 — Per-sender RBAC for multi-tenant deployments 11 comments Multi-tenant isolation and least-privilege access. Discussion has narrowed scope to building sender roles on the existing agent/risk-profile model; a draft exists in #11068.
Issue #10999 — Prove Discord plugin installation from a release binary 9 comments Trustworthy plugin distribution and installation from published artifacts. Real Discord inbound/outbound delivery was verified on v0.8.6, but the issue remains blocked.

Analysis: The community is pushing hardest on security isolation and operational trust — multi-tenant RBAC, per-agent memory/knowledge ownership, and plugin installation integrity. A second cluster is UX consistency across channels and surfaces: Slack progress indicators, web chat state preservation, and skill-learning behavior outside the CLI.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity/risk:

Severity Item Status Notes / fix PR
S0 / P1 Issue #9647 — Knowledge graph has no per-agent attribution; any agent can read/mutate another’s knowledge OPEN High-risk data isolation bug. No fix PR shown.
S1 Issue #11957 — OIDC enrollment sends raw client credentials in Basic header CLOSED Fixed by PR #11968.
P1 Issue #9394 — gateway.pairing_dashboard accepted but unread; pairing codes never expire OPEN Security hardening for v0.9.0. No fix PR shown.

S2 Issue #11517 — Web chat reload during a turn drops prompt from screen and localStorage CLOSED Fixed by PR #11571.
S2 Issue #11432 — Killed daemon leaves session marked running forever CLOSED Fixed by PR #11523.
P2 Issue #11416 — Slack thinking status missing since v0.8.5 OPEN, in progress Channel UX regression.

S3 / P3 Issue #11358 — plugin migrate moves packages without package lock OPEN Concurrency/plugin integrity.
S3 Issue #11792 — Interrupted plugin install leaves abandoned staging directory OPEN Cleanup/operator hygiene.

Stability read: The day closed several meaningful regressions, especially around session state and web chat. However, plugin state integrity and cross-agent memory isolation remain the largest unresolved stability/security themes.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Likely v0.9.0 scope

Items explicitly tagged release:v0.9.0 and already receiving active PRs:

  • Runtime composition and capability-based constructors: Issue #10993, PR #11174.
  • CLI-only build and feature-graph correctness: PR #11975, PR #11976.
  • Security fixes for OIDC and gateway pairing: Issue #9394, PR #11968.
  • Agent lifecycle correctness without gateway: Issue #11970, PR #11973.

Accepted but blocked or parked

  • Issue #10997 — Install and activate selected plugins during onboarding. Blocked.
  • Issue #10998 — Deliver minimal core tool set and binary-size evidence. Blocked.
  • Issue #10999 — Publish/prove Discord plugin installation from release binary. Blocked.
  • Issue #6998 — Schema-validated memory consolidation. Parking lot.

Newer feature signals

  • Issue #11890 — Consolidation evidence gate: label memory updates durable/transient and quote user text before writing to Core.
  • Issue #11561 — Check an update’s added plugin authority inside the plugin host.
  • Issue #11793 — Owner-only data directory and detection of group/world-writable roots.
  • PR #12085 — Add Obscurify.ai as a typed OpenAI-compatible provider.
  • Issue #5982 — Per-sender RBAC, accepted but architecturally significant; likely post-v0.9.0 unless narrowed further.

Prediction: v0.9.0 will primarily be a hardening and architecture release — runtime composition, CLI-only correctness, plugin/security trust boundaries, and gateway feature separation — rather than a broad feature release. RBAC and advanced memory consolidation are more likely to follow after the composition and isolation foundations settle.

7. User Feedback Summary

Main pain points reported by users:

  • Multi-tenant isolation is insufficient. Both #5982 and #9647 point to the same concern: agents can operate with too much shared authority. Users want per-sender roles and per-agent ownership of memory/knowledge.
  • Plugin installation and upgrade behavior is hard to trust. Users report misleading plugin info output (#11336), manifest/component generation mismatches (#11562), lock-file permission issues (#11360), and abandoned staging directories (#11792).
  • Memory consolidation is fragile across providers and models. #6998 describes raw JSON parsing failures, Markdown fences, extra prose, and invalid fields. #11890 asks for stronger evidence before promoting transient information into long-term memory.
  • Channel behavior is inconsistent. Slack users lost the “is thinking…” indicator after v0.8.5 (#11416), and skill-learning loops do not run for channel/webhook/gateway turns (#11332).
  • CLI and running daemon can diverge. #11820 reports that config set updates disk but does not reach a live daemon, which is a significant operator-experience problem.
  • Configuration UX is improving. The closure of #11486 via PR #11511 addresses inconsistent ZeroCode save/cancel behavior.

Satisfaction signal: The project is responsive — many reported issues received fixes or accepted-status updates within the same period. Dissatisfaction is concentrated in security isolation, plugin trust, and surface parity, not in general project responsiveness.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-running or important items that need maintainer attention:

Item Age / Status Why it matters
Issue #5982 — Per-sender RBAC Created 2026-04-22; open, accepted, 11 comments Foundational for multi-tenant deployments. Scope has narrowed, but implementation is still pending.
Issue #6998 — Schema-validated memory consolidation Created 2026-05-29; parking lot Memory reliability across providers remains a recurring user concern.
Issue #9394 — Pairing dashboard unread; pairing codes never expire Created 2026-07-26; P1, release:v0.9.0 Security-sensitive and release-tagged, but still open with no visible fix PR.
Issue #9647 — Knowledge graph lacks per-agent attribution Created 2026-08-01; S0/P1 Highest-severity open issue in the snapshot; directly affects data isolation.
Issue #10162 — Plugin install persists package before config seeding Created 2026-08-20; in progress Fresh-install path partially handled; already-installed reseed behavior still unresolved.
Issue #10373 — Share agent-rename recovery across CLI and gateway Created 2026-08-26; P1 follow-up Cross-surface consistency for durable state migrations.
Issue #10993 / PR #11174 — Runtime composition boundary Since 2026-09-20 / 2026-09-26; large PR open Key v0.9.0 architecture work; XL PR needs careful review.
Issue #10997 and Issue #10998 — Plugin onboarding and minimal core tool set Since 2026-09-20; blocked Both are part of the same v0.9.0 release-train phase and remain blocked.
Issue #11416 — Slack thinking status regression Since 2026-10-02; in progress Visible channel UX regression; appears actively worked.

Bottom line: Project throughput is healthy and v0.9.0 hardening is visibly progressing, but the open backlog still contains three high-impact security/isolation items — #9647, #9394, and #5982 — that should be prioritized before the project markets itself as safe for multi-tenant or shared-agent deployments.
